# APS Classroom Dashboard --- Architecture & Config Reference

> **Source snapshot saved in this project**: the full current `Code.gs`
> and `Dashboard.html` are saved alongside this doc as `claude/Code.gs`
> and `claude/Dashboard.html` (as of the fifth round, Sept 2026 --- the
> Student Onboarding Status redesign). A future session can read those
> two docs directly to see the exact current code without needing to
> reconnect to the user's computer. **Keep them in sync**: whenever
> `Code.gs` or `Dashboard.html` changes again, re-save the updated file
> to the same path (`project_write` replaces in place) alongside
> updating this architecture doc, so the snapshot never drifts from
> what's actually deployed.


## Realtime operational status update (Sept 14, 2026)

### Problem fixed

The live dashboard previously refreshed the full dashboard only every 5 minutes. Although the
Teacher NOT in Class / Needs Tech Support action wrote its state immediately, other already-open
dashboards could therefore remain stale until their next full refresh or a manual Refresh.

### Implementation

- Added `getRealtimeStatusSnapshot()` in `Code.gs`. It reads only the two Script Property status
  maps (`teacherNotInClassMap` and `needsTechSupportMap`) and does not call Classroom, roster,
  presence, or the expensive `getDashboardData()` pipeline.
- `Dashboard.html` polls this lightweight endpoint every 2 seconds while the page is visible.
- When a status changes, only the affected card's status badge/action area is updated in the DOM.
  The entire `#grid` is NOT rebuilt.
- Search text, focus, scroll position, weekly controls, and the rest of the card remain untouched.
- The reporting user's own successful click no longer calls the full `load()` function; it updates
  that card immediately from the server response.
- Monitoring summary counts and the active Teacher NOT in Class / Needs Tech Support filters are
  updated without a full render.
- The existing 5-minute quiet dashboard refresh remains as the general fallback for all other
  dashboard data.

### User-visible result

A student can click **Teacher NOT in Class**, and Admin/Headmaster dashboards that are already open
will normally show the updated status within about **0–2 seconds**, without page refresh and without
visible UI flickering. This is polling-based near-real-time behavior; Google Apps Script Web Apps do
not provide a persistent browser push channel in this implementation.

## Current merged production release (Sept 14, 2026)

The authoritative merged production files for this release are:

- `CODE_MERGE_FINAL.gs` — merged Google Apps Script server code.
- `CODE_MERGE_FINAL.html` — merged APS Dashboard Web App UI.
- `APS_Dashboard_Feature_Updates.md` — this architecture/configuration reference.

### Merged changes included

1. **Secure Google identity verification**
   - Server authentication continues to use `Session.getActiveUser().getEmail()`.
   - `Session.getEffectiveUser()` is not used as an authentication fallback.
   - `ScriptApp.requireScopes()` is not called during the Web App login flow, avoiding the misleading authorization error that can occur through `google.script.run`.
   - Returning browser sessions are revalidated against the live Google identity.
   - The entered APS email is compared server-side with the authenticated Google account.
   - Existing APS role/authorization checks remain authoritative.

2. **Simplified Class/Grade Change email notifications**
   - Removed the duplicated legacy request-detail block.
   - The email presents only the relevant request information: Request ID, type, student/APS ID, student APS email, current class, requested class, status, reason/comments, approver, and final approver.
   - EST schedule labeling remains.
   - Existing APS Dashboard button, school logo, automatic-email notice, and signature remain.
   - Parent email is not repeated in the main notification.

3. **Student-only EST schedule notice**
   - The EST schedule banner is displayed only for users whose server-authenticated role is `student`.
   - Admin, headmaster, teacher, and other roles do not see the banner.

4. **Quiet dashboard background refresh**
   - Replaced the disruptive 1-minute full `load()` polling with a 5-minute quiet refresh.
   - No browser `location.reload()` is used.
   - No loading screen is shown during background refresh.
   - Classes view is re-rendered only when course data actually changes, with search/input and scroll state preserved.
   - Specialized working views are not forcibly rebuilt during the background refresh.
   - Manual Refresh continues to perform the existing explicit refresh behavior.
   - Chat polling remains independent and unchanged.

5. **Existing APS functionality retained**
   - Class/Grade Change workflow and validation.
   - Grade dropdown ordering with `MUNMAZHALAI` first.
   - Optional parent email.
   - Admin-only Assign Classroom workflow, capacity warning, audit history, remapping, rollback, and notifications.
   - Student-only school calendar.
   - Student login notices through Nov. 15, 2026.
   - Live status, teacher-not-in-class, tech-support, feedback, chat, sync, onboarding, and knowledge-base functionality.

### Deployment requirement

For the Web App authentication model used by this release, deploy the Web App with **Execute as: User accessing the web app** and require users to sign in. Do not use anonymous access for the APS Dashboard. The server-side APS authorization list/role logic remains the final access control.

The repository manifest is `current_appsscript.json`. It pins the Apps Script runtime to V8, uses the `America/New_York` timezone, configures the Web App as `USER_ACCESSING` with domain-only access, and declares the Classroom, Admin Directory, Admin Reports, Sheets, Docs, and AdSense Advanced Services used or retained by the project. After importing or syncing the project, confirm that each listed Advanced Service is also enabled in the linked Google Cloud project.

## Data flow

### Role and availability additions

- The dashboard environment is controlled by the Script Property `APS_ENV`. `PROD` (or an unset/unknown value, for safe production defaulting) is displayed as `LIVE`; `TEST` is displayed as `DEMO`. The server resolves this once per dashboard payload and the client displays the environment badge without adding another server round trip. Set `APS_ENV=TEST` in the test deployment and change it to `PROD` only for the production deployment.
- Protected role lists are explicit: `info@avvaiyarpadasalai.org` is `superadmin`; `info1@avvaiyarpadasalai.org`, `info3@avvaiyarpadasalai.org`, `principal@avvaiyarpadasalai.org`, and `simplysuga_aps501@avvaiyarpadasalai.org` are Admins; `vsugadev@amchats.org` and `valvil.ori@amchats.org` are `VCFO_AMCHSTS_BOD` read-only viewers. Email matching is normalized, so accidental surrounding whitespace does not change the assigned role.
- Classroom roster membership is evaluated from the synchronized course data. Teacher membership gives teacher access to that class; student membership gives student access to that class. If an account is present in both rosters, its dashboard view contains the union of both assigned class sets rather than hiding one category.
- A signed-in user from an approved APS domain is allowed to enter the dashboard even when no synchronized class contains that account. Such a user receives the `AUTHORIZED` role label and an in-screen message explaining that Google Classroom will appear after a teacher or student assignment and the next data synchronization.
- `Dashboard_User_Roles` is created in the dashboard workbook on first use. Admins manage active role overrides from the **User Roles & Permissions** tab. The `vcfo_amchsts_bod` role receives the same all-classroom visibility and filters as Admin/HM, but server-side mutation guards keep it read-only; chat remains enabled.
- The Admin-only **User Roles & Permissions** tab also provides role-wide toggle switches for **Read-only**, **Action buttons**, **Filters**, and **UI tabs**. Settings are stored in Script Properties under `dashboardRolePermissions_v1` and cached for 60 seconds. Admin and Super Admin permissions are protected. `VCFO_AMCHSTS_BOD` remains read-only regardless of its button toggle. Teachers default to buttons, filters, and tabs enabled, and an Admin can make all Teacher actions read-only with one toggle.
- The existing `Teacher_Weekly_Availability` sheet is reused. Its `confirmed`, `not_available`, and `pending` values are exposed on each course as `Available to Take Classes`, `Not Available to Take Classes`, and `Not Set`, respectively. The Teacher Availability filter is hidden for Students and available to recognized non-student roles.
- Availability action buttons reflect the saved weekly status: `Confirm - I'm Available` is hidden after a teacher saves `confirmed`, and `Not Available` is hidden after a teacher saves `not_available`. When the status is pending/not set, both actions remain visible. The reset action remains available to the existing Admin, Headmaster, and Teacher roles.
- Manual Class Status actions (`Cancel Class`, `Reschedule Class`, and `Restore Automatic Status`) are now Admin/Headmaster-only. Teacher and Student users do not see these controls, and the server rejects direct calls from them until this workflow is implemented in a later project stage.
- User-role lookups use a short-lived Apps Script cache and are invalidated immediately after Admin changes, avoiding a Spreadsheet read during every dashboard poll while keeping role updates responsive.
- Normal role resolution only reads `Dashboard_User_Roles` when the optional tab already exists; it never attempts to create that tab for teachers or students. The tab is created only when an Admin opens or saves the Admin role-control feature, preventing authorization failures for read-only spreadsheet users.
- Warning and error feedback remains in-screen. Native browser `alert`, `confirm`, and `prompt` dialogs are not used; destructive confirmations use the dashboard's existing modal styling.
- If authorization fails after a session has been remembered, the error screen offers `Review Access Again`, restores the remembered APS email, and routes the user through the normal server verification and `Review Dashboard Permissions` screen. This lets the user review access again without manually clearing browser state or retyping the email.

1.  **Classroom → Sheet**: `syncClassroomData()` in `Code.gs` calls the
    Google Classroom API (with retry/backoff), filters to only courses
    whose name ends with the configured suffix, and writes the results
    to the "Courses" tab of the target spreadsheet.
2.  **Sheet → Dashboard**: `getDashboardData()` reads only from that
    Sheet --- it never calls the Classroom API directly, so opening the
    dashboard can't trigger quota errors. It also applies role-based
    filtering before returning data --- see "Role-based access" below;
    its return shape is `{ email, role, name, courses }` (see "Signed-in
    badge" below for `name`).
3.  Both legs run on a cadence:
    -   The Classroom→Sheet sync runs on a time trigger created by
        `createSyncTrigger()`, at `SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (default 15;
        see "Key configuration").
    -   The open dashboard uses a **quiet 5-minute background refresh**
        (`DASHBOARD_POLL_MS` in `Dashboard.html`) via `setInterval`.
        The background refresh re-reads the Sheet without showing the
        loading screen or performing a browser/page reload. It preserves
        the active search/input and scroll position when a normal Classes
        view actually needs to re-render. Specialized Class/Grade Change,
        Assign Classroom, and other working views are not forcibly rebuilt
        while the user is working in them. This only re-reads the Sheet
        (no Classroom API call), so the background refresh does not itself
        consume Classroom/Reports API quota. The refresh also touches the
        session activity and keeps the dashboard data current.
    -   The chat panel polls separately and much more often --- every 8
        seconds (`CHAT_POLL_MS`) --- see "Shared dashboard chat" below.
    -   A manual "Force Sync Now" button on the dashboard can trigger an
        immediate Classroom→Sheet sync without waiting for the timer;
        "Refresh" re-reads the Sheet immediately.
    -   **Practical effect on "as soon as" claims**: any auto-detected
        status (Meet-based, Classroom-activity-based) only updates when
        a Classroom sync runs --- so at most a
        `SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES`-minute lag, or instantly via "Force Sync
        Now". The "Teacher NOT in Class" / "Needs Tech Support" status
        flows are different --- they patch the Sheet the instant someone
        clicks a button (see below), independent of the sync cadence,
        and additionally trigger an email on the first step (see "Staff
        notifications"). The dashboard-open heartbeat (part of "Live
        online presence") is also instant, independent of the sync
        cadence.
4.  **Workbook**: `getWorkbook_()` in `Code.gs` resolves the underlying
    Spreadsheet once (either `TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID`, or an auto-created
    one remembered via `CACHE_SHEET_ID_KEY`), and every tab-specific
    helper (`getOrCreateCacheSheet_()` for "Courses",
    `getOrCreateChatSheet_()` for "Dashboard_Chat_Window",
    `getOrCreateWhatsAppLinksSheet_()` for "WhatsApp_Group_Links") calls
    it --- so all of these tabs always live in the same spreadsheet, and
    adding another tab later just means adding another thin
    `getOrCreateXSheet_()` wrapper around `getWorkbook_()`.

## Role-based access

`getDashboardData()` determines who's viewing and filters the course
list before sending it to the browser, via `getViewerRole_()` /
`getViewerContext_()` in `Code.gs`:

-   **Admin** (`ADMIN_EMAILS`) and **Headmaster** (`HEADMASTER_EMAILS`)
    --- two hardcoded email lists near the top of `Code.gs`, just below
    `COURSE_ID_LOG_PARAM`. Both always see **every** synced classroom;
    the two roles behave identically today and only exist as separate
    lists/labels in case they ever need to diverge. Both are also
    treated as the "tech support team" / "staff" for the status-flow
    permission rules below.
    -   Admin: `info@`, `info1@`, `info3@`, `saranv_aps546@`,
        `simplysuga_aps501@` (all `@avvaiyarpadasalai.org`), plus
        `valvil.ori@amchats.org`.
    -   Headmaster: `logeswari_aps615@`, `premananth2002_aps759@`,
        `rajathigobi_aps551@`, `sakthivel_aps921@`,
        `sathiya.phy_aps568@`, `shyam.duraishyam_aps523@` (all
        `@avvaiyarpadasalai.org`).
-   **Teacher** --- anyone not in the two lists above is checked against
    every synced course's teacher roster (matched by email,
    case-insensitive --- the same `email` field already captured on each
    teacher object in `buildCourseRecord_`, which exists but was never
    rendered in the UI). If their email matches one or more courses'
    teachers, they see only those courses.
-   **Student** --- same idea against each course's student roster. If
    their email matches one or more courses' students, they see only
    those courses.
-   **None** --- an email that isn't an admin/headmaster and isn't found
    as a teacher or student in any synced course sees an empty course
    list (and no chat access --- see below). `Dashboard.html` shows a
    dedicated message for this case instead of the generic "No classes
    match."
-   Teacher/student membership is **dynamic** --- it's whatever the last
    Classroom sync wrote into the Sheet, so no separate roster needs to
    be maintained by hand; only the admin and headmaster lists are
    hardcoded.
-   **This exactly matches the school's stated policy** (confirmed Sept
    2026, no code change needed): only the emails in `ADMIN_EMAILS` /
    `HEADMASTER_EMAILS` are ever considered for those two roles; every
    other signed-in account is assigned Teacher or Student purely from
    their live Google Classroom enrollment (teacher roster vs. student
    roster), never hardcoded.

**Deployment requirement**: this relies on
`Session.getActiveUser().getEmail()`, which only returns a real address
when (a) the person opening the page is signed into a Google account in
the same Workspace domain as the script, and (b) the web app is deployed
with access set to "Anyone within \[the organization\]" (Deploy → Manage
deployments → Edit → Who has access) rather than public "Anyone". If
deployed as public "Anyone", the email comes back blank and every viewer
falls into the "none" role.

**Signed-in badge (top-right corner)**: `Dashboard.html` shows a pill
near the top-right of the header (`#viewerBadge`, CSS `.viewer-badge`)
reading "`<Google Profile Name>` (`<ROLE>`)" --- e.g. "Sugadev
Velayutham (ADMIN)", "Logeswari (HEADMASTER)", "Anandi (TEACHER)", "Ram
(STUDENT)" --- driven by the `{ email, role, name, courses }` object
`getDashboardData()` returns (`renderViewerInfo()` in `Dashboard.html`
builds the exact "Name (ROLE)" text). `name` is computed server-side via
`resolveViewerBadgeName_()` in `Code.gs` --- **not** the same function
`chatDisplayName_()` used in chat/status captions (that one is
deliberately unchanged, see "Shared dashboard chat"): -
**Teacher/student**: their real Classroom display name
(`findDisplayName_()`, looked up across every synced course's rosters),
same as before. - **Admin/headmaster**: their real Google account name,
via `getGoogleProfileName_()` --- an Admin SDK **Directory API** lookup
(`AdminDirectory.Users.get(email).name.fullName`), cached per email for
24h in the `staffNameCache` Script Property to avoid re-querying on
every 1-minute poll. This requires the "Admin Directory API" advanced
service added to this Apps Script project (Editor → Services (+) → Admin
Directory API) plus the same Workspace super-admin authorization already
required by `AUTO_LIVE_DETECTION` / `AUTO_CLASSROOM_PRESENCE_DETECTION`.
If that service isn't enabled, or the lookup fails for any reason, it
fails silently (same graceful-degradation pattern as the Meet/Classroom
auto-detection) and falls back to the old "Role · email-prefix" style
(e.g. "Admin · info1") so the badge never breaks.

Hovering the badge shows a longer role description (via the
`ROLE_LABELS` map in `Dashboard.html`). **Sept 2026, fifth round**: the
badge's container is no longer `position: fixed` --- it now sits inline
in a header row (`.app-header-top`) beside the title, specifically so it
can never overlap the header action buttons (which live in their own row
below, `.app-header-actions`) at any screen width; on narrow screens it
simply wraps onto its own line like any other flex item, rather than
floating over whatever happens to be underneath it. This replaced the
old "Signed in as `<email>` · `<role>`" line that used to sit under the
title, and later the fixed-corner-pill version from the second round.

## "Teacher NOT in Class" / "Needs Tech Support" --- 3-stage status flow

Both statuses are no longer a simple on/off flag --- each is a **3-stage
cycle** that advances one step at a time, refreshing on the Sheet
immediately on every click (independent of the sync trigger interval),
and wrapping back to the start once resolved. Both are role-gated on
**both** the client (`Dashboard.html`'s `roleCan()` shows a disabled
read-only pill instead of a button when the viewer can't perform the
next step) **and** the server (`setTeacherNotInClassStage` /
`setNeedsTechSupportStage` in `Code.gs` re-check and throw an `Error` if
not allowed, and also reject a call whose `targetStage` doesn't match
the expected next step for the row's *current* stage --- the client is
just UX, the server is the real gate). "Staff" below means admin or
headmaster.

**Teacher NOT in Class** (`teacherNotInClassStage`, values
`'none' | 'reported' | 'in_progress'`):

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Stage (label shown)     Who can advance it      Advances to
  ----------------------- ----------------------- -----------------------
  `none` --- "Teacher NOT a **student in that     `reported`
  in Class"               class**, or staff       

  `reported` --- "Tech    **staff only** (tech    `in_progress`
  Team talking with       team acknowledging)     
  Teacher"                                        

  `in_progress` ---       **that class's          `none`
  "Teacher Returned to    teacher**, or staff     
  Class"                                          
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

**Needs Tech Support** (`needsTechSupportStage`, values
`'none' | 'reported' | 'in_progress'`):

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Stage (label shown)     Who can advance it      Advances to
  ----------------------- ----------------------- -----------------------
  `none` --- "Need Tech   **the teacher or a      `reported`
  Support in Google       student in that         
  Class"                  class**, or staff       

  `reported` --- "Teach   **staff only** (tech    `in_progress`
  Team will Join to your  team acknowledging)     
  Classroom"                                      

  `in_progress` --- "Tech **staff only** (tech    `none`
  issue is been Resolved" team resolving)         
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

Notes: - The label shown on the card/button IS the current stage's name
--- clicking (when allowed) advances to the next stage in the table.
There's no separate "resolve" vs "report" wording; the arrow chain the
school asked for (e.g. "Teacher NOT in Class → Tech Team talking with
Teacher → Teacher Returned to Class → Teacher NOT in Class") is exactly
the sequence of labels the card cycles through. - Since a
teacher/student only ever sees their **own** classes (the role filter
above already restricts their course list), any card they see is
automatically "their" class --- so the permission checks just need to
know the viewer's role, not re-derive which class is theirs. - The
server stores `{ stage, updatedAt, updatedBy }` per course in Script
Properties (`teacherNotInClassMap` / `needsTechSupportMap`) and also
understands the older `{ flagged, updatedAt }` shape via
`normalizeStageEntry_()` (a `flagged: true` entry from before this
redesign is treated as `stage: 'reported'`), so no data was lost when
this changed from a boolean to a 3-stage cycle. - **Who clicked, and
when**: every stage transition records `updatedBy` ---
`{ email, name, role }` for whoever just clicked, computed via the same
`chatDisplayName_()` helper the chat uses (real Classroom name for
teacher/student, "Role · email-prefix" for staff). `Dashboard.html`
shows this directly on the card as a small caption under the badge ---
"by `<name>` · `mm/dd hh:mm`" (`renderStatusBadgeGroup()`) --- not just
in a tooltip, so it's visible without hovering. Because `updatedBy` is
overwritten on every transition (not just the initial report), the
caption always reflects whoever most recently acted on that status ---
e.g. it also shows who acknowledged or resolved it, not only who first
reported it. - If two people click at nearly the same moment (e.g. a
double-click, or two staff both open the dashboard), the server rejects
the second click with "That status just changed --- click Refresh and
try again." rather than silently applying an out-of-sequence transition
--- because it checks the *current* stage in Script Properties still
matches what the requested transition expects before writing.

## Staff notifications (email)

When a status is newly **reported** (the `none → reported` step only ---
not the later acknowledge/resolve steps), `notifyStaff_()` in `Code.gs`
sends a best-effort email via `MailApp.sendEmail()` to every address in
`ADMIN_EMAILS`, so the tech-support team / admin gets pushed a message
immediately rather than needing to have the dashboard open: - "Teacher
NOT in class --- `<course name>`" when a student (or staff) reports
it. - "Tech Support needed --- `<course name>`" when a teacher/student
(or staff) requests it.

Each email includes who reported it (email + role), the class
name/section, and a timestamp. `notifyStaff_()` swallows any `MailApp`
failure (e.g. daily quota) so a notification problem never blocks the
actual status update --- the Sheet/dashboard is already updated by the
time the email is attempted. `MailApp.sendEmail` counts against the
script owner's daily email quota (small schools are very unlikely to hit
it, but worth knowing if reports start coming in at high volume).

## Role-gated UI: "Force Sync Now" and "Open in Classroom"

Two controls are restricted beyond the course-list role filtering above:

-   **"Force Sync Now"** (pulls fresh data from the Classroom API on
    demand --- the one action that spends API quota) is visible only to
    admin/headmaster. `updateForceSyncVisibility()` in `Dashboard.html`
    hides the button (`display:none`) for teacher/student/none, called
    every time `getDashboardData()` returns (same place
    `updateChatVisibility()` runs). The button starts hidden in the raw
    HTML too, so there's no flash of it before the first load completes.
    This is UI-only unless backed by a server check, so the actual sync
    call was moved behind a new wrapper: `forceSyncClassroomData()` in
    `Code.gs` re-checks the viewer's role and throws if they're not
    admin/headmaster, then calls the real `syncClassroomData()` ---
    mirroring the same "client is just UX, server is the real gate"
    pattern used by
    `setTeacherNotInClassStage`/`setNeedsTechSupportStage`.
    `Dashboard.html`'s Force Sync click handler calls
    `forceSyncClassroomData()`, not `syncClassroomData()` directly. The
    time-driven trigger created by `createSyncTrigger()` still calls
    `syncClassroomData()` directly and is unaffected.
-   **"Open in Classroom →"** (the per-card link to that course's actual
    Google Classroom page, `c.link`) is visible only to **Admin** ---
    not Headmaster, Teacher, or Student. This was previously commented
    out entirely; it's now rendered conditionally via
    `roleCan('openInClassroom')` in `Dashboard.html`
    (`return role === 'admin'`), the same permission-check pattern
    already used for the status-flow buttons. This is a client-side-only
    restriction --- the underlying course record (and its `c.link`) is
    still present in the data sent to every role, same as before this
    change; actually opening the link still goes through Google
    Classroom's own access control, so a non-admin who found the URL
    some other way would just hit Google's own "you don't have access"
    page rather than the dashboard leaking anything sensitive.

## Live online presence (green dot on a person's photo)

Every teacher/student chip in a course card's roster can show a green
dot on their profile picture, indicating they're currently online. This
combines three signals, computed fresh on every `getDashboardData()`
call via `applyLivePresence_()` (so it's not baked into the
once-per-sync cache the way course rosters are):

1.  **Dashboard heartbeat (real-time)** --- every time a person's own
    browser loads or polls the dashboard, `getDashboardData()` calls
    `recordHeartbeat_(email)`, which stamps `{ lastSeen, loginAt }` for
    that email in the `presenceMap` Script Property. A heartbeat counts
    as "online" for `PRESENCE_ONLINE_WINDOW_MINUTES` (default 3 --- a
    little more than the 1-minute dashboard poll) after the last-seen
    time; if someone wasn't seen within that window (or ever), the next
    heartbeat resets `loginAt` to now, so `onlineSince` reflects when
    this online spell actually started, not just the latest poll.
2.  **Active Google Meet call** --- same `getMeetPresenceMap_()` used
    for the course-level "Live (Meet)" badge, but the call's start time
    is kept (not just a boolean) so it can double as an online-since
    proxy for that person specifically (teacher or student).
3.  **Recent Classroom activity** --- same `getClassroomActivityMap_()`
    used for the course-level "Teacher in Class (auto)" badge, keyed
    `email|courseId`, also keeping the most recent event's timestamp.

Signals 2 and 3 only refresh once per Classroom sync (same
`SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES` lag as the rest of that auto-detection feature
--- this was already true before this change and hasn't gotten worse).
Signal 1 is real-time. `applyLivePresence_()` sets `online` (bool) and
`onlineSince` (ISO string) on each person object, preferring the
heartbeat's `loginAt` when a heartbeat is live, else the Meet call start
time, else the Classroom activity time. `Dashboard.html`'s
`renderPeople()` shows a small green `.online-dot` on the avatar
whenever `online` is true.

This is separate from the pre-existing `inMeet`/`.person.in-meet`
styling (light-green chip background specifically for "currently in a
Google Meet call", still driven by the same Meet detection) --- a person
who's in Meet will show both.

`online`/`onlineSince` on every teacher/student object also feeds the
permanent "onboarded" flag (see "Student Onboarding Status page" below)
and the Student Onboarding Status page's online-count summary cards ---
both deduped by email, since one teacher can teach multiple courses.

**Twelfth round note**: `onlineSince` (this transient, "online right
now" value) is distinct from the newer, permanent, cross-source **Last
Login** value (`lastLoginDisplay`) described in its own section below
--- see "Cross-source Last Login tracking (Classroom / Meet /
Dashboard)". The green dot and its tooltip still use
`online`/`onlineSince`-derived data exactly as described here; the
visible "MM/DD HH:mm (GS/DB)" text under each person's avatar now comes
from the newer, permanent record instead, so it no longer disappears
when someone goes offline.

## Permanent student "onboarded" status

Separate from the transient `online`/`onlineSince` fields above, every
student object also carries `onboarded` (bool) and `onboardedAt` (ISO
string or null) --- set **once, permanently**, and never cleared again
even after that student goes offline. `applyStudentOnboardedFlag_()` in
`Code.gs` computes this on every `getDashboardData()` call, right after
`applyLivePresence_()` (which must run first, since this reads the
`online` flag it sets): the first time a student is ever seen `online`
(by **any** of the three presence signals above --- dashboard heartbeat,
Meet, or Classroom activity), their email is stamped into the
`onboardedStudents` Script Property with that moment's timestamp and
never removed. A student who has been online at least once always reads
`onboarded: true` from then on, regardless of their current
online/offline state.

This is intentionally simple --- there's no multi-stage "onboarding
pipeline" (no separate Assigned/Contacted/Scheduled stages); "onboarded"
just means "has ever logged in and been detected online, by any signal."
This was a deliberate scope decision (Sept 2026, fifth round) since no
such pipeline data exists in Classroom or the Sheet today --- see the
fifth-round changelog entry below for the alternatives that were
considered and rejected.

## Cross-source "Last Activity" tracking (Classroom / Meet / Dashboard) --- added twelfth round, redesigned thirteenth round to three independent sources + Dashboard sign-off

Every teacher and student has a **permanent, cross-source Last
Activity/Login value**, shown as the small text under their avatar in
every course card's roster (`.login-time`) ---
e.g. `09/11 09:30 (GC/GM/DB)`, `09/11 09:25 (GC/GM)`,
`09/11 09:30 (GC/DB)`, `09/11 09:15 (GC)`, `09/11 09:45 (GM)`, or
`09/11 09:30 (DB)`. Unlike the "online" green dot (see "Live online
presence" above), which is only true while the person is detected online
*right now*, this value is never cleared and never moves backward.

**Thirteenth-round redesign, in one sentence**: the twelfth round
tracked a single merged timestamp labeled `(GS)` (Classroom or Meet,
indistinguishable) or `(DB)`; the thirteenth round replaced that with
**three fully independent per-source timestamps** --- `GC` (Classroom),
`GM` (Meet, never confused with `GC`), and `DB` (Dashboard) --- and
changed the displayed label from "whichever ONE source was newest" to
"the newest TIMESTAMP, alongside ALL sources that have ever recorded
activity for that person." It also added an explicit Dashboard
**sign-off** signal (see below) so `DB` reflects the moment someone
actually leaves, not just their last periodic poll.

**Three independent source labels, always shown in this fixed order (GC,
then GM, then DB --- never reordered by recency):** - `GC` --- **Google
Classroom** activity. - `GM` --- **Google Meet** activity (never labeled
`GC` --- the two are tracked and displayed completely separately, per
the requirement that Meet must not be mistaken for Classroom). - `DB`
--- activity (a visit, or a sign-off) on the **Avvaiyar Padasalai
Classroom Dashboard** itself.

**Two calculations, done independently (this is the crux of the
thirteenth-round redesign)**: 1. **The displayed TIMESTAMP** is the
single most recent value among whichever source(s) have a recorded
timestamp for that person. 2. **The displayed SOURCE LIST** is every
source that has EVER recorded real activity for that person --- not just
whichever one happens to be the newest --- always rendered `GC/GM/DB` in
that fixed order, with any source that has no activity simply omitted.

For example, `GC = 10:00`, `GM = 10:05`, `DB = 10:03` → the newest
timestamp is `10:05` (from `GM`), but all three sources have activity on
file, so the result is `"10:05 (GC/GM/DB)"`, not `"10:05 (GM)"`.
Likewise `GC = 09/11 09:10`, `GM` = nothing, `DB = 09/11 09:30` → result
is `"09/11 09:30 (GC/DB)"` --- `GC`'s older timestamp still appears in
the source list even though `DB` is what's actually newest, because `GC`
did once have real recorded activity for this person. This split logic
lives in `summarizeLastLogin_(entry)` in `Code.gs`.

**Design note --- sources are permanent, like the rest of this record,
not a "recent activity" window.** Once a source has ever recorded real
activity for a person, it stays in that person's source list
indefinitely (mirroring the already-permanent, monotonic nature of this
whole record, and the "onboarded" flag pattern elsewhere in this app)
--- it is not automatically dropped after some number of days of no new
evidence from that source. This matches every example given when this
feature was specified. If the school later decides a source should
instead "expire" out of the displayed list after N days of silence
(independent from the timestamp comparison, which would be unaffected),
that would be a small, well-contained addition to
`summarizeLastLogin_()` (compare each source's own timestamp against
`Date.now()` before including it in `present`) --- flagging this now
since it's a real design choice, not an oversight, in case it's not
what's actually wanted long-term.

**Where each source's timestamp actually comes from** (no source is ever
fabricated --- if a source has no signal, it simply contributes
nothing): 1. **Google Classroom (`GC`)** --- the Admin Reports API's
Classroom application audit log, the exact same feed already used for
the "Teacher in Class (auto)" badge (`getClassroomActivityMap_()`, gated
behind `AUTO_CLASSROOM_PRESENCE_DETECTION` and requiring domain
audit-log collection --- see "Key configuration"). Google Classroom's
APIs do not expose a direct "last login" timestamp for a Classroom user,
so this --- a person's own most recent Classroom audit-log event --- is
the most reliable available proxy, and is what's used.
`getClassroomActivityMap_()` already builds
`{ "email|courseId": mostRecentTime }` for the badge; a few extra lines
collapse that down to one *per-person* latest timestamp (across all of a
person's courses) and merge it into the `gc` slot of the persistent Last
Activity record --- see `mergeLastLoginActivity_()` below. 2. **Google
Meet (`GM`)** --- the same Admin Reports API Meet audit log already used
for Meet-based "Live" detection (`getMeetPresenceMap_()`, gated behind
`AUTO_LIVE_DETECTION`). That function already scans every
`call_started`/`call_ended` event per person in the lookback window and
keeps the single most recent one; a few lines feed that same
most-recent-event timestamp into the `gm` slot of the persistent record.
Note this is intentionally a little broader than the "Live (Meet)" badge
itself, which only counts an *unmatched* `call_started` (i.e., presumed
still ongoing) --- for Last Activity purposes, having been in a Meet
call at all (even one that has since ended) is still real evidence of
activity and is used. 3. **Dashboard (`DB`)** --- two moments feed the
`db` slot, both through the exact same `recordHeartbeat_(email)`
function, so they're indistinguishable in the data (both are simply
"real proof this person's own browser was in contact with the Dashboard
at this moment") and both are labeled the same `DB`: - **Sign-on /
ongoing use** --- every time a person's own browser loads or polls the
dashboard (`getDashboardData()`, called on load and every
`DASHBOARD_POLL_MS` = 60s while the tab stays open), exactly as
before. - **Sign-off (added thirteenth round)** --- `Dashboard.html`
listens for `visibilitychange` (state becoming `'hidden'`) and, as a
backstop, `pagehide`, and on either fires one more best-effort call to a
new exposed function, `recordDashboardSignOff()`, which just calls
`recordHeartbeat_()` again for the current (server-derived,
un-spoofable) viewer. `visibilitychange` was used instead of
`beforeunload`/`unload` specifically because those two are not reliably
fired on tab close, mobile app-switch/kill, or OS-level termination ---
`visibilitychange` is the reliable, currently-recommended signal for
"the user is (probably) done with this page." Because this is layered on
top of the existing, already-reliable server-side heartbeat rather than
replacing it, a missed sign-off ping (offline, crashed tab, etc.) simply
leaves the last regular heartbeat as the recorded `DB` time --- nothing
is ever lost, and this can only make the recorded time MORE precise,
never wrong or worse.

**"Each source only ever moves forward" rule**: all three sources funnel
through one helper, `mergeLastLoginActivity_(candidates, sourceKey)` in
`Code.gs` (`sourceKey` is `'gc'`, `'gm'`, or `'db'`), which reads the
persistent record (`lastLoginMap` Script Property, keyed by normalized
email, each value now a `{ gc, gm, db }` object), and for each candidate
only overwrites THAT source's own slot if the candidate's timestamp is
strictly newer than what's already on file there --- a Meet timestamp
can never land in the `gc` slot or vice versa, and an older event from a
source can never overwrite that same source's newer stored value.
`summarizeLastLogin_()` (see above) is what separately computes the
newest-overall timestamp and the combined source list from those three
independent slots --- the "most recent wins" comparison and the "which
sources are present" question are two distinct calculations, never
conflated. Because each source's merge only ever moves that source's own
timestamp *forward*, it's safe to call on every sync/poll even though
the same underlying event may be observed again on a later call
(e.g. the same Meet call is still inside the Reports API lookback window
on the next sync) --- the timestamp simply doesn't move, so this doesn't
create duplicate records or spurious updates.

**Where this is stored and computed**: -
`LAST_LOGIN_PROP_KEY = 'lastLoginMap'` --- a single Script Property
holding
`{ normalizedEmail: { gc: isoUTC|absent, gm: isoUTC|absent, db: isoUTC|absent } }`
for every person ever seen by any of the three sources. This is
intentionally separate from `presenceMap` (the transient online/offline
tracker) --- Last Activity is a permanent record, presence is not. -
**Migration from the twelfth-round shape**:
`normalizeLastLoginEntry_(entry)` transparently reads the old
`{ ts, source: 'GS'|'DB' }` shape wherever it's still stored and
converts it: an old `'DB'` entry becomes `{ db: ts }` (unambiguous,
safely carried forward); an old `'GS'` entry is **dropped** rather than
guessed into `gc` or `gm`, because the twelfth round intentionally
logged Classroom and Meet under one shared label and genuinely doesn't
know which one it was --- per the "never fabricate" requirement, that
ambiguous history is not attributed to either specific source. That
person's `GC`/`GM` columns simply start blank again and refill with
correctly-labeled evidence on the very next sync; their `DB` history is
unaffected. This migration happens transparently and repeatedly (every
read/merge), with no separate migration step to run. -
`getClassroomActivityMap_()` and `getMeetPresenceMap_()` (both already
run once per `syncClassroomData()` call, i.e. every
`SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES`) each call `mergeLastLoginActivity_()` once ---
with a per-person map of their single latest timestamp from that source,
into their own `'gc'`/`'gm'` slot respectively --- as a side effect of
building the data they already return for the existing Meet/Classroom
"Live" detection features. No new API calls were added. -
`recordHeartbeat_()` (run on every `getDashboardData()` call ---
load/poll --- AND now also on sign-off, via `recordDashboardSignOff()`)
merges the current moment into the `'db'` slot only, under the same
`LockService` best-effort lock it already uses for `presenceMap`. -
`applyLastLogin_(courses)` --- a step in `getDashboardData()`, run right
after `applyLivePresence_(courses)` --- reads `lastLoginMap`,
normalizes/migrates each entry, and calls `summarizeLastLogin_()` to
stamp fields onto every teacher/student object: `lastLoginAt` (raw ISO
UTC of the newest applicable source, or `null`), `lastLoginSource`
(combined string in fixed order, e.g. `'GC/GM/DB'`, `'GC/DB'`, `'GM'`,
or `null`), `lastLoginDisplay` --- the ready-to-render string,
e.g. `"09/11 09:30 (GC/GM/DB)"`, or `''` if this person has no recorded
activity yet from any source (preserving the existing "nothing shown"
behavior rather than fabricating a value) --- and `lastLoginBySource`
(`{ gc, gm, db }` raw per-source timestamps or `null`, exposed for any
future admin-facing detail view without needing to re-derive it). -
`Dashboard.html`'s `renderPeople()` shows `p.lastLoginDisplay` (when
non-empty) as the `.login-time` label under each avatar, exactly as it
did after the twelfth round --- no client-side rendering logic changed
in the thirteenth round, since the combined string is fully computed
server-side. The green online dot and its "Online · last activity ..."
tooltip are unaffected --- they still come from `online`/`onlineSince`
exactly as described in "Live online presence" above.

**Timezone**: `formatLastLoginTimestamp_(isoUtc)` in `Code.gs` converts
the stored UTC timestamp using
`Utilities.formatDate(date, 'America/New_York', 'MM/dd HH:mm')` ---
computed **server-side**, so the displayed timestamp is always US
Eastern time (EST/EDT, DST-aware) no matter what timezone the viewer's
own browser/OS happens to be set to. `LAST_LOGIN_TIMEZONE` holds the
`'America/New_York'` IANA timezone name as a named constant near the top
of `Code.gs`. This is deliberately different from the pre-existing
`formatLoginTime()` in `Dashboard.html` (used for the "online since"
tooltip and for the unrelated "who clicked / when" status-flow
captions), which formats in the *viewer's own local* browser time and
was left completely unchanged.

**Error handling / resilience** --- matches the existing
graceful-degradation pattern used everywhere else in this file: - If the
Classroom Reports API call fails or isn't authorized,
`getClassroomActivityMap_()` catches the error and returns `{}`
**before** any merge happens --- nothing is written to the `gc` slot,
and whatever value was already on file there (or in `gm`/`db`) is left
untouched. - Same for `getMeetPresenceMap_()` --- a Reports API failure
returns `{}` with no merge attempted, and `gc`/`db` are unaffected. - If
`AUTO_CLASSROOM_PRESENCE_DETECTION` or `AUTO_LIVE_DETECTION` is turned
off, that source simply never runs and never contributes to Last
Activity --- the other sources are unaffected. - If the Dashboard
sign-off ping (`recordDashboardSignOff`) never reaches the server
(offline, crashed tab, browser killed instantly), the `db` slot simply
keeps whatever the last successful regular heartbeat recorded ---
`gc`/`gm` are completely unaffected either way. - One
Classroom/Meet/Dashboard source failing never blocks or clears any other
student/teacher's record, nor any OTHER source's slot for the same
person --- `mergeLastLoginActivity_()` operates per-person, per-source,
and only ever adds/advances that one slot, never deletes any slot. -
**No activity from any source ever** --- the person's `lastLoginDisplay`
stays `''` (nothing rendered), matching the pre-existing "No Login"
behavior for someone who's never been detected active anywhere.

**Limitations to know about**: - Google Classroom's public/Admin APIs do
not expose a literal "user login" timestamp --- the Classroom
audit-log-based signal here reflects **Classroom activity**, which is
the closest and most reliable proxy available, not a raw sign-in event.
It also depends on the domain having Classroom audit log collection
enabled (Admin console → Reports → Audit and investigation) and the
script running as an authorized Workspace super admin --- the same two
requirements `AUTO_CLASSROOM_PRESENCE_DETECTION` already has. - Google
Meet activity likewise depends on `AUTO_LIVE_DETECTION` being enabled
and the same super-admin authorization, and only sees the events the
Admin Reports API's Meet audit log surfaces (`call_started` /
`call_ended`) inside `MEET_ACTIVE_WINDOW_MINUTES` of each sync. - Both
Classroom and Meet detection only refresh at the `SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES`
cadence (or on "Force Sync Now") --- so a very recent Classroom/Meet
event may take up to that long to be reflected in this person's record,
whereas a Dashboard visit (or sign-off) is reflected instantly, on the
very next `getDashboardData()`/`recordDashboardSignOff()` call. - The
Dashboard sign-off signal is inherently best-effort --- no browser
guarantees a script gets to run as a tab closes. `visibilitychange` is
materially more reliable than `beforeunload`/`unload` for this, but "the
user closed the laptop lid" or "the OS force-killed the browser" can
still occasionally beat it. This is why it's built as a *enhancement* on
top of the already-reliable 60-second heartbeat, not the only mechanism
--- the worst case is simply up to \~60s of imprecision on the `DB`
timestamp, never a missing one. - No new Advanced Google Services or
Google Cloud APIs are required beyond what `AUTO_LIVE_DETECTION` /
`AUTO_CLASSROOM_PRESENCE_DETECTION` already needed (the Admin SDK's
Reports API, via the `AdminReports` advanced service) --- this feature
is purely additive logic on top of data those two features already
fetch, plus the existing Dashboard heartbeat mechanism (now also
triggered on sign-off). No new OAuth scopes are required either, for the
same reason.

## Shared dashboard chat

A live, shared chat room --- every recognized viewer (admin, headmaster,
teacher, or student; **not** role `'none'`) can read every message and
post their own. There are no separate rooms per class or per role; it's
one shared stream for the whole school, rendered as a slide-in panel
from the right edge of the screen (`.chat-panel` in `Dashboard.html`),
toggled by a floating 💬 button (bottom-right, `#chatToggleBtn`) that
carries an unread-count badge while the panel is closed.

-   **Storage**: every message is one appended row on the
    **`Dashboard_Chat_Window`** tab (the `CHAT_SHEET_NAME` constant) of
    the same workbook as "Courses" (created automatically via
    `getOrCreateChatSheet_()` / `getWorkbook_()` the first time anyone
    posts). Columns: `Timestamp` (ISO string), `Email`, `Role`, `Name`,
    `Message`, `Class Name`. `Class Name` was added as a 6th column
    **after** `Message` (not inserted in the middle) specifically so any
    pre-existing rows from before this change --- which only ever had 5
    columns --- still read back correctly; their (missing) Class Name
    cell just comes back blank. Nothing chat-related is stored in Script
    Properties --- the Sheet tab **is** the full history (aside from the
    retention prune below).
-   **Class name tagging**: when a student or teacher posts,
    `postChatMessage()` computes their class name(s) via
    `findClassNamesForViewer_()` (comma-joined if enrolled in/teaching
    more than one synced course) and stores it in the `Class Name`
    column. `Dashboard.html`'s `renderChat()` shows it in the message's
    meta line --- "`<Student Name>` · `<Class Name>` · `<time>`" --- so
    every student message is traceable to both who sent it and which
    class they're in. Admin/headmaster messages have no class name
    (staff aren't enrolled in a course).
-   **10-day retention**: `pruneOldChatMessages_()` deletes chat rows
    older than `CHAT_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 10) directly from the
    Sheet tab. It's called from both `getChatMessages()` and
    `postChatMessage()`, but throttled via the `chatLastPruneAt` Script
    Property to run at most once per `CHAT_PRUNE_MIN_INTERVAL_MS`
    (default 6h) --- since `getChatMessages()` alone is polled every 8
    seconds by every open dashboard, and a full-column scan+delete on
    every poll would be wasteful. No separate time trigger is needed;
    the prune just piggybacks on however chat is already being
    read/posted to. This only prunes the underlying Sheet --- it's
    independent of `CHAT_HISTORY_LIMIT` (200), which separately caps how
    many recent rows a single `getChatMessages()` call returns to the
    browser.
-   **Reading** (`getChatMessages()`): returns the most recent
    `CHAT_HISTORY_LIMIT` (200) rows, oldest first. An unrecognized
    (`'none'`) viewer gets an empty array --- same access rule as the
    rest of the dashboard.
-   **Posting** (`postChatMessage(text)`): rejects blank messages,
    truncates anything over `CHAT_MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH` (2000 chars), and
    throws if the viewer's role is `'none'`. On success it appends the
    row and returns the fresh message list, so the poster's own UI
    updates in the same round trip.
-   **Display name** (`chatDisplayName_()`): a teacher/student shows
    their real Classroom display name (looked up by email across every
    synced course's rosters via `findDisplayName_()`); admin/headmaster
    show as `"Admin · <email-prefix>"` / `"Headmaster · <email-prefix>"`
    (e.g. `Admin · info1`) since staff accounts don't have a Classroom
    profile name to borrow --- this still lets people tell the different
    admin/headmaster accounts apart without exposing full email
    addresses in the chat log itself (though `person.email` is stored in
    the underlying Sheet row). This same helper is now also reused for
    the "who clicked" caption on status-flow badges (see its section
    above) --- but NOT for the top-right badge, which uses
    `resolveViewerBadgeName_()` instead (see "Role-based access").
-   **Polling**: the open dashboard polls `getChatMessages()` every 8
    seconds (`CHAT_POLL_MS`) regardless of whether the panel is open, so
    the unread badge updates even while it's closed; opening the panel
    also force-reloads and scrolls to the latest message. This is
    independent of the main 1-minute dashboard poll and the Classroom
    sync cadence.
-   **Visibility**: `updateChatVisibility()` (called after every
    `getDashboardData()` response) hides the chat toggle button entirely
    for role `'none'` --- an unrecognized account never sees the chat
    exists.
-   No moderation/delete tooling exists yet beyond the automatic 10-day
    retention prune --- if a message needs removing sooner than that, it
    isn't exposed as an admin action today.

## Student Onboarding Status page

A second top-level view in `Dashboard.html`, next to "Classes"
(`.view-tabs` --- `#tabClasses` / `#tabOnboarding`, toggled by
`switchView()`), redesigned (Sept 2026, fifth round) as a compact,
Google Workspace-admin-style page. Layout, top to bottom:

1.  **Tabs** --- underline-style, Google-tab look (`.view-tab` --- gray
    text, blue text + blue underline when active).
2.  **Summary cards** (`.onboarding-summary`, id
    `#onboardingOnlineSummary`) --- six compact stat cards, recomputed
    from the **currently filtered** groups (so narrowing the filters
    below also updates these numbers):
    -   **Total Students** --- roster size across the filtered groups
        (always visible, per the school's explicit requirement that this
        count never be hidden).
    -   **Students Online** / **Teachers Online** --- distinct people
        (deduped by email) currently online right now, from the same
        `online` flag as "Live online presence" above.
    -   **Students Assigned** --- roster size for groups that have at
        least one teacher (as opposed to a class with no teacher on
        record).
    -   **Students Pending** --- a **class-level rollup**: roster size
        for groups whose overall status (see below) is "Pending" ---
        i.e. no student in that class has EVER been onboarded yet.
    -   **Students Not Onboarded** --- a **student-level count**:
        individual students (across all filtered groups) whose own
        permanent `onboarded` flag is still false --- this also counts
        stragglers inside a class that's already "Onboarding" (partially
        onboarded), so it's deliberately not the same number as
        "Students Pending".
3.  **Filter bar** (`.report-filters`) --- one row: grade `<select>`
    (`#onboardingGradeFilter`), day `<select>` (`#onboardingDayFilter`),
    a live student-name search box (`#onboardingStudentSearch`, filters
    to groups containing a matching student --- new in this round), and
    "Clear Filters".
4.  **Table** (`.report-table-wrap`, capped at `max-height: 56vh` with
    its own internal scrollbar and a sticky `<thead>`, so a long roster
    scrolls inside the table rather than growing the whole page) ---
    columns **Class / Section \| Day & Time \| Teacher \| Students \|
    Status**:
    -   **Class / Section** --- the grade name (course Name) with the
        `COURSE_NAME_SUFFIX` suffix (e.g. "AY26-27") stripped off for
        display and shown as a small secondary line underneath instead
        (`stripCourseSuffix()` in `Dashboard.html`; purely cosmetic, the
        underlying data is untouched).
    -   **Day & Time** --- the course Section string, unchanged.
    -   **Teacher** --- each teacher's name; their phone number
        (`person.phone`, already captured server-side but historically
        not rendered --- see `SHOW_CONTACT_PHONE`) is appended only when
        `getShowContactPhone()` reports the flag is `true`, so this
        table respects the same phone-visibility setting as the rest of
        the dashboard rather than introducing its own rule.
    -   **Students** --- the group's student count as a small blue
        badge/chip (e.g. "6 Students"), not a bare number.
    -   **Status** --- one of five deterministic badges, computed by
        `computeGroupStatus()` in this priority order: **No Students**
        (zero students on the roster) → **Active** (any teacher or
        student in the group is online right now) → **Completed** (every
        student has been permanently onboarded) → **Pending** (no
        student has EVER been onboarded) → **Onboarding** (some
        onboarded, some not --- the remaining case). This is
        intentionally NOT a multi-step pipeline the school manages by
        hand; it's fully derived from the `online`/`onboarded` data
        already described above.
5.  **Footer** (`<footer class="app-footer">`, shared with the Classes
    view, not duplicated per tab) --- "© Avvaiyar Padasalai \| World's
    First Online Tamil School", with a top border and margin so it's
    never mistaken for another table row.

**Where the data comes from** (unchanged since the third round): course
**Name** = grade/NILAI, course **Section** = class time;
`buildOnboardingGroups()` in `Dashboard.html` groups by
`name + '||' + section`, now carrying each group's full
`teachers[]`/`students[]` arrays (not just a count) so
status/online/onboarded can be derived per group --- still entirely
client-side from the same `allCourses` the Classes view already has, no
new server call for the grouping itself (though the underlying
`online`/`onboarded` flags are computed server-side, see their own
sections above). Role-based filtering is inherited the same way as
before: staff see every grade/time combination school-wide; a
teacher/student only ever has their own class(es) in `allCourses`. -
**Sorting**: unchanged --- grades sort numerically by their trailing
number (`naturalCompare()`), then by class time within a grade
(`timeSortKey()`). - **"Total Students" footer row** in the table itself
is still kept (`<tfoot>`, `#onboardingTotal`) alongside the new "Total
Students" summary card, for continuity with the pre-redesign version. -
**Staying live**: still refreshed on the same 1-minute dashboard poll as
the Classes view (`load()`'s success handler calls `renderOnboarding()`
instead of `render()` when this tab is active).

## Key configuration (top of Code.gs)

-   `TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID` --- hardcoded to the school's spreadsheet:
    `1rlFMiXDMVaBcZS89AL0OC5TYeXz4PIZyXXboYoDGzX0`
-   `COURSE_NAME_SUFFIX = 'AY26-27'` --- only Classroom courses whose
    name ends with this (case-insensitive, trimmed) are synced. Set to
    `''` to sync every active course. Exposed to the client via
    `getCourseNameSuffix()` (added fifth round) so `Dashboard.html` can
    display/strip it without hardcoding the string a second time. Also
    used by `normalizeClassKey_()` (tenth round) to match WhatsApp group
    links regardless of whether this suffix is present in a given name.
-   `SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (default `15`) --- how often
    `syncClassroomData()` runs on its time trigger. Change this
    constant, then re-run `createSyncTrigger()` once to reschedule (it
    deletes any existing trigger first, so it's safe to re-run any time
    the value changes). `createSyncTrigger()` validates the value
    against Apps Script's allowed `.everyMinutes()` intervals --- **1,
    5, 10, 15, or 30 only** --- and throws a clear error if it's
    anything else (e.g. 60; use a separate `.everyHours()` trigger
    instead if an hourly cadence is ever wanted). The dashboard's "syncs
    automatically every N min" text reads this value live via
    `getSyncIntervalMinutes()`, so it never goes stale.
-   `ADMIN_EMAILS` / `HEADMASTER_EMAILS` --- see "Role-based access"
    above; also used as the "staff" / tech-support-team recipient list
    for `notifyStaff_()`.
-   `CHAT_SHEET_NAME` / `CHAT_MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH` / `CHAT_HISTORY_LIMIT`
    / `CHAT_RETENTION_DAYS` / `CHAT_PRUNE_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` --- see
    "Shared dashboard chat" above.
-   `PRESENCE_PROP_KEY` / `PRESENCE_ONLINE_WINDOW_MINUTES` --- see "Live
    online presence" above.
-   `LAST_LOGIN_PROP_KEY` / `LAST_LOGIN_TIMEZONE` /
    `LAST_LOGIN_SOURCE_ORDER` / `LAST_LOGIN_SOURCE_LABELS` --- added
    twelfth round, redesigned thirteenth round; see "Cross-source 'Last
    Activity' tracking (Classroom / Meet / Dashboard)" above.
    `LAST_LOGIN_PROP_KEY` is the Script Property name for the permanent,
    cross-source `{gc, gm, db}`-per-person map; `LAST_LOGIN_TIMEZONE`
    (`'America/New_York'`) is the IANA timezone it's always displayed
    in, server-side, regardless of viewer timezone;
    `LAST_LOGIN_SOURCE_ORDER` (`['gc','gm','db']`) fixes the display
    order (never reordered by recency); `LAST_LOGIN_SOURCE_LABELS` maps
    each internal key to its display code (`GC`/`GM`/`DB`).
-   `ONBOARDED_STUDENTS_PROP_KEY` --- Script Property key for the
    permanent per-student onboarded map (see "Permanent student
    'onboarded' status" above). Added fifth round.
-   `KNOWLEDGE_BASE_VIDEOS` --- the Knowledge Base --- Videos catalog
    (see "Knowledge Base -- Videos tab" below). Added sixth round; edit
    this array and redeploy to add/remove/edit a video.
-   `WHATSAPP_LINKS_SHEET_NAME` --- the Sheet tab name for the WhatsApp
    group link lookup (see "WhatsApp join links on class cards" below,
    tenth/eleventh round). There is **no** hardcoded array of the links
    themselves in `Code.gs` (the tenth round's one-time
    `WHATSAPP_LINKS_SEED` array was removed in the eleventh round, see
    below) --- the `WhatsApp_Group_Links` Sheet tab is the sole source
    of truth, and ongoing edits happen there, not in this file.
-   **Hidden co-teacher accounts** --- two lists exclude admin/support
    co-teacher accounts from every course's "Teacher(s)" roster:
    -   `HIDDEN_TEACHER_NAMES` --- exact match (case-insensitive,
        trimmed). Currently: `google classroom admin`.
    -   `HIDDEN_TEACHER_NAME_PREFIXES` --- hides any name that STARTS
        WITH one of these (case-insensitive, trimmed). Currently:
        `avvaiyar padasalai`, `aps` --- the `aps` prefix alone covers
        "APS Tech Support", "APS Admin", "APS - IT Desk", or any other
        name starting with APS, so there's no need for a separate "APS
        Tech Support" entry.
    -   Add more entries to either list as new admin/support logins get
        added as co-teachers. If a course's only "teacher" is a hidden
        name, it correctly shows as "No teacher assigned".
-   `SHOW_CONTACT_PHONE` --- defaults to `false`. Several
    teacher/headmaster Google accounts have a phone number baked into
    their Classroom display name (e.g. "Mrs. Kavitha - 98410 12345").
    `splitNameAndPhone_()` strips that phone number out of the name
    before it's shown in the dashboard, applied to both teachers and
    students in `buildCourseRecord_`. The phone number itself is still
    captured in `person.phone` on each teacher/student object --- it's
    rendered nowhere in `Dashboard.html` while this is `false`,
    INCLUDING the Student Onboarding Status page's Teacher column (added
    fifth round, gated behind the same flag via `getShowContactPhone()`)
    --- so flipping `SHOW_CONTACT_PHONE` to `true` later brings the
    phone number back into both places with no other code changes
    needed.
-   `AUTO_LIVE_DETECTION` --- when true, marks a class "Live (Meet)"
    automatically if its teacher is in an active Google Meet call (via
    the Admin Reports API, applicationName `meet`). Requires the script
    to be authorized by a Workspace super admin; otherwise fails
    silently and the manual "Mark Live" toggle still works. Can't tell
    WHICH course a call belongs to --- if a teacher teaches multiple
    active courses, all go live together. Also feeds the per-person
    "online" dot (see "Live online presence" above) for both teachers
    and students, and (twelfth round) the Meet side of Last Login.
-   `MEET_ACTIVE_WINDOW_MINUTES` --- how far back to look for an
    unfinished Meet call; should be at least as long as the longest
    class period.
-   `AUTO_CLASSROOM_PRESENCE_DETECTION` --- when true, marks a class
    "Teacher in Class" automatically as soon as a teacher's Classroom
    activity shows up in the Admin Reports API's Classroom audit log
    (applicationName `classroom`, parameter `course_id` on each event
    via `COURSE_ID_LOG_PARAM`). Unlike Meet detection, this IS tied to
    the exact course, since Classroom log events carry a course_id.
    Requires the same super-admin authorization as Meet detection,
    **plus** Classroom audit log data collection enabled for the domain
    in the Admin console (Reports \> Audit and investigation) --- only
    available on some Google Workspace for Education editions, so this
    may do nothing on some domains. Fails silently (same
    graceful-degradation pattern as Meet detection) if
    unavailable/unauthorized --- nothing else breaks. The `course_id`
    parameter name is based on Google's published schema at time of
    writing and hasn't been verified against a live domain; if sync
    succeeds but "Teacher in Class" never triggers, check the Apps
    Script execution log for what the Classroom audit log actually
    returns in this domain and adjust `COURSE_ID_LOG_PARAM` if needed.
    Also feeds the per-person "online" dot (see "Live online presence"
    above) for both teachers and students, and (twelfth round) the
    Classroom side of Last Login.
-   `CLASSROOM_ACTIVE_WINDOW_MINUTES` --- how recent a teacher's
    Classroom activity must be to still count as "currently in class";
    default 20 min.

## Dashboard UI features

-   **Header** --- restructured (fifth round) into two rows inside
    `.app-header`: `.app-header-top` (school logo + title + subtitle on
    the left, the signed-in badge on the right --- flex-wrapping, never
    fixed-position) and `.app-header-actions` below it (School Calendar
    / Syllabus / Live Tech Support (Zoom) / Raise Service Request, in
    their own independently-wrapping row). Keeping these as two separate
    flex rows, instead of one row with a fixed-position badge floating
    over it, is what guarantees the badge and the action buttons can
    never visually overlap at any screen width.
-   **School logo**: `.brand-logo`, pulled from the school's public
    website (`https://www.avvaiyarpadasalai.org/media/aps-logo.jpg`),
    shown beside the title. This was inferred from "refer the school
    website for image/logo/colour code" rather than an explicit
    instruction --- swap the `src` if a different logo asset is
    preferred. Its `onerror` hides it gracefully if that URL ever
    breaks, same defensive pattern used for avatar photos.
-   **Brand color**: the existing `--blue: #1a73e8` CSS variable (Google
    blue) was kept/reused as "APS branded blue" everywhere the redesign
    needed a primary action color. The school website's exact brand hex
    code could not be confirmed (page-fetching tools return rendered
    text, not the underlying CSS) --- if the school has an exact hex
    code on file, it's a one-line change to `--blue` in
    `Dashboard.html`'s `:root`.
-   **Header title / accreditation line** (ninth round): the `<h1>`
    reads "Avvaiyar Padasalai Tamil Virtual School --- Classroom
    Dashboard"; directly beneath it a small `.brand-accreditation` line
    reads "A registered 501(c)(3) non-profit public charity, run
    entirely by volunteers. Fully accredited by WASC, California, USA."
    --- sits above the existing sync-status `.subtitle` line, styled
    with the same muted gray/small-text treatment.
-   **Header links/actions** (`.header-actions`): "📅 School Calendar"
    (`https://www.avvaiyarpadasalai.org/calendar.html`), "📚 Syllabus"
    (`https://www.avvaiyarpadasalai.org/syllabus.html`), "📹 Live Tech
    Support (Zoom)" (opens the Zoom modal --- see below), and "🎫 Raise
    Service Request"
    (`https://helpdesk.avvaiyarpadasalai.org/portal/en/newticket`) ---
    all plain links/buttons in one row. Update the `href`s directly in
    `Dashboard.html` if any URL changes.
-   **Live Tech Support (Zoom) button**: opens a small modal with a
    "Join Zoom Meeting" link, Meeting ID, and Passcode --- currently
    `https://us06web.zoom.us/j/89487502551?pwd=cLtFRxjbQdGpeq0YYiypozzuWEHaEZ.1`,
    ID `894 8750 2551`, passcode `APS2026`. All three values are
    hardcoded in the modal markup in `Dashboard.html`; update them there
    if the meeting ever changes.
-   **Classes / Student Onboarding Status tabs** --- see "Student
    Onboarding Status page" above for the redesigned tab; tab styling is
    now an underline (Google-style) rather than a filled pill.
-   **WhatsApp join link on every class card** (tenth round; label
    updated eleventh round) --- see "WhatsApp join links on class cards"
    below.
-   **Floating chat button** --- kept bottom-right (`.chat-toggle-btn`),
    no position change; instead `body`'s bottom padding was increased
    (fifth round, to `110px`) so that when the page is scrolled all the
    way down, the fixed button hovers over blank buffer space rather
    than over the footer text or the last table row.
-   **"Force Sync Now" (admin/headmaster only) and "Open in Classroom"
    (Admin only)** --- see "Role-gated UI: 'Force Sync Now' and 'Open in
    Classroom'" above.
-   **Shared dashboard chat** --- see its own section above.
-   **Live online presence (green dot)** --- see its own section above.
    **Twelfth round**: the text label under each avatar shows a
    permanent, cross-source Last Activity value instead of the transient
    "online since" time. **Thirteenth round**: that value now
    independently tracks and combines THREE sources --- `GC`/`GM`/`DB`
    --- instead of a merged `GS`/`DB`, and `DB` is now also updated on
    Dashboard sign-off, not just sign-on/poll --- see "Cross-source
    'Last Activity' tracking" above.
-   **Confirmation toast**: advancing "Teacher NOT in Class" or "Needs
    Tech Support" to its next stage shows a brief bottom-of-screen toast
    (`showToast()` in `Dashboard.html`, e.g. "Teacher marked as back in
    class.") right after the server call succeeds. This exists
    specifically because the card can immediately disappear from view
    once the list refreshes (e.g. the "Teacher NOT in Class" filter is
    active and the course no longer matches it) --- without the toast, a
    successful action could look like nothing happened.
-   **Dedicated student search** (Classes tab): a second toolbar row
    with its own input + "Find Student" button (separate from the main
    class/teacher search box above it). Filters the grid to only classes
    containing a matching student, and highlights that student's chip in
    the roster. Has its own "Clear student search" link; also reset by
    the main "Clear filters" button. (The Student Onboarding Status tab
    has its own, separate, always-live student-name search --- see that
    section above.)
-   **Filter buttons** are color-coded when active, via a `.active`
    class toggled in `updateFilterButtons()` (called on every
    `render()`):
    -   "Live only" → green
    -   "No students only" → red
    -   "Teacher NOT in Class" → red (matches any course whose
        `teacherNotInClassStage` isn't `'none'`)
    -   "Needs Tech Support" → blue (matches any course whose
        `needsTechSupportStage` isn't `'none'`)
    -   Only one filter can be active at a time (clicking one deselects
        any other); "Clear filters" resets to none.
-   **Live status badge has three possible sources** (`c.liveSource`),
    checked in this priority order: `'meet'` (teacher in an active Meet
    call --- badge reads "Live (Meet)", toggle button disabled/auto),
    `'classroom'` (teacher's recent Classroom activity detected ---
    badge reads "Teacher in Class", toggle button disabled/auto, labeled
    "Teacher in Class (auto)"), or `'manual'` (someone clicked "Mark
    Live" --- badge reads "Live (manual)", toggle button active and
    clickable). Only when none of these apply does the manual toggle
    button do anything.
-   **"Teacher NOT in Class" and "Needs Tech Support" are role-gated
    3-stage status flows** --- see their own section above for exactly
    who can advance each stage, plus the "who clicked, and when"
    caption. Mechanically:
    -   `setTeacherNotInClassStage(courseId, targetStage)` /
        `setNeedsTechSupportStage(courseId, targetStage)` both persist
        to Script Properties (`teacherNotInClassMap` /
        `needsTechSupportMap`, storing
        `{ stage, updatedAt, updatedBy }`, same overall pattern as the
        existing `liveMap`/"Mark Live" toggle) and patch the same row's
        Sheet columns + Detail JSON immediately, so they show up in the
        raw Sheet too, not just the dashboard.
    -   Each button's clickable state and label come from
        `TEACHER_NOT_IN_CLASS_STAGE_INFO` /
        `NEEDS_TECH_SUPPORT_STAGE_INFO` in `Dashboard.html`, keyed by
        the course's current stage; the button carries a
        `data-next-stage` attribute so the click handler knows exactly
        which stage to request without re-deriving it.
    -   A course with either status not `'none'` shows a colored badge
        on the card (the badge text is the current stage's label) plus a
        small "by `<name>` · `mm/dd hh:mm`" caption underneath, and
        rolls up into the two summary chips ("Teacher NOT in Class",
        "Needs Tech Support") and the two matching filter buttons above.
    -   **Sheet column order**: `Teacher NOT In Class Stage`,
        `Teacher NOT In Class Updated At`, `Needs Tech Support Stage`,
        `Needs Tech Support Updated At` sit after `Live Updated At` and
        before `Last Synced`/`Detail JSON` --- same column positions as
        before this redesign (columns just now hold a stage string like
        `reported` instead of `TRUE`/`FALSE`). `updatedBy` is NOT a
        separate column --- it only lives inside the `Detail JSON`
        column, same as the new per-person presence fields --- so
        nothing that reads this sheet by column position needs updating
        for either of those. If anything else reads this sheet by column
        position, it needs updating.
-   **Teacher/student names show without phone numbers by default** (see
    `SHOW_CONTACT_PHONE` above) --- the "Teacher(s)" and "Students"
    roster sections, and the Student Onboarding Status page's Teacher
    column, only render `person.phone` when that flag is `true`.
    `person.email` is likewise never rendered directly in the course
    cards, though it IS used server-side (in
    `getViewerRole_`/`getViewerContext_`, the status-flow permission
    checks, presence heartbeat lookup, Last Login lookup, and chat
    display-name lookup) to match the signed-in viewer to their
    course(s)/identity.
-   **Footer** --- "© Avvaiyar Padasalai \| World's First Online Tamil
    School", shared across both tabs, added fifth round (see "Student
    Onboarding Status page").

## WhatsApp join links on class cards (tenth round; seed array removed & label updated eleventh round)

Every class card (Classes tab) can show a "Join to WhatsApp" link with
the WhatsApp glyph --- visible to **every role** (student, teacher,
headmaster, admin), with no `roleCan()` gate at all, unlike "Open in
Classroom" (Admin-only, see above).

-   **Live, editable lookup --- not a hardcoded array.**
    `WhatsApp_Group_Links` is a Sheet tab in the same workbook as
    "Courses"/"Dashboard_Chat_Window", auto-created if missing
    (`getOrCreateWhatsAppLinksSheet_()`), with columns
    `Class Name | Schedule (reference only) | WhatsApp Group Link`. Only
    columns A and C are ever read by code --- column B is a free-text
    note for humans only, never parsed. This is Sheet-backed by
    deliberate choice: the school asked for this lookup to live
    somewhere they can update themselves "whenever needed" without a
    code change --- unlike `KNOWLEDGE_BASE_VIDEOS` (a hardcoded array
    you edit + redeploy).
-   **Eleventh-round cleanup: the one-time seed array is gone.** The
    tenth round's `WHATSAPP_LINKS_SEED` array (194 `[className, url]`
    pairs, used only to populate the sheet the first time it was
    created) has been **deleted from `Code.gs` entirely** --- the
    `WhatsApp_Group_Links` sheet was already fully populated in
    production, so the seed had already served its one-time purpose and
    was pure dead weight (194 lines of link data duplicated in source
    that could only ever drift from the real sheet).
    `getOrCreateWhatsAppLinksSheet_()` now just creates an empty tab
    (header row only) if one somehow doesn't exist yet --- e.g. for a
    brand-new copy of this project deployed for a different school ---
    with no seed data. The Sheet has been, and remains, the **only**
    place these links are stored.
-   **Matching**: `normalizeClassKey_(name)` strips a trailing
    `COURSE_NAME_SUFFIX` if present, then removes everything except
    letters/digits and uppercases the rest --- so "NILAI 5 - EA", "NILAI
    5-EA AY26-27", and "Nilai 5 - EA" all resolve to the same key,
    tolerating spacing/dash/suffix differences between the Sheet's
    `Class Name` column and however Google Classroom actually names the
    course. `getWhatsAppLinksMap_()` reads the sheet into
    `{ normalizedKey: url }`, skipping any row with a blank name or
    blank link.
-   **Applied fresh at request time, not baked into the 15-minute sync
    cache**: `applyWhatsAppLinks_(courses)` runs inside
    `getDashboardData()` right after
    `applyStudentOnboardedFlag_(courses)`, stamping `c.whatsappLink`
    (`''` if no link is on file) onto every course --- mirroring the
    `applyLivePresence_` pattern (computed live) rather than
    `buildCourseRecord_`'s pattern (computed once per Classroom sync).
    This means an admin's edit to the Sheet shows up on the very next
    1-minute dashboard poll, not after the next 15-minute sync or a
    "Force Sync Now" click.
-   **Rendering**: `renderWhatsAppLink(url)` in `Dashboard.html` --- an
    inline WhatsApp SVG glyph (brand green `#25D366`) + **"Join to
    WhatsApp"** text (changed from "Join WhatsApp Group" in the eleventh
    round), inside the card's `.card-footer-links` wrapper alongside
    "Open in Classroom →" (grouped together so they wrap as a unit on
    narrow cards). Omitted entirely when `c.whatsappLink` is `''`.
-   **One class has no link on file**: "NILAI 6 - LA" had a blank link
    in the school's original list, so it has no WhatsApp button until a
    link is added to that row in the Sheet.
-   **To add/change a link going forward**: edit the
    `WhatsApp_Group_Links` Sheet tab directly (column C for the link,
    column A for the class name) --- no code edit, no redeploy; the
    change shows up on the next dashboard poll (≤ 1 minute).

## Setup / re-setup steps

1.  Paste `Code.gs` and `Dashboard.html` into the Apps Script project,
    replacing the existing files.
2.  Run `syncClassroomData` once manually from the editor (authorize if
    prompted) to confirm data lands in the "Courses" tab --- note the
    column layout (see above), so if any external tool/report reads this
    sheet by column letter, re-check it.
3.  Run `createSyncTrigger` once --- it deletes any existing
    `syncClassroomData` trigger first, so it's safe to re-run whenever
    `SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES` changes.
4.  **Deployment access must be "Anyone within the organization"**, not
    public "Anyone" --- otherwise role-based access (and the
    status-flow/chat/presence permission checks) can't tell who's
    viewing, and everyone is treated as unrecognized.
5.  Redeploy the web app (Deploy → Manage deployments → new version) so
    the dashboard picks up HTML/Code.gs changes.
6.  Open the dashboard and use "Force Sync Now" to verify end-to-end,
    including the red error banner if the sync fails (surfaces
    `getLastSyncError()`). Also verify the signed-in badge shows the
    expected name and role for a few different test accounts (an admin
    email, a teacher email, a student email), and that each sees only
    the buttons they're allowed to click on "Teacher NOT in Class" /
    "Needs Tech Support".
