7.  Test the notification email: as a test student/teacher account,
    click "Need Tech Support in Google Class" or "Teacher NOT in Class"
    (the `none → reported` step) and confirm an email lands in the
    `ADMIN_EMAILS` inboxes, and that the resulting badge shows "by
    `<your name>` · `<time>`" on the card.
8.  Test chat: post a message as one test student/teacher account,
    confirm it appears (within \~8s) for another test account's open
    panel with that student's name AND class name in the meta line, and
    confirm a `Dashboard_Chat_Window` tab appeared in the spreadsheet
    with that row (6 columns, `Class Name` last).
9.  **Test each full 3-stage round trip** (this class of bug broke once
    already --- see "Bugs fixed" below): as a student, click "Teacher
    NOT in Class" (→ `reported`); as staff, click "Tech Team talking
    with Teacher" (→ `in_progress`); as the teacher, click "Teacher
    Returned to Class" (→ `none`). Confirm the card's label/badge and
    "by `<name>`" caption actually update at each step (not just that a
    toast appears), both immediately and after a fresh page load, and
    open the "Courses" sheet tab directly to confirm the "Teacher NOT In
    Class Stage" column for that row reads the expected stage string at
    each step. Repeat for "Need Tech Support in Google Class" → "Teach
    Team will Join to your Classroom" → "Tech issue is been Resolved"
    (all three "Needs Tech Support" steps are staff-only past the
    initial report).
10. To confirm "Teacher in Class" auto-detection is actually working:
    have a teacher open their Classroom, click "Force Sync Now", and
    check whether that course's badge changes. If it never does (and
    sync itself succeeds with no error banner), the domain's Workspace
    edition likely doesn't have Classroom audit logging enabled, or the
    log's course-id parameter name differs from `COURSE_ID_LOG_PARAM`
    --- check the Apps Script execution log for the raw Reports API
    response to diagnose.
11. Test the online presence dot: have a test student/teacher account
    open the dashboard and confirm their own avatar shows a green dot
    within one load (real-time heartbeat); leaving the dashboard closed
    for longer than `PRESENCE_ONLINE_WINDOW_MINUTES` should turn it off
    again on the next viewer's load.
12. Test 10-day chat retention: `pruneOldChatMessages_()` is throttled
    to run at most every `CHAT_PRUNE_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` (6h default), so
    to verify it sooner, either temporarily lower that constant or
    manually run `pruneOldChatMessages_` from the Apps Script editor
    after backdating a test row's Timestamp cell to more than 10 days
    ago.
13. Test the Student Onboarding Status page as an admin/headmaster
    account: confirm the table groups by NILAI/grade + time exactly
    matching the real course Name/Section values, that the
    grade/day/student-name filters actually narrow the table and update
    the six summary cards, that the "Total Students" card and footer row
    match the filtered rows, and that "Students Online"/"Teachers
    Online" move when a test account's online status toggles. Also
    confirm a student's Status badge moves from Pending →
    Onboarding/Completed the first time they're detected online, and
    never moves back to Pending afterward even once they go offline.
    **If the school's real course Name/Section don't cleanly separate
    into "grade" and "time"** (e.g. both are combined in the Name), the
    grouping will need `buildOnboardingGroups()` in `Dashboard.html`
    adjusted to parse them out instead of reading `c.name` / `c.section`
    directly.
14. **Enable the "Admin Directory API" advanced service** (Apps Script
    Editor → Services → click "+" → find "Admin Directory API" → Add),
    needed for the signed-in badge to show an admin/headmaster's real
    Google profile name instead of falling back to "Admin ·
    email-prefix" / "Headmaster · email-prefix". This is separate from
    the "Admin Reports API" service already used for Meet/Classroom
    detection --- both need to be added independently. Skipping this
    step doesn't break anything; the badge just falls back
    automatically.
15. Test the role-gated UI: sign in as an admin, a headmaster, a
    teacher, and a student, and confirm (a) the signed-in badge reads
    "`<Google Profile Name>` (`<ROLE>`)" for each --- with the real name
    for admin/headmaster once step 14 is done --- and never visually
    overlaps the header action buttons at any window width; (b) "Force
    Sync Now" is visible for admin/headmaster only and hidden for
    teacher/student; (c) "Open in Classroom →" on a course card is
    visible for Admin only --- hidden even for Headmaster.
16. **Test the fifth-round layout on a narrow/mobile width** (resize the
    browser or use a phone): confirm the header action buttons wrap onto
    their own row(s) without ever sitting under the signed-in badge; the
    onboarding filter bar wraps to full-width controls; the table
    becomes horizontally scrollable if needed instead of squeezing text
    unreadably small; and the floating chat button never visually sits
    on top of the footer text or the last visible table row.
17. **Test the WhatsApp join link**: open the `WhatsApp_Group_Links`
    sheet tab and confirm it's populated (production already has \~194
    rows). Sign in as a student, teacher, and admin and confirm each
    sees the same "Join to WhatsApp" button (with the WhatsApp glyph) on
    a class card that has a link on file, and that it actually opens the
    right WhatsApp group. Edit one row's link in the Sheet, reload the
    dashboard within a minute, and confirm the card now points at the
    new link --- no redeploy needed. Confirm `Code.gs` no longer
    contains any hardcoded WhatsApp links (search for
    `chat.whatsapp.com` --- it should not appear in the source at all,
    only in the Sheet).
18. **Test the twelfth/thirteenth-round Last Activity feature**: as a
    test student/teacher account, load the dashboard and confirm their
    own roster chip shows `MM/DD HH:mm (DB)` under their avatar (Eastern
    time --- check it matches the current Eastern clock time, not the
    tester's own local time if different). Have that same account join a
    real Google Meet call, run (or wait for) a sync, and confirm the
    label updates to include `GM` (e.g. `(GM/DB)` or, if Classroom
    activity is also on file, `(GC/GM/DB)`) with the displayed TIMESTAMP
    equal to whichever of the applicable sources is actually newest.
    Separately have them use Google Classroom (with no Meet activity)
    and confirm `GC` appears instead. Confirm the combined source list
    always renders in `GC/GM/DB` order regardless of which source
    triggered the update. Manually inspect the `lastLoginMap` Script
    Property (Apps Script Editor → Project Settings → Script Properties,
    or log it from a temporary test function) to confirm it holds one
    `{ gc, gm, db }` entry per person and that each present slot only
    ever moves forward, independently of the other two. Confirm a person
    who has never been seen by any of the three sources shows no Last
    Activity text at all (not a fabricated value).
19. **Test the thirteenth-round Dashboard sign-off**: open the dashboard
    as a test account, note the current time, then close the tab (or
    switch to another tab/app so the page becomes hidden) rather than
    leaving it open. Reload the dashboard (as any viewer with visibility
    into that account, e.g. an admin) and confirm that account's `DB`
    timestamp reflects roughly the moment the tab was closed/hidden, not
    up to 60 seconds earlier. Repeat by switching away and back to the
    same tab WITHOUT closing it, then actually closing it later, to
    confirm a sign-off is still sent on the real close (this exercises
    the `visibilitychange` "came back" reset in `Dashboard.html`). This
    is inherently best-effort --- an instantly-killed browser process
    may still miss it --- so treat "usually within a second or two of
    closing, worst case \~60s stale" as the expected result, not an
    exact guarantee.

## Bugs fixed

**Sept 2026, initial**: The dashboard was never loading data at all:
`Dashboard.html`'s script wired click handlers to `#forceSync` and
`#refresh` buttons that were commented out of the HTML.
`document.getElementById(...)` returned `null`, and calling
`.addEventListener` on `null` threw an uncaught error --- which halted
the rest of the script, so the final `load()`/`loadSyncInfo()` calls
never ran. Fixed by restoring both buttons in the HTML so the IDs
resolve. The same class of bug also existed in `loadSyncInfo()`'s
`getCacheSheetUrl()` handler (referencing a commented-out `#sheetLink`
element) --- that one didn't halt anything since it's inside its own
callback, but was made defensive (`if (url && link)`) once the
dashboard's poll interval was shortened to run much more often.

**Sept 2026, stale flag status**: A student reported "Teacher NOT in
Class"; staff clicked to resolve it; the click succeeded with no error,
but the dashboard kept showing the class as flagged. Root cause: the
row-patch functions all located the Sheet row to patch with
`data[i][0] === courseId` --- a strict-equality comparison between a raw
Sheet cell value and the course ID string. Classroom course IDs are long
digit-only strings, and Google Sheets can silently store that cell as a
**Number** rather than text; `Number !== String` under `===`, so the
comparison quietly never matched, the row-patch loop's `break` never
ran, and the Sheet's actual status column / Detail JSON were never
updated --- even though the separate Script Properties map (used only as
a secondary cache) *did* update, and the click returned successfully.
The only thing that ever fixed the visible status was the next full
`syncClassroomData()` run, which rebuilds each row from scratch and
reads that Properties map correctly (object-key lookups always coerce to
string, unlike `===`). Fixed two ways: (1) `writeCache_()` now
explicitly formats the Course ID column as plain text
(`setNumberFormat('@')`) before writing, so Sheets can no longer
reinterpret it as a Number; (2) all row-lookups now compare
`String(data[i][0]) === String(courseId)` regardless, so this can't
silently regress even if the formatting fix is ever undone (e.g. someone
clears formatting on that column by hand). Also added a confirmation
toast (see "Dashboard UI features") so a successful status change is
never ambiguous even when the card leaves the current filtered view.

## Design history: from boolean flags to a 3-stage status flow

The original design for "Teacher NOT in Class" and "Needs Tech Support"
was a simple on/off flag per course (`teacherNotInClass` /
`needsTechSupport` booleans, functions
`setTeacherNotInClassStatus(courseId, flagged)` /
`setNeedsTechSupportStatus(courseId, flagged)`). This was replaced (Sept
2026) with the 3-stage cycle documented above (`teacherNotInClassStage`
/ `needsTechSupportStage`, functions
`setTeacherNotInClassStage(courseId, targetStage)` /
`setNeedsTechSupportStage(courseId, targetStage)`) so the dashboard
could show an explicit "someone is actively handling this" middle state
--- e.g. "Tech Team talking with Teacher" --- rather than jumping
straight from "reported" to "resolved" with no visibility into whether
anyone had picked it up yet. The Sheet column positions were kept the
same (renamed to "...Stage" and now holding a stage string instead of
`TRUE`/`FALSE`) specifically to avoid disturbing the Detail JSON column
or anything else that might read this sheet by position.
`normalizeStageEntry_()` in `Code.gs` transparently upgrades any
leftover `{flagged}`-shaped Script Properties data from before this
change.

## Sept 2026, fifth round: Student Onboarding Status page redesign (Google Workspace admin style)

A full visual redesign of the Student Onboarding Status page, following
a detailed design brief, with three clarifications resolved up front
(via user choice) before implementation: - **No screenshot was
available** --- built purely from the written spec. - **Per-class
Headmaster column dropped** --- no per-class headmaster mapping exists
today (headmasters currently see every class equally, not one assigned
class each), so the previously-requested "HEADMASTER" column was left
out of this round rather than inventing a mapping. The table is 5
columns (Class/Section, Day & Time, Teacher, Students, Status), not 6. -
**"Onboarded" defined as**: a student is marked onboarded the FIRST TIME
they are EVER seen online by any presence signal (dashboard heartbeat,
Meet, or Classroom activity), tracked PERMANENTLY --- never reset when
they go offline. See "Permanent student 'onboarded' status" above. This
was chosen over inventing a multi-stage manual pipeline (no such
pipeline data exists anywhere in Classroom or the Sheet).

Changes, by area: 1. **New permanent onboarding tracking** ---
`ONBOARDED_STUDENTS_PROP_KEY` Script Property +
`applyStudentOnboardedFlag_()` in `Code.gs`, called from
`getDashboardData()` right after `applyLivePresence_()`. Two new
lightweight getters, `getCourseNameSuffix()` and
`getShowContactPhone()`, expose existing server-side constants to the
client (mirroring the existing `getSyncIntervalMinutes()` pattern) so
the redesigned page can display the "AY26-27" suffix and respect the
phone-number visibility setting without duplicating those constants
client-side. 2. **Header restructure** --- the signed-in badge is no
longer `position: fixed`; it now lives inline beside the title in a new
`.app-header-top` row, with the action buttons
(Calendar/Syllabus/Zoom/Raise Ticket) in their own `.app-header-actions`
row below --- guaranteeing they can never overlap at any screen width. A
school logo (fetched from the public website) was added beside the
title. 3. **Tabs** restyled from filled pills to a Google-style
underline (gray text, blue text + blue underline when active). 4. **Six
summary cards** (`.onboarding-summary`) replace the old two-chip
"Students Online"/"Teachers Online" pair: Total Students, Students
Online, Teachers Online, Students Assigned, Students Pending, Students
Not Onboarded --- see "Student Onboarding Status page" above for exact
definitions, especially the deliberate distinction between "Students
Pending" (class-level) and "Students Not Onboarded" (student-level). 5.
**New student-name search filter** added to the onboarding page's filter
bar (`#onboardingStudentSearch`), live-filtering as you type, alongside
the existing grade/day filters and "Clear Filters". 6. **Table
redesign** --- 5 columns (Class/Section, Day & Time, Teacher, Students,
Status), sticky header, capped-height scrollable body
(`max-height: 56vh`) instead of letting the page grow tall, a blue "N
Students" badge instead of a bare number, and 5 color-coded Status
badges driven by the new `computeGroupStatus()`. 7. **Footer** --- "©
Avvaiyar Padasalai \| World's First Online Tamil School" (this exact
wording, per the school's request --- note this differs slightly from
the tagline on the live site, "World's First Virtual Tamil School"). 8.
**Floating chat button** --- position unchanged (bottom-right), but body
bottom padding was increased so it never visually sits on top of the
footer or the last table row once scrolled to the bottom of the page. 9.
**Assumptions flagged for follow-up**: the school's exact brand hex
color code could not be extracted from the live website (page-fetching
returns rendered text, not CSS), so the dashboard's existing
`--blue: #1a73e8` (Google blue) was kept as the closest reasonable
stand-in; the logo image was inferred from "refer the school website for
image/logo" rather than an explicit instruction to add one.

## Sept 2026, sixth round: Knowledge Base -- Videos tab (role-gating superseded eighth round --- see below)

Added a third tab, "Knowledge Base -- Videos", next to "Classes" and
"Student Onboarding Status" (`#tabKb`, toggled via the same
`switchView()` used by the other two tabs). Purpose: give teachers a
library of embedded training/reference videos (Google Classroom, Google
Meet, student onboarding, teacher training, APS procedures) without ever
leaving the dashboard or being redirected to youtube.com.

**Role-gating (Teacher/Admin/Headmaster only, Student never sees it)**
--- gated the same "client hides it, server actually withholds the data"
way as everything else in this app: - `Dashboard.html`:
`updateKbTabVisibility()` (called from `load()`'s success handler,
alongside `updateForceSyncVisibility()`) hides `#tabKb` for role
`student`/`none`, and snaps a viewer back to the Classes tab if their
role changes to a hidden one while the KB tab happens to be open. The
tab starts `display:none` in the raw HTML too, same convention as
`#forceSync`. - `Code.gs`: `getKnowledgeBaseVideos()` re-checks the
viewer's role and returns an **empty array** for student/none --- the
video catalog itself is never sent to a browser that shouldn't see it,
not just hidden by CSS.

**Video catalog** --- a new hardcoded array, `KNOWLEDGE_BASE_VIDEOS` in
`Code.gs` (same "edit the constant, redeploy" pattern as
`ADMIN_EMAILS`/`HIDDEN_TEACHER_NAMES`/etc. --- see "Key configuration"),
each entry `{ videoId, title, description, category, audience }`.
`videoId` is the bare YouTube ID (the part after `v=` or after
`youtu.be/`), never a full watch/share URL. `audience` (`Teachers` \|
`Students` \| `Teachers & Students`) is **display-only metadata** --- it
helps a teacher spot "here's what to forward to my students" content, it
does NOT grant students access; the whole tab stays teacher/staff-only
regardless of a video's tagged audience. Currently seeded with 9 videos
across 5 categories (Student Onboarding, Google Classroom, Google Meet,
Teacher Training, APS Procedures) from the videos the school provided. -
**One data quality note carried over from the source material**: the
school's message listed video ID `-1cB0TOnbQc` twice with two different
titles/descriptions --- once as a Student-audience "how to submit
homework" video, once as a Teacher-audience "how teachers use Google
Account/Classroom" video. Since it's the same YouTube ID, only one
catalog entry was created (using the homework-submission
title/description, since that was the more detailed of the two) ---
**this should be confirmed with the school**; if the teacher-specific
video is actually a different link, update that entry's `videoId` in
`KNOWLEDGE_BASE_VIDEOS`. - **Moving this to a Sheet later**: if the
school wants to add/edit videos without a code redeploy, this array is
the one place that would move to a Sheet-backed catalog (mirrors the
"in-dashboard settings panel" idea suggested for other hardcoded config)
--- not built now since no such request was made this round. (The
WhatsApp link lookup DID get this treatment in the tenth round --- see
"WhatsApp join links on class cards" above --- as a possible template if
this ever comes up for the video catalog too.)

**Client fetch**: `loadKnowledgeBase()` calls `getKnowledgeBaseVideos()`
**lazily**, only the first time the tab is opened (cached in the
`kbVideos` client variable) --- not on every 1-minute dashboard poll,
since the catalog is static reference content, not live data. Re-opening
the tab later just re-renders from the cached array.

**Search/filter bar** (`.kb-filters`): a live search box (`#kbSearch`,
matches against title + description) and a category `<select>`
(`#kbCategoryFilter`, options populated dynamically from whatever
categories are actually present via `populateKbCategoryOptions()` ---
same dynamic-options pattern as the onboarding page's grade/day
filters), both feeding `renderKnowledgeBase()`.

**Video cards** (`.kb-grid`, `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(340px, 1fr))` ---
same responsive-grid idiom as the Classes view's course-card grid, so
it's naturally 2-up on desktop and collapses to 1-up on narrow screens
with no extra media query needed): each card shows a title ("🎥" +
title), description, and two small tag chips ("Category: ...",
"Audience: ..."), matching the requested card layout.

**Click-to-load embedding (never auto-loads or auto-plays)** --- this
was an explicit requirement ("Do not automatically play videos... Only
load/play the video when the teacher chooses to play it"), so
`renderVideoCard()` never renders a live `<iframe>` up front. Instead
each card shows a static YouTube thumbnail
(`https://img.youtube.com/vi/<id>/hqdefault.jpg`) with a play-button
overlay; a single delegated click listener on `#kbGrid` replaces that
one card's thumbnail with a real
`https://www.youtube.com/embed/<id>?rel=0` iframe **only when clicked**,
and only for that card (other cards on the page stay as thumbnails). The
embed iframe intentionally omits `autoplay=1` --- a click loads the
YouTube player paused, showing YouTube's own native play button, so
actual playback still requires a second, unambiguous click on the player
itself. This means zero videos ever load or play without a deliberate
teacher click, and the page never opens or redirects to youtube.com ---
everything happens inside the dashboard.

**Quick links**: a small `.kb-quicklinks` row at the top of the tab
links out to the real Google Classroom (`https://classroom.google.com/`)
and Google Meet (`https://meet.google.com/`) apps (`target="_blank"`,
since these are full product UIs teachers need to actually work in, not
embeddable reference content --- unlike the training videos, redirecting
here is expected and fine).

**Layout/placement**: sits as its own view `<div id="kbView">`, sibling
to `#classesView`/`#onboardingView`, so it inherits the shared
`<footer>` and the page's existing bottom padding (110px) that already
keeps the floating chat button off the footer/last-row content --- no
new spacing rules were needed for this tab specifically.

## Sept 2026, seventh round: dashboard chat widget usability fixes

Three small, purely presentational fixes to the shared dashboard chat
panel (`.chat-panel` in `Dashboard.html`) --- no server-side change, no
new data:

1.  **Chat input no longer overlaps the floating chat button.** The
    compose box (`.chat-compose`, holding the textarea + Send button)
    used to sit flush against the very bottom of the chat panel --- the
    same screen position where the floating `.chat-toggle-btn` (52px,
    20px from the bottom edge, so its top edge sits 72px up) is fixed,
    and the button's `z-index: 95` is higher than the panel's `90`, so
    it visually sat on top of the input. Fixed by giving `.chat-compose`
    a `margin-bottom: 100px` --- leaves the button's fixed footprint
    plus a \~28px visible gap (within the requested 20--24px+ minimum)
    below the input at all times. Since the button's position/size don't
    change per screen width, this one fixed reservation works the same
    on desktop, tablet, and mobile without needing separate
    per-breakpoint values.
2.  **New chat footer note** --- a small `.chat-footnote` strip ("APS
    Tech Support • Please raise a Service Request for technical

    this hyperlink wasn't explicitly requested but was a natural,
    low-risk addition since the URL already exists elsewhere in the app;
    it opens in a new tab like the header link does.
3.  **No other layout changed** --- the panel's slide-in behavior,
    message rendering, polling, and the floating button's own
    position/visibility logic (`updateChatVisibility()`) are all
    unchanged. The button's z-index and the panel's overall structure
    already satisfied the "must stay above dashboard content, never
    cover it" requirement from earlier rounds (via the page's existing
    110px bottom body padding), so nothing needed to change there.

## Sept 2026, ninth round: announcements marquee above the footer, header title/accreditation update

Two unrelated presentational changes to `Dashboard.html`, both
HTML/CSS-only (no `Code.gs` change, no new server data):

**1. Animated announcements marquee.** A new `.marquee-section` sits
directly above `<footer class="app-footer">`, shared across all three
tabs (Classes / Student Onboarding Status / Knowledge Base --- Videos)
exactly like the footer already is, since it lives right next to it in
the markup rather than inside any one view. It shows the school's 13
supplied Tamil announcement messages scrolling continuously
right-to-left, separated by a `✦` glyph, message 13 ending in a real
hyperlink to `https://www.avvaiyarpadasalai.org`. - **Seamless CSS-only
loop, no `<marquee>` tag, no JS animation loop**: `.marquee-track`
renders the same sequence of 13 messages **twice** (two `.marquee-group`
blocks --- the second `aria-hidden="true"` and its link `tabindex="-1"`,
so assistive tech and tab order only ever see the messages once) inside
a fixed-height, `overflow:hidden` `.marquee-viewport`. A single
`@keyframes marquee-scroll` animates `transform` from `translateX(0)` to
`translateX(-50%)` on `infinite linear` --- since both halves are
identical, the moment the first copy scrolls fully out of view the
second copy is already in exactly the same position, so the loop has no
visible jump or blank gap. - **Pause on hover/focus** --- pure CSS, no
JS: `.marquee-section:hover .marquee-track` and
`:focus-within .marquee-track` set `animation-play-state: paused`,
resuming automatically on mouse-leave/blur. -
**`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`** --- the keyframe animation is
disabled AND the track is switched to `flex-wrap: wrap` (a static, fully
readable wrapped block) with the duplicate `aria-hidden` group hidden
entirely, so reduced-motion users get all 13 messages readable at once
rather than a frozen half-scrolled strip. - **No horizontal page
scroll**: both `.marquee-section` and the inner `.marquee-viewport` have
`overflow: hidden`, containing the oversized `width: max-content` track
so it can never expand the page's own scrollable area, including on
mobile. - **Mobile**: a `max-width: 640px` override reduces font size
and gap slightly while keeping the same smooth-scroll behavior. -
**Styling**: APS-blue-based gradient background, rounded corners, soft
shadow, generous padding --- designed as a premium information strip
rather than an old-style ticker, per the school's brief. Tamil text uses
the `Noto Sans Tamil` webfont (Google Fonts `<link>` tags added to
`<head>`, scoped only to `.marquee-item`/`.marquee-sep` so it doesn't
change any other text in the app). - **Placement**: inserted between the
last view (`#kbView`) and the existing `<footer class="app-footer">`,
with margin so it never touches the footer, and it sits above the app's
existing 110px bottom body padding that already keeps the floating chat
button clear of footer-level content --- so the chat button still never
overlaps it. - **Speed**: originally 120s per loop; slowed to **170s**
in the tenth round. - **Assumption flagged to the school**: the request
said "at the very bottom of the website" --- since this Claude session
only has file/device access to this dashboard
(`Dashboard.html`/`Code.gs`), not the public marketing site at
`www.avvaiyarpadasalai.org`, and the brief explicitly cross-referenced
"any floating chat/support button" (which only exists in this
dashboard), the marquee was built into `Dashboard.html` just above its
footer. If the intent was actually the public website instead, that's a
separate, unrelated file this session cannot reach.

**2. Header title and accreditation line.** The `<h1>` changed from "APS
Tamil Virtual School --- Classroom Dashboard" to "Avvaiyar Padasalai
Tamil Virtual School --- Classroom Dashboard". A new line was added
directly beneath it (above the existing sync-status subtitle line): "A
registered 501(c)(3) non-profit public charity, run entirely by
volunteers. Fully accredited by WASC, California, USA." --- styled as a
small, muted `.brand-accreditation` line, matching the visual weight of
the existing `.subtitle` line beneath it.

-   **Storage --- a separate, live-editable Sheet tab**, not a hardcoded
    array. `getOrCreateWhatsAppLinksSheet_()` in `Code.gs` creates
    (once) a `WhatsApp_Group_Links` tab in the same workbook as
    "Courses" and "Dashboard_Chat_Window", with columns
    `Class Name | Schedule (reference only) | WhatsApp Group Link`. Only
    columns A and C are read by code; column B is a free-text note for
    humans (e.g. "FRI 6:30 - 8:00 PM EST") purely so an admin editing
    the sheet can tell classes apart --- it's never parsed. **This was a
    deliberate choice this round**: the school asked to "keep this
    WhatsApp join link file as separate lookup file and update link
    whenever needed" --- i.e. editable without a code change or
    redeploy, unlike `KNOWLEDGE_BASE_VIDEOS` (which stays a hardcoded
    array you edit + redeploy). `WHATSAPP_LINKS_SEED` (an array of
    `[className, url]` pairs, seeded from the school's initial list of
    194 class → WhatsApp-group mappings) was used **only once**, to
    populate the tab the first time it was created --- after that, the
    Sheet became the sole source of truth, and re-running the seed logic
    never happened again (the function only wrote the seed rows in the
    `!sheet` branch). **This seed array was fully removed from `Code.gs`
    in the eleventh round** --- see below.
-   **Matching**: `normalizeClassKey_(name)` strips the trailing
    `COURSE_NAME_SUFFIX` (e.g. "AY26-27") if present, then removes every
    non-alphanumeric character and uppercases what's left --- so "NILAI
    5 - EA", "NILAI 5-EA AY26-27", and "Nilai 5 - EA" all normalize to
    the same key, tolerating spacing/dash/suffix differences between the
    Sheet's `Class Name` column and however Google Classroom actually
    stores the course's Name field. `getWhatsAppLinksMap_()` reads the
    sheet (skipping the header row, skipping any row with a blank name
    or blank link) into `{ normalizedKey: url }`.
-   **Applied fresh on every request, not baked into the 15-minute sync
    cache**: `applyWhatsAppLinks_(courses)` --- a new step in
    `getDashboardData()`, run right after
    `applyStudentOnboardedFlag_(courses)` --- stamps `c.whatsappLink`
    (possibly `''`) onto every course by looking up its normalized name
    in the map. This mirrors the `applyLivePresence_` pattern (computed
    at read time) rather than the `buildCourseRecord_` pattern (computed
    once per Classroom sync and cached in the Sheet's Detail JSON)
    specifically so an admin's edit to the `WhatsApp_Group_Links` tab
    shows up on the very next 1-minute dashboard poll, without needing
    to wait for the next Classroom sync or click "Force Sync Now".
-   **One class from the school's original list has no link on file
    yet**: "NILAI 6 - LA" (the source spreadsheet's cell was blank) ---
    that card simply shows no WhatsApp button until a link is added to
    the Sheet row.
-   **Rendering (label since changed --- see eleventh round)**:
    `renderWhatsAppLink(url)` in `Dashboard.html` builds a small
    `<a class="whatsapp-link">` with an inline WhatsApp SVG glyph (brand
    green `#25D366`) + text, `target="_blank" rel="noopener"`. It sits
    in a new `.card-footer-links` wrapper alongside the (still
    Google Classroom icon link, grouped together so they
    wrap as a unit on narrow cards instead of the old
    `justify-content: space-between` spreading two-vs-three items
    unevenly.

**2. Marquee speed slowed down.** The announcements marquee's scroll
duration (`@keyframes marquee-scroll`, `.marquee-track`'s `animation`)
was changed from 120s to **170s** per one full loop --- same
seamless-loop/pause-on-hover/reduced-motion behavior as the ninth round,
just slower.

Two small follow-ups to the tenth round's WhatsApp feature, both
confirmed with the school before making the change (the
`WhatsApp_Group_Links` sheet was confirmed already populated in
production, so it was safe to drop the seed):

1.  **`WHATSAPP_LINKS_SEED` deleted from `Code.gs` entirely.** It was

    tab (used exactly once, in the `!sheet` branch of
    `getOrCreateWhatsAppLinksSheet_()`, the very first time the tab
    didn't exist). Since that sheet is now fully populated and is the

    `getOrCreateWhatsAppLinksSheet_()` now creates a fresh tab with just

2.  **Button label changed from "Join WhatsApp Group" to "Join to
    WhatsApp"** in `renderWhatsAppLink()` in `Dashboard.html` --- same

Nothing else about the feature changed: the Sheet
(`WhatsApp_Group_Links`, columns

## Sept 2026, twelfth round: unified, permanent "Last Login" tracking across Classroom, Meet, and Dashboard

**Why the previous behavior only ever reflected Dashboard activity**:
before this round, the only per-person "login time" the dashboard
displayed was `onlineSince` (see "Live online presence"), and ---
critically --- it was only ever *shown* while `online` was `true`.
Although `onlineSince` already blended in Meet/Classroom-derived
timestamps when those were the most recent *online* signal, the moment a
person's online window expired (they closed the dashboard, their Meet
call ended, or their Classroom activity aged out of
`CLASSROOM_ACTIVE_WINDOW_MINUTES`), the label disappeared entirely ---
there was no durable record of "the last time this person was seen, from
any source." That's why it read as "only updates on Dashboard login": a
Dashboard heartbeat was the only source that both updated frequently
(every 1-minute poll) and was visible for a reasonably long window
(`PRESENCE_ONLINE_WINDOW_MINUTES`), so in practice it dominated what
anyone actually saw.

**What changed**: a brand-new, permanent, cross-source Last Login record
was added (see "Cross-source 'Last Login' tracking (Classroom / Meet /
Dashboard)" above for the full design) that: 1. Independently tracks the
single latest timestamp from each of Google Classroom activity, Google
Meet activity, and Dashboard visits. 2. Compares all three and keeps
only the most recent, labeling it `(GS)` for Classroom/Meet or `(DB)`
for Dashboard. 3. Never moves backward --- an older signal from any
source can never overwrite a newer one already on record, regardless of
source. 4. Displays permanently (not just while the person is currently
"online") as `MM/DD HH:mm (GS)` / `MM/DD HH:mm (DB)`, always in US
Eastern time regardless of the viewer's own timezone. 5. Shows nothing
(no fabricated timestamp) for a person who has never been seen by any of
the three sources.

**Exact changes made**: - `Code.gs`: added `LAST_LOGIN_PROP_KEY` /
`LAST_LOGIN_TIMEZONE` constants; added `mergeLastLoginActivity_()`,
`getLastLoginMap_()`, `formatLastLoginTimestamp_()`, and
`applyLastLogin_()`; added a small side effect to the end of
`getClassroomActivityMap_()` and `getMeetPresenceMap_()` (each merges
its own per-person latest timestamp into the new record --- no new API
calls); added a few lines to `recordHeartbeat_()` to merge in the
Dashboard visit; added one line to `getDashboardData()` calling
`applyLastLogin_(courses)`. No existing function's return shape, the
Sheet's column layout, the CRM/role-based access logic, the "Teacher NOT
in Class"/"Needs Tech Support" flows, chat, WhatsApp links, or the
Knowledge Base tab were touched. - `Dashboard.html`: `renderPeople()`
now reads `p.lastLoginDisplay` (instead of computing
`formatLoginTime(p.onlineSince)`) for the `.login-time` label under each
avatar, and shows it whenever it's non-empty rather than only while
`p.online` is true. `formatLoginTime()` itself is untouched and still
used, unchanged, for the "who clicked / when" status-flow captions
(`renderStatusBadgeGroup()`) --- those intentionally continue to show
the *viewer's own local* time, since they're a different feature (an
audit trail of admin/staff actions, not a login record) and the user's
requirements were scoped to the login-activity field specifically. - No
spreadsheet columns were added or reordered, no existing Script
Properties keys were renamed or repurposed, and no
CRM/Classroom-sync/role-filtering logic was changed.

**New Advanced Google Services / Google Cloud APIs required**: none
beyond what `AUTO_LIVE_DETECTION` and
`AUTO_CLASSROOM_PRESENCE_DETECTION` already needed (the Admin SDK
Reports API via the `AdminReports` advanced service) --- this feature is
additive logic on data those two already fetch, plus the pre-existing
Dashboard heartbeat.

**New OAuth scopes required**: none --- same reasoning as above; no new
API surface is called.

**Google Classroom / Google Meet API limitations** (also documented
above): neither the Classroom API nor the Meet API expose a literal
"last login" or "last sign-in" timestamp for a user. This implementation
therefore uses the most reliable available proxy for each --- the Admin
Reports API's Classroom application audit log for Classroom, and its
Meet application audit log for Meet --- both of which are the exact same
feeds `AUTO_CLASSROOM_PRESENCE_DETECTION` and `AUTO_LIVE_DETECTION`
already relied on, so no fabricated or invented timestamp is ever
introduced; if a source has no data (feature disabled, API unauthorized,
or the domain's Workspace edition doesn't collect that audit log), it
simply contributes nothing and the other sources' data (or a blank Last
Login) stands.

**Exactly how `(GS)` and `(DB)` are calculated, end to end**: each of
the three sources --- `getClassroomActivityMap_()`,
`getMeetPresenceMap_()`, `recordHeartbeat_()` --- independently computes
its own latest-known timestamp for a person and calls
`mergeLastLoginActivity_(candidates, source)`, which loads the single
shared `lastLoginMap` Script Property, and for each person only replaces
the stored `{ ts, source }` if the new timestamp is strictly newer.
Because this happens independently every time any of the three sources
runs (Classroom/Meet on every `syncClassroomData()`, Dashboard on every
`getDashboardData()`), the map converges to "the single most recent
activity timestamp from any source, and which source it came from"
without ever needing to compare all three at once --- the comparison
happens incrementally, one candidate at a time, against whatever is
currently stored, which is mathematically equivalent to comparing all
three simultaneously since only the maximum survives at any point.
`applyLastLogin_()` then simply reads that already-computed
`{ ts, source }` per person and formats it as `MM/DD HH:mm (GS)` or
`MM/DD HH:mm (DB)` in Eastern time for display --- no comparison logic
happens at read/render time at all.

## Sept 2026, thirteenth round: split "Last Login" into three independent sources (GC/GM/DB), combined multi-source display, and Dashboard sign-off tracking

**Why this round happened**: the twelfth round's single `(GS)` label
correctly captured "some Google-side activity happened" but couldn't
distinguish Classroom from Meet, and displayed only ONE source code even
when a person had recorded activity from more than one place --- the
school's actual requirement is to show every applicable source
(e.g. `GC/GM/DB` together when all three have activity), always in a
fixed `GC/GM/DB` order, with Meet specifically labeled `GM` (never `GC`)
so the two are never confused. The school also wanted an explicit
Dashboard "sign-off" moment recorded, not only sign-on/poll activity.

**Exact changes made** (all additive/refactoring of the twelfth round's
own mechanism --- no unrelated functionality touched): - `Code.gs`: -
`LAST_LOGIN_PROP_KEY`'s stored shape changed from
`{ ts, source: 'GS'|'DB' }` per person to `{ gc, gm, db }` per person
(each an ISO UTC string or absent) --- three independent slots instead
of one merged value. Added `LAST_LOGIN_SOURCE_ORDER`
(`['gc','gm','db']`) and `LAST_LOGIN_SOURCE_LABELS`
(`{gc:'GC', gm:'GM', db:'DB'}`) as named constants for the fixed display
order/labels. - Added `normalizeLastLoginEntry_(entry)` --- reads either
the new `{gc,gm,db}` shape or the old twelfth-round `{ts,source}` shape
and returns a normalized `{gc,gm,db}` object, migrating an old `'DB'`
entry (unambiguous) into `{db: ts}` and safely dropping an old `'GS'`
entry (ambiguous --- could have been Classroom or Meet) rather than
guessing, per the "never fabricate" requirement. - Rewrote
`mergeLastLoginActivity_(candidates, sourceKey)` to take a specific
source key (`'gc'`/`'gm'`/`'db'`) and update only that slot of each
person's entry, going through `normalizeLastLoginEntry_()` first so
legacy data migrates transparently. - `getClassroomActivityMap_()` now
calls `mergeLastLoginActivity_(latestByEmail, 'gc')` (was `'GS'`);
`getMeetPresenceMap_()` now calls
`mergeLastLoginActivity_(latestMeetByEmail, 'gm')` (was `'GS'`) --- this
is the change that makes Classroom and Meet activity independently
trackable and separately labeled for the first time. -
`recordHeartbeat_()`'s inline Last Login merge now updates only the `db`
slot (via the same normalize-then-compare pattern), leaving `gc`/`gm`
completely untouched. - Added `recordDashboardSignOff()` --- a new,
minimal, publicly-callable function (the only wholly new capability
added this round) that resolves the current viewer's email server-side
via `Session.getActiveUser().getEmail()` (never trusts a client-supplied
email) and calls the existing `recordHeartbeat_()` again. It does not
duplicate or replace any existing session/login mechanism --- it reuses
the exact one already in place. - Added `summarizeLastLogin_(entry)` ---
computes the newest applicable timestamp and the full ordered
source-code list from a normalized `{gc,gm,db}` entry, as two explicitly
separate steps (per the spec's requirement that these be independent
calculations). - Rewrote `applyLastLogin_(courses)` to normalize each
person's stored entry and call `summarizeLastLogin_()`, stamping
`lastLoginAt`, `lastLoginSource` (now a combined string like
`'GC/GM/DB'`), `lastLoginDisplay`, and a new `lastLoginBySource` detail
object onto each person. - `Dashboard.html`: only the explanatory
comment above `renderPeople()` was updated (to describe the new
combined-source display instead of the old single-source one) --- the
function's actual rendering code was already just printing whatever
string `p.lastLoginDisplay` holds, so no client-side logic change was
needed there. Separately, near the existing `DASHBOARD_POLL_MS` polling
setup, added a `visibilitychange` listener (plus a `pagehide` backstop)
that calls the new `recordDashboardSignOff()` once, best-effort, as the
tab is hidden/closed --- with a small guard (`signOffSent`) so it fires
once per "session" of the tab being visible, resetting if the tab
becomes visible again so a later real close still sends its own
signal. - Nothing about the CRM/role-based access logic, the Classroom
sync job, the Sheet's column layout, the "Teacher NOT in Class"/"Needs
Tech Support" flows, chat, WhatsApp links, the Knowledge Base tab, or
any other pre-existing feature was touched. `presenceMap` (the transient
"online now" tracker) and its `PRESENCE_ONLINE_WINDOW_MINUTES` window
are completely unaffected --- this round only changed the permanent Last
Activity record.

**New Advanced Google Services / Google Cloud APIs required**: none ---
this round adds no new external API calls at all; it only restructures
how already-fetched Classroom/Meet audit-log data and already-happening
Dashboard heartbeats are stored and combined for display.

**New OAuth scopes required**: none, for the same reason.

**Google Classroom / Google Meet API limitations**: unchanged from the
twelfth round (see above and the "Limitations to know about" list in the
main design section) --- neither API exposes a literal "last login"
event; the Admin Reports API's Classroom/Meet audit logs remain the best
available proxies, refreshed at `SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES` cadence,
requiring Workspace super-admin authorization (and, for Classroom,
domain audit-log collection enabled).

**Exactly how the combined `(GC/GM/DB)`-style value is calculated, end
to end**: `getClassroomActivityMap_()`, `getMeetPresenceMap_()`, and
`recordHeartbeat_()`/`recordDashboardSignOff()` each independently
maintain their OWN slot (`gc`, `gm`, `db` respectively) in one shared
per-person record, each slot only ever advancing to a newer value, never
influenced by the other two slots. At render time, `applyLastLogin_()` →
`summarizeLastLogin_()` performs two separate, explicit calculations
against that person's three slots: (1) take the maximum timestamp among
whichever slots are populated --- this is the number displayed; (2) list
every populated slot's label in fixed `GC/GM/DB` order --- this is the
parenthetical shown next to that number. Because these two calculations
read from the same three slots but never influence each other, a source
can appear in the parenthetical without being the number that's shown
(as in the spec's own `GC=10:00, GM=10:05, DB=10:03` →
`"10:05 (GC/GM/DB)"` example), and a source that stops producing new
activity does not disappear from the parenthetical --- it simply stops
being able to advance the displayed number.

**Confirmation all pre-existing, unrelated functionality is preserved**:
role-based access (`getViewerRole_`/`getViewerContext_`), Classroom
roster sync and the Sheet cache, the "Teacher NOT in Class"/"Needs Tech
Support" 3-stage flows and their notification emails, the shared
dashboard chat, WhatsApp join links, the Knowledge Base --- Videos tab,
the Student Onboarding Status page and its permanent `onboarded` flag,
the live "online" green dot and its
`PRESENCE_ONLINE_WINDOW_MINUTES`/`MEET_ACTIVE_WINDOW_MINUTES`/`CLASSROOM_ACTIVE_WINDOW_MINUTES`
windows, and every existing time-driven trigger are all untouched by
this round --- verified by re-checking `Code.gs` for duplicate
function/variable declarations (none) and by running `node --check`
against both files after the change.

## Class Status state machine (Scheduled / Yet to Start / Class Started / Class Completed / Class Cancelled / Class Rescheduled) --- added fourteenth round

A brand-new per-course "Class Status" is computed and shown as a colored
badge on every course card, alongside the existing Live/Idle badge
(unrelated --- Live/Idle is Meet/Classroom-presence-based "is the
teacher active right now"; Class Status is the new scheduling state
machine below).

**The six statuses (exact display strings)**: `Scheduled`,
`Yet to Start`, `Class Started`, `Class Completed`, `Class Cancelled`,
`Class Rescheduled` --- internal codes (`scheduled`, `yet_to_start`,
`started`, `completed`, `cancelled`, `rescheduled`) are a stable
identifier separate from the display label (`CLASS_STATUS_LABELS` in
`Code.gs`), so wording can be corrected later without touching stored
data.

**Where the weekly schedule comes from**: Course Name and Section are
unchanged --- still `course.name`/`course.section` straight from the
Classroom API. The NEW piece is `parseCourseSchedule_(rawName)` in
`Code.gs`, which extracts the day/start-time/end-time/timezone segment
embedded in the course title text
(e.g. `"NILAI 99 - SA | TUE 11:30 AM - 12:30 PM EST | AY26-27"` →
Tuesday, 11:30 AM--12:30 PM). It prefers the pipe-delimited segment
between the first two `|` characters (this school's apparent convention)
but falls back to scanning the whole title if no pipes are found. If
either time is missing an unambiguous AM/PM marker, the schedule is
intentionally left unparsed (never guessed) --- that course simply shows
a plain `Scheduled` badge with no automatic transitions, rather than
risk transitioning at the wrong wall-clock time. The timezone
abbreviation found in the title (e.g. "EST") is kept only for potential
display --- every actual calculation always uses `LAST_LOGIN_TIMEZONE`
(`America/New_York`), per the explicit requirement that all class-status
timing use Eastern time regardless.

**The automatic state machine** (`computeAutomaticClassStatus_`, run
fresh every `getDashboardData()` call --- no new trigger needed, the
existing 1-minute dashboard poll is the cadence): 1. Before the
scheduled start time (Eastern) → `Scheduled`. 2. At/after the scheduled
start, before anyone joins Meet → `Yet to Start`. 3. As soon as any
teacher OR student in that course is detected in an active Meet call
(reusing the same per-person `inMeet` flag already computed from
`getMeetPresenceMap_`) → `Class Started`. A small persisted marker
(`CLASS_STARTED_MARK_PROP_KEY`) remembers that this week's occurrence
was seen as started, so a brief Meet disconnect doesn't flicker the
badge back to `Yet to Start` before the completion mark. 4. 90 minutes
after the **scheduled** start time (never the join time --- so a class
nobody ever joined still completes on schedule) → `Class Completed`.

**Weekly recurrence --- a design decision, not a literal spec
requirement (flagged for confirmation)**: since each course's schedule
repeats weekly, "Class Completed" needs to eventually give way to next
week's "Scheduled" state. This implementation only runs the Yet to Start
→ Started → Completed cycle on the actual scheduled weekday (Eastern
calendar date) itself; every other day of the week reads as plain
`Scheduled` (anticipating the next occurrence). So `Class Completed`
stays visible for the rest of that same Eastern calendar day, then
reverts to `Scheduled` the moment the date rolls over. If different
behavior was actually intended (e.g. `Class Completed` persisting
indefinitely until someone manually clears it), that's a small, isolated
change to `computeAutomaticClassStatus_`.

**Manual overrides (`Class Cancelled` / `Class Rescheduled`)** --- the
ONLY part of this feature that's actually persisted
(`CLASS_STATUS_PROP_KEY` Script Property,
`{courseId: {status, updatedAt, updatedBy}}`). `applyClassStatus_`
checks this FIRST for every course and, if present, uses it as-is with
automatic computation skipped entirely --- so nothing automatic can ever
revert or downgrade a manual Cancel/Reschedule (the explicit "manual
status priority" requirement). Set via the new
`setClassStatusManual(courseId, action)` server function, restricted
server-side (never just UI-hidden) to Admin, Headmaster, or that
course's own Teacher --- a Student is always rejected, regardless of
what the client sends. A third action, `'restore'`, clears the override
back to fully automatic --- this is an added convenience beyond the
literal spec (so a mistaken Cancel/Reschedule click isn't permanent
without editing Script Properties by hand), surfaced as a "Restore
Automatic Status" button once a manual override is active.

**Sheet/CRM visibility**: two columns were appended AFTER the existing
"Detail JSON" column (never inserted in the middle, so every
pre-existing column position 1-18 is unchanged, same convention as the
chat sheet's "Class Name" column) --- "Class Status (Manual Override)"
and "Class Status Updated At" --- snapshotting ONLY the manual override
for direct-Sheet/CRM visibility. The automatic Scheduled/Yet to
Start/Started/Completed states are deliberately never written to the
Sheet at all (they're recomputed fresh on every dashboard load, so a
stale Sheet snapshot of them would be actively misleading between
syncs).

**Class Status filter (Admin/HM only)**: a new dropdown
(`#classStatusFilter`) --- All / Scheduled / Yet to Start / Class
Started / Class Completed / Class Cancelled / Class Rescheduled ---
shown only when `roleCan('seeClassStatusFilter')` (admin or headmaster),
combined with the existing Live/No-students/etc. filter via AND.

**Colors (Part 16)**: `scheduled`→info (blue), `yet_to_start`→attention
(amber), `started`→success (green), `completed`→neutral (gray),
`cancelled`→danger (red), `rescheduled`→warning (orange) --- see
`.class-status-badge.status-*` in `Dashboard.html`. The text label is
always rendered alongside the color; color is never the only signal.

**Error handling / resilience**: if a course's title doesn't parse (no
day/time pattern, or ambiguous AM/PM), that course simply always shows
`Scheduled` with no automatic transitions --- it never crashes sync or
blocks any other course from computing correctly. A manual override
always short-circuits automatic computation regardless of parse success.
Nothing here calls a new external API, so there's no new failure mode
beyond "this course's title didn't parse the way this school's
convention expects."

## Role-based dashboard title (Part 19) --- added fourteenth round

The browser TAB title is now generated per-role in `doGet()`
(`Code.gs`), using the exact strings specified:
`"Avvaiyar Padasalai — Classroom Dashboard (ADMIN)"` / `"...(HM)"` /
`"...(Teacher)"` / `"...(Student)"`. This requires `doGet()` to resolve
the viewer's role before rendering, which it does via a read-only
`readAllCoursesFromCache_()` + `getViewerRole_()` call (same cache read
`getDashboardData()` already does --- no Classroom API call, no quota
risk); any failure (e.g. brand-new deployment with no cache sheet yet)
falls back to the original generic title rather than blocking the page.

**A deliberate scope decision**: the requested title strings drop "Tamil
Virtual School" from the branding. Since only the TAB title was
explicitly specified, and the on-page `<h1>` heading's full branding
("Avvaiyar Padasalai Tamil Virtual School --- Classroom Dashboard") was
a deliberate earlier design choice, the on-page heading keeps its full
text and only has `" (ROLE)"` appended client-side (`renderViewerInfo()`
in `Dashboard.html`, once `currentUser.role` is known) --- rather than
being shortened to match the tab title verbatim. Flagged in case the
shorter wording was actually intended for the visible heading too.

## Standardized status/button wording (Parts 20-24) --- added fourteenth round

The "Teacher NOT in Class" and "Needs Tech Support" 3-stage flows
previously used ONE shared `label` per stage for both the passive status
badge (shown to everyone) AND the clickable action button (shown to
whoever's permitted to advance it) --- which is exactly the "status
vs. action" confusion the spec called out (e.g. the button that
*reports* a problem was itself worded as if it were the problem's own
status). `TEACHER_NOT_IN_CLASS_STAGE_INFO` /
`NEEDS_TECH_SUPPORT_STAGE_INFO` in `Dashboard.html` now carry two
separate fields per stage: - `statusLabel` --- the stable, standardized
status text (`"Teacher Not in Class"` /
`"Need Tech Support in Google Classroom"`, correcting "...Google Class"
and the broken-grammar "Tech issue is been Resolved"), shown on the
passive card badge and unchanged across both the "reported" and
"in_progress" sub-stages, since from a viewer's perspective the
underlying problem is the same the whole time. - `actionLabel` --- a
short, action-oriented button label describing exactly what clicking
will do (`"Report Teacher Not in Class"` → `"Mark Tech Team Engaged"` →
`"Confirm Teacher Back"`; `"Request Tech Support"` →
`"Mark Tech Team Joining"` → `"Mark Resolved"`).

**Interpretation flagged for confirmation**: the spec's own old→new text
pairs for Parts 20/21 didn't map perfectly onto which exact stage-slot
each phrase currently occupied in the code (e.g. "Teacher Returned to
Class" → "Teacher Not in Class" would, read literally, turn a *resolve*
action into the *problem's own* status name). This implementation's
synthesis --- one stable status name per flow (matching Part 14/24's
canonical list) plus distinct short action verbs for each transition ---
is a best-effort reconciliation of the given text corrections with the
broader "separate status from action" requirement (Part 24) and the
exact final status list (Part 14). If a different specific mapping was
intended, the four label pairs above are the only things to adjust.

**"1 minute default transition timing" (Parts 20/21)**: no such timing
existed in the prior implementation (verified --- no matching
constant/mechanism), so this is treated as a NEW requirement rather than
something to "preserve." Implemented as a server-side cooldown
(`STATUS_STAGE_MIN_TRANSITION_MS = 60000` in `Code.gs`, enforced in both
`setTeacherNotInClassStage`/`setNeedsTechSupportStage` via a new
`assertStageTransitionCooldownElapsed_()` check against the stage's own
`updatedAt`) --- a click within 1 minute of the flow's last change is
rejected with a clear error, rather than silently no-op'ing. This
satisfies "not implemented only with browser `setTimeout()`" since it's
a real server-side check independent of the client. **Flagged**: if
"default transition timing" actually meant something else (e.g. an
automatic timed reset back to `none` after 1 minute of inactivity,
rather than a click-cooldown), this is the one function/constant to
revisit.

## Sept 2026, fifteenth round: three bug fixes --- one-sided AM/PM course-title parsing, legacy roster-filter visibility corrected, native alert() replaced with a warning toast

Three targeted fixes, all in `Code.gs`/`Dashboard.html`, none touching
Sheet schema, role-access logic, or any other feature:

1.  **Course-title time parsing failed when only one side of the time
    range stated AM/PM** ---
    e.g. `NILAI 4 - ED | FRI 6:30 - 8:00 PM EST | AY26-27` (only the END
    time says "PM") previously fell through to
    `(time not recognized — check the class title)` because
    `parseCourseSchedule_()` required BOTH `start` and `end` to have an
    explicit AM/PM. Fixed by only giving up when **both** sides are
    ambiguous; when just one side is, a new helper
    `inferMissingMeridiem_(hour12, minute, anchorMinutes, solvingForStart)`
    tries both the AM and PM reading of the ambiguous side and keeps
    whichever produces a positive, plausible class duration relative to
    the known side (e.g. `6:30 - 8:00 PM` resolves to `18:30-20:00`, not
    a nonsensical multi-hour or negative span). Verified against the
    example title plus a noon-boundary case (`FRI 11:00 - 12:00 PM` →
    11:00 AM-12:00 PM, correctly not 23:00-12:00) via a standalone Node
    test harness before applying.
2.  **"No students joined" / "No teacher assigned" filter+chips
    visibility was backwards** --- these two summary chips (and the "No
    students only" filter button) are now shown **only for Admin/HM**
    and hidden for Teacher/Student (`roleCan('seeLegacyRosterFilters')`
    in `Dashboard.html` now returns `isStaff` instead of `!isStaff`).
    This is the opposite of how it was originally implemented in the
    fourteenth round (Part 17/18) --- that implementation had the
    visibility rule inverted from what the school actually wanted,
    corrected here. The testing-checklist line under the
    fourteenth-round section above has been updated to match.
3.  **The 1-minute Class-Status-change cooldown (and any other
    server-thrown error) surfaced as a native browser dialog** --- "An
    embedded page at ...script.googleusercontent.com says Error: Please
    wait 53 more seconds before updating this status again." --- because
    every `withFailureHandler` callback called `alert(err.message)`.
    Apps Script's HTML Service renders `alert()` as that jarring
    embedded-page dialog rather than a normal in-app message. Replaced
    every `alert(...)` call (5 call sites: Teacher-NOT-in-Class,
    Needs-Tech-Support, Class-Status manual actions, chat send, Force
    Sync) with the existing `showToast(message)` function, extended to
    take a second `isWarning` argument: `showToast(err.message, true)`.
    A warning toast reuses the same fixed-position toast element but
    recolors it (`.toast.warn { background: var(--red); }`, new CSS
    rule) and stays visible slightly longer (4200ms vs. the normal
    3200ms) so an error message isn't missed.

No Sheet columns, Script Properties, Advanced Services, or role-access
rules changed. Verified with `node --check` on both files
(Dashboard.html's `<script>` block extracted first) before saving.

**Follow-up same round**: the 1-minute stage-change cooldown (item 3
above) was initially still implemented as a thrown `Error` server-side
(`assertStageTransitionCooldownElapsed_()`), just displayed more gently
client-side via the new warning toast. Since hitting this cooldown is an
expected, routine condition --- not a bug or a failed operation --- it
was changed to a genuinely non-error "warning" path: the helper was
renamed `stageTransitionCooldownWarning_()` and now **returns** the wait
message (or `null`) instead of throwing;
`setTeacherNotInClassStage()`/`setNeedsTechSupportStage()` return early
with the *current* (unchanged) stage entry plus a `warning` field when
blocked, rather than throwing --- so `google.script.run` treats it as a
normal, successful call. `Dashboard.html`'s two success handlers now
check `result.warning` first: if present, they re-enable the button,
show it as a warning toast, and re-render from the still-current data
(nothing changed, so no reload is needed); otherwise they proceed with
the normal success toast + `load()`. The permission checks and "That
status just changed" (Refresh-and-retry) case are unrelated and still
`throw new Error(...)` as before --- only the cooldown itself moved off
the exception path.

## Sept 2026, sixteenth round: Teacher Weekly Availability, Parent Feedback, and Teacher Star Points

Adds two new, purely additive features to the "This Week" area of the
Classes tab (a new `<div class="weekly-panels">` row rendered between
the summary chips and the class grid) --- nothing existing was
redesigned, moved, or removed. All new server functions live in one new
block in `Code.gs`, immediately before the "ONE-TIME SETUP" section; all
new client code lives in new functions in `Dashboard.html`, wired into
the existing 60-second poll (`load()`/`DASHBOARD_POLL_MS`) via one added
call, `loadWeeklyPanel()` --- no new timer.

**Two flagged assumptions** (the request didn't pin these down
explicitly; confirm with the school and say so if either should
change): - **"Parent" role = the Student login.** This app's 4-role
system (`getViewerRole_`/`getViewerContext_`) has no separate Parent
account or login mechanism, and adding one would mean a new Sheet-backed
Parent→Student mapping and a new role branch --- a materially larger,
speculative addition. Instead, the Student-role account is treated as
covering both "Student: view-only" and "Parent: submit feedback" from
the request --- a signed-in Student can view their own class(es)
read-only AND submit thumbs/star feedback for them. If APS actually has
(or wants) separate parent email logins, that's a distinct follow-up
feature, not a tweak to this one. - **Week boundary = Sunday-Saturday,
Eastern time.** `getCurrentWeekId_()` returns `WK-YYYY-MM-DD` where the
date is the Eastern-time Sunday that starts the current week (using the
same `easternDayOfWeek_`/`easternWallTimeToDate_`/`LAST_LOGIN_TIMEZONE`
helpers every other date calculation in this app already uses) ---
deliberately NOT tied to an assumed academic-year start date (none is
recorded anywhere in this project), which is what the request's own
"...or an equivalent reliable week/date key" wording allows for.
`getWeekLabel_()` turns that key into "Week of Sep 7 - Sep 13, 2026" for
display.

**New Sheet tabs** (both in the existing target spreadsheet ---
`TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID`, no new spreadsheet --- created on first use via
`getOrCreateXSheet_()`, the same pattern as
`WhatsApp_Group_Links`/`Dashboard_Chat_Window`), names per the school's
explicit instruction: - **`Teacher_Weekly_Availability`** --- columns:
Week ID, Teacher Email, Teacher Name, Course ID, Course Name, Section
(Day/Time), Availability Status (`pending`/`confirmed`/`not_available`),
Alternative Arrangement (one of
`parent_teacher_arranged`/`sub_teacher_arranged`/`need_hm_support`, or
blank), Updated At, Updated By Email, Updated By Name. One row per
Teacher+Course+Week (upserted in place, never duplicated). -
**`Teacher_Star_Points`** --- columns: Week ID, Student Email, Parent
Email (currently always the same value as Student Email, per the
Parent-role assumption above), Teacher Email, Teacher Name, Course ID,
Course Name, Thumbs (`up`/`down`/blank), Stars (1-5 or blank), Feedback
At (first-submitted timestamp, preserved across updates), Updated At.
One row per Student+Course+Week (upserted in place --- resubmitting the
same week just updates the existing row, never creates a duplicate).

**New server functions in `Code.gs`** (all reuse
`readAllCoursesFromCache_()`/`getViewerContext_()` --- no new
Classroom/Reports/Directory API calls): - `getCurrentWeekId_()` /
`getWeekLabel_()` --- the week key and its display label (see assumption
above). - `primaryTeacherOf_(course)` --- the one "teacher of record"
for availability/feedback purposes (first teacher on the course). -
`buildAvailabilityBoard_(courses, weekId)` --- merges the
(role-filtered) course list with saved `Teacher_Weekly_Availability`
rows, defaulting any course with no saved response yet this week to
`pending`/⚪ (nothing is written just by viewing). -
`setTeacherAvailabilityStatus(courseId, status, alternative)` --- the
only way to write an availability row. **Server-side permission check**:
admin/headmaster (any course), or that course's own teacher --- a
student can never call this successfully no matter what the client
sends, matching the "Student Role Restriction: view-only, no edit
controls" requirement. Validates `status` and (when `not_available`)
that `alternative` is one of the three defined arrangement keys. -
`computeTeacherSummaryFromRows_(rows, teacherEmail)` --- pure
aggregation over an already-fetched `Teacher_Star_Points` rows array
into one teacher's auto-computed totals (`totalFeedback`, `totalStars`,
`averageStars`, `thumbsUp`, `thumbsDown`, plus this-week-only figures)
--- **never manually entered**, always derived. Takes `rows` as a
parameter (rather than re-reading the sheet) specifically so a caller
summarizing many teachers, or one student's several classes, reads
`Teacher_Star_Points` exactly **once** and reuses that array ---
avoiding the N-times-larger read a naive per-teacher/per-class loop
would otherwise do. - `summarizeTeacherStars_(teacherEmail)` ---
convenience single-teacher wrapper around the above for the one-off case
(a Teacher viewing only their own summary). -
`submitParentFeedback(courseId, thumbs, stars)` --- the only way to
write a feedback row. **Server-side permission check**: only a
`student`-role viewer enrolled in that specific course; requires at
least one of thumbs/stars. Upserts (never duplicates) the
Student+Course+Week row. - `getWeeklyPanelData()` --- the single
combined, role-aware payload the dashboard fetches per load/poll
(mirrors the existing `getDashboardData()` pattern --- one call, not
several): always includes `{ weekId, weekLabel, role, availability }`;
additionally includes `teacherPerformance` (admin/headmaster: every
teacher, sorted by total stars descending; teacher: just their own
one-item array) or `myClasses` (student: per-class `myFeedback` + that
class's teacher's `teacherSummary`).

**New client code in `Dashboard.html`**: a `.weekly-panels` CSS grid
(two cards side by side on desktop, stacked under 640px) reusing the
existing `--green`/`--red`/`--amber`/`--blue`/`--gray` palette --- no
new colors --- with every status shown as an icon **and** a text label,
never color alone (🟢 Teacher Confirmed / 🔴 Not Available / 🟡 Not
Available - `<arrangement>` / ⚪ No Response Yet). `loadWeeklyPanel()`
fetches `getWeeklyPanelData()` and `renderWeeklyPanels()` picks, per
role: an availability card (`renderAvailabilityCard`/`renderAvailRow`,
edit controls shown only for admin/headmaster/teacher --- never
rendered, not just disabled, for a student) plus either a "Teacher Star
Points" leaderboard/summary card (`renderStaffPerformanceCard`,
admin/headmaster/teacher) or a "Parent Feedback" card with thumbs + a
5-star row per enrolled class (`renderStudentFeedbackCard`/`starRow`,
student). `setAvailability()` and `submitFeedback()` call the
corresponding server functions and refresh the panel from the server
afterward (no optimistic/local-only state), so what's displayed always
reflects what was actually saved.

Nothing existing was touched beyond the one added `loadWeeklyPanel();`
call inside `load()`'s success handler. Verified with `node --check` on
both files (Dashboard.html's `<script>` block extracted first) plus a
small standalone Node check of the client-side status→color mapping
logic before saving.

## Sept 2026, seventeenth round: country flag beside each person's name (header badge + class-card rosters)

Adds a small, best-effort country flag next to a name in two places: the
signed-in viewer's own header badge (e.g. "🇺🇸 Sugadev Velayutham
(ADMIN)") and every Teacher/Student roster chip on a class card. No
existing login, role-detection, Google Classroom integration, layout, or
CSS was changed beyond adding the new flag elements/rules --- everything
else (dashboard tabs, role logic, chat, WhatsApp links, Class Status,
Weekly Availability/Parent Feedback) is untouched.

**Key architectural decision (flagged)**: the request's own spec called
for a `Code.gs` backend function that does the IP-geolocation lookup
server-side. That would not actually work correctly --- any code called
via `google.script.run` executes on Google's own servers, not on the
signed-in person's computer, so a server-side call to an IP-geolocation
service would report **Google's** network location, not the person's.
This was caught before writing any code and the design changed
accordingly, rather than shipping a backend function that would show the
wrong country for everyone: the geolocation lookup happens entirely
**client-side**, via a plain `fetch('https://ipapi.co/json/')` call made
directly from each person's own browser (`loadUserCountryFlag()` in
`Dashboard.html`), which is what actually reads their real connection.
The result is then reported to a small, genuinely server-side function
(`recordViewerCountry(countryCode, countryName)`) purely to **persist**
it --- trusted via `Session.getActiveUser().getEmail()`, never a
client-supplied identity --- so other viewers can also see that person's
flag in their roster chip. No `getLoggedInUserInfo()` function was
added, since `getDashboardData()` already returns the viewer's
email/role/name and now also carries every roster person's country via
the same payload --- a separate function would just be a second,
redundant call.

**Where it runs / how often (Part 9)**: `loadUserCountryFlag()` is
called exactly once, from the same one-time startup block at the bottom
of `Dashboard.html` as the initial
`load()`/`loadSyncInfo()`/`loadChat(false)` calls --- never from the
60-second poll inside `load()`, never on tab/view switches, never on
refresh. A module-level `userCountryInfo` variable (starts `null`)
guards this: the very first thing `loadUserCountryFlag()` does is set it
to the 🌎 fallback and return early on any later call, so this can never
fire twice in one session even if something else calls it again.

**Server-side, `Code.gs`**: - `USER_COUNTRY_PROP_KEY` --- a new Script
Property,
`{ normalizedEmail: { countryCode, countryName, updatedAt } }`, same
storage pattern as `lastLoginMap`/presence maps. -
`countryCodeToFlagServer_(code)` --- ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 → emoji flag via
the standard "regional indicator symbol" Unicode trick (each letter A-Z
maps to a code point in the U+1F1E6-U+1F1FF range) --- **no hardcoded
per-country list**, exactly matching the identical client-side
`countryCodeToFlag()` in `Dashboard.html`. Returns `''` for anything
that isn't exactly 2 letters. - `getUserCountryMap_()` --- reads/parses
the Script Property. - `recordViewerCountry(countryCode, countryName)`
--- the only function that writes to it. Identity comes ONLY from
`Session.getActiveUser().getEmail()` (never a client-supplied email ---
can't be used to set someone else's country); validates `countryCode` is
exactly 2 letters and `countryName` is non-empty (capped to 100 chars)
and silently no-ops otherwise; never throws (best-effort,
fire-and-forget from the client, no failure handler needed). Only
`countryCode`/`countryName` are ever accepted or stored --- never an IP
address, coordinates, city, postal code, or ISP (Part 10 of the
request). - `applyUserCountry_(courses)` --- merges each person's stored
country onto every teacher/student object across `courses` (same
pattern/call-site style as `applyLastLogin_`/`applyLivePresence_`),
adding `countryCode`, `countryName`, and a ready-to-render `countryFlag`
(each `''` for anyone never recorded yet --- never guessed). Wired into
`getDashboardData()` alongside the other `applyX_()` calls, so it rides
the exact same request/poll --- no new API call, no new endpoint hit on
its own.

**Client-side, `Dashboard.html`**: - Header badge (`#viewerBadge`) was
restructured to hold two child spans --- `#userCountryFlag` (new) and
`#viewerBadgeText` (the existing name/role text) --- so
`renderViewerInfo()` can keep rewriting just the text on every poll
without wiping out or re-fetching the flag each time. -
`countryCodeToFlag(code)` --- identical logic to the server-side mirror
above. - `loadUserCountryFlag()` --- the one-time fetch described above,
with a 4-second client-side timeout; on any failure, timeout, or
malformed/error response, it leaves the flag at the generic 🌎 fallback
that was set immediately when the function started --- no popup, no
error toast, no retry loop, and the rest of the dashboard is completely
unaffected either way (Part 8). On success it also fires
`recordViewerCountry(...)` (fire-and-forget) so this viewer's flag
becomes visible to others. - `applyUserCountryFlag()` --- sets
`#userCountryFlag`'s text to the flag emoji and its `title` attribute to
the full country name (the hover tooltip from Part 6); the flag glyph
itself is always visible with no JS needed for that part, so mobile (no
hover) still shows it (Part 12). - `renderPeople()` (the Teacher/Student
roster chip renderer used on every class card) now also renders a
`.person-flag` span (same flag + `title`-tooltip pattern) immediately
before each person's name, sourced from `p.countryFlag`/`p.countryName`
on the course data `getDashboardData()` already returns --- `''` renders
nothing, so a person who hasn't been recorded yet just shows no flag
rather than a broken/placeholder one. - New CSS: `.user-country-flag`
(header badge) and `.person-flag` (roster chips) --- both small, inline,
and built from existing spacing/typography conventions; no new colors,
no new layout containers, and the existing chip
height/wrapping/truncation behavior is unchanged (Part 12).

Scope note: flags were added to the header badge and the Classes-tab
roster chips only (the two places names are shown "near" a person,
matching the request) --- the Student Onboarding Status report table and
chat panel were deliberately left unchanged, consistent with "make the
smallest possible change."

No Sheet columns, existing Script Property keys, role-access rules, or
Classroom integration were touched. Verified with `node --check` on both
files (Dashboard.html's `<script>` block extracted first), a duplicate
function/variable-declaration scan (none found), and a standalone Node
check of `countryCodeToFlag()` against all the example codes in the
request (US/IN/CA/SG/AU/GB/DE/FR, plus invalid input) before saving.

The sixteenth round shipped Teacher Weekly Availability and Teacher Star
Points as **two separate cards**, each repeating the same class
name/time (visible in the user's screenshot: a "This Week -- Teacher

-   `renderPerformanceCard`/`renderAvailabilityCard`/`renderStaffPerformanceCard`/`renderStudentFeedbackCard`/`renderAvailRow`
    were removed outright (not deprecated in place) and replaced by
