Verified with `node --check` on the extracted `<script>` block and a
scan confirming no leftover references to the removed render functions
before saving.

## Sept 2026, nineteenth round: teacher mobile number shown to all roles; Classroom Section already fully visible under the course name

Two clarifying questions were asked before touching code, since the
request ("Display Google Classroom Section values under the Course Name.
Such as teacher and Mobile number and HM Mobile number to all the
users") named a value --- an HM mobile number --- that has no existing
per-course data source anywhere in this codebase:

1.  **Where should an HM mobile number come from?** Answer: the school
    will put it directly in a course's Google Classroom **Section**
    field text (the same free-text field Classroom already exposes per
    course) --- not a new structured field or Sheet column.
2.  **Should the teacher's phone number (captured but hidden by default)
    now show to everyone, including Students?** Answer: yes, to all
    roles.

**What was already true, unchanged**: `course.section` (the raw Google
Classroom Section field, synced verbatim into the `Courses` cache sheet
--- see `section: course.section || ''` in `buildCourseRecord_`) has
always been rendered in FULL, to every role, directly under the course
name in `Dashboard.html`'s `course-meta` line (`renderCard()`) --- there
was no gating and nothing was truncating it. So whatever the school
types into a course's Section field in Classroom (schedule info, an HM
contact line, anything else) already appears there verbatim for every
viewer with no code change needed. This was confirmed rather than
assumed, by reading `renderCard()` and the
`buildCourseRecord_`/cache-sheet plumbing end to end.

**What changed**: - `SHOW_CONTACT_PHONE` (`Code.gs`) flipped from
`false` to `true` --- teacher phone numbers (extracted from a Classroom
display name like "Mrs. Kavitha - 98410 12345" via the existing
`splitNameAndPhone_()`) now show dashboard-wide, to
Admin/HM/Teacher/Student alike, both on each class card's Teacher roster
chip and the Student Onboarding Status page's Teacher column
(`renderGroupTeachers()`, unchanged, already gated on this same flag). -
**A latent double-render bug was caught and fixed while wiring this up,
before it could ever surface**: the OLD `SHOW_CONTACT_PHONE=true`
behavior substituted the person's `name` field with the **raw,
un-stripped** Classroom display name
(`name: SHOW_CONTACT_PHONE ? rawName : parsed.name`) --- which still had
the phone number embedded in the text --- while ALSO populating a
separate `phone` field with that same phone number. Turning the flag on
would have made the Student Onboarding Status Teacher column show the
phone number TWICE ("Mrs. Kavitha - 98410 12345 📞 98410 12345"). Fixed
by always using the clean, phone-stripped `parsed.name` for both
teachers and students (never substituting the raw name back in) and
treating `phone` as the one and only place the number is ever rendered
from, client-side. - **Deliberately scoped to teachers only, never
students**: the exact same name/phone-splitting logic already runs on
the Students roster too (`buildCourseRecord_`, unchanged) --- a
Student's `phone` field is still captured but was, and remains, **never
rendered anywhere** in `Dashboard.html`, regardless of
`SHOW_CONTACT_PHONE`. `Dashboard.html`'s `renderPeople()` gained a new
`showPhone` parameter so this is enforced at the call site, not just by
convention: the Teacher roster call passes `showContactPhone` (the
client's copy of the flag, fetched via the existing
`getShowContactPhone()`); the Student roster call never passes it, so a
phone can never appear there no matter how the flag is set. This was a
deliberate privacy call --- the request only ever asked for "teacher and
HM mobile number," never a student's --- flagged here in case the school
actually wants a student contact number visible to their own
teacher/parent somewhere; that would be a distinct, separate decision. -
New teacher-phone display reuses the existing `.teacher-phone` CSS class
(already used identically on the Student Onboarding Status page) rather
than introducing a new style, so it looks consistent with what was
already there.

No Sheet columns, Script Properties, role-access rules, or Classroom
integration were touched beyond the one config flag. Verified with
`node --check` on both files (Dashboard.html's `<script>` block
extracted first) before saving.

## Sept 2026, twentieth round: "This Week" merged directly into each class's own card --- one single compact block, not two separate cards

The eighteenth round consolidated Teacher Availability + Teacher Star
Points into one card, but it still stood as its OWN separate section
above the class grid --- so a class's "Classroom Details" card (name,
section, roster, live/status controls) and its "This Week" status were
still two visually separate blocks for the same class (visible in the
user's screenshot). This round merges them into ONE block: the "This
Week" content now renders **inside** each class's own card in
`renderCard()`, directly under that card's status badges --- same
information, same interactivity, but literally the same card now, for
every role.

`Dashboard.html`-only change; `Code.gs`/Sheets/server are untouched ---
`getWeeklyPanelData()` already returned everything needed
(`availability`, `teacherPerformance`, `myClasses`), this was purely a
client-side layout change plus one small behavioral change described
below.

-   The standalone `#weeklyPanels` container `<div>` (between the
    summary chips and `#grid`) was **removed** from the HTML.
    `renderThisWeekCard`/`renderStaffTeacherWeekCard`/`renderStudentWeekCard`/`renderClassWeekRow`/`renderWeeklyPanels`/`wireWeeklyPanelEvents`
    were all removed and replaced by a single `renderWeeklyInline(c)`
    --- called from inside `renderCard(c)` for the ONE class `c`
    currently being rendered, looking up that class's own row from
    `weeklyPanelData.availability` (matched by `c.id`) rather than
    iterating every class into a separate list.
-   `renderWeeklyInline(c)` returns `''` (renders nothing) for a class
    with no teacher on record, or before `weeklyPanelData` has loaded
    yet --- see the behavioral change below for what happens once it
    has.
-   Role behavior is unchanged, just relocated: Admin/HM/Teacher get the
    availability badge + Yes/No/alternative edit controls
    (`renderAvailEditActions`, extracted from the old
    `renderClassWeekRow` as its own small helper) plus that row's
    teacher's Star Points line; Student gets the same availability badge
    **read-only** (no edit controls --- still never rendered at all, not
    just disabled) plus their own thumbs/star feedback controls and that
    teacher's Star Points. All the same
    `data-avail-*`/`data-thumb`/`data-star` attribute names are used, so
    `wireWeeklyInlineEvents()` (the renamed/adapted
    `wireWeeklyPanelEvents`) is nearly identical, just querying `#grid`
    instead of `#weeklyPanels`, and called once at the end of
    `render()`'s existing per-card wiring loop rather than after a
    separate render pass.
-   **One small necessary behavioral change**: `getWeeklyPanelData()`
    resolves slightly after `getDashboardData()`, so on the very first
    page load the grid can render once WITHOUT any class having its
    "This Week" block yet (since `weeklyPanelData` is still `null` at
    that instant). `loadWeeklyPanel()`'s success handler used to just
    repaint the old standalone section (`renderWeeklyPanels()`); now
    that the data lives inside the class cards, it calls `render()`
    again once `weeklyPanelData` arrives (only when still on the Classes
    view), so the grid re-renders and every card picks up its block.
    This happens once per load/poll, not repeatedly, and is invisible in
    practice (typically resolves within the same second).
-   CSS: the old
    `.weekly-panels`/`.weekly-card`/`.weekly-card-title`/`.weekly-card-subtitle`/`.weekly-week-label`/`.weekly-empty`/`.avail-row*`/`.feedback-row*`
    rules (all specific to the removed standalone section/cards) were
    deleted as dead CSS. New, much smaller rules were added for the
    inline block instead: `.weekly-inline` (a thin block with a top and
    bottom border, sitting between the card's status badges and its
    Teacher/Student roster --- visually part of the same card, not a
    nested card of its own),
    `.weekly-inline-top`/`.weekly-inline-label`/`.weekly-inline-week`
    (the "📅 This Week (Week of ...)" header line + status badge), and
    `.weekly-inline-feedback` (lays out a Student's thumbs + star row
    together). `.avail-status-badge`, `.avail-actions`, `.avail-btn`,
    `.row-perf-line`, `.star-row`/`.star-btn`,
    `.thumbs-row`/`.thumb-btn`, and `.feedback-saved-note` were kept
    as-is (still used, just now inside `.weekly-inline` instead of the
    old `.avail-row`/`.feedback-row`).

Verified with `node --check` on the extracted `<script>` block, a scan
confirming zero leftover references to any of the removed
functions/classes, and a duplicate-function-declaration scan (none
found) before saving.

## Sept 2026, twenty-first round: week boundary changed from calendar Sunday-Saturday to the school's actual Friday-Sunday class schedule --- CONFIRMED, no longer a flagged assumption

Every previous round (starting with the sixteenth) built the Teacher
Weekly Availability / Parent Feedback / Teacher Star Points feature on a
**flagged assumption**: `getCurrentWeekId_()` used a calendar
Sunday-Saturday week, because the school's actual class-day schedule
hadn't been confirmed yet. The school clarified: **classes only run
Friday, Saturday, and Sunday this year** --- so a Sunday-Saturday
boundary was actively wrong, splitting a Friday+Saturday class from the
very next day's Sunday class into two different "weeks." This round
replaces that assumption with the school's confirmed schedule.

A second question had no single obviously-correct answer, so it was
asked directly rather than guessed: **on the off days (Monday-Thursday,
when there is no school), which Friday-Sunday block should "This Week"
show --- the one that just ended, or the upcoming one?** The school's
answer: **the upcoming weekend** (so teachers/HM/admin can see and act
on availability ahead of time, e.g. mark themselves unavailable for the
coming weekend, before it arrives) --- this is the "roll-forward"
behavior implemented below.

**`Code.gs` --- the only file changed** (`Dashboard.html`'s "This Week"
header already renders whatever `weeklyPanelData.weekLabel` the server
sends, with no hardcoded day assumption of its own, so it needed no
change):

-   `getCurrentWeekId_(now)` --- re-anchored from "the Sunday that
    starts a 7-day calendar week" to **"the Friday that starts the
    current or upcoming Friday-Saturday-Sunday class block."**
    Implemented as a per-day-of-week offset table
    (`offsetToFridayByDow = [-2, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0, -1]`, indexed
    0=Sun...6=Sat, reusing the existing
    `easternDayOfWeek_()`/`easternWallTimeToDate_()` Eastern-time
    helpers unchanged): Friday/Saturday/Sunday map to (or stay on) the
    Friday that started their own in-progress block;
    Monday/Tuesday/Wednesday/Thursday roll **forward** to the upcoming
    Friday. The `WK-YYYY-MM-DD` key format itself is unchanged --- only
    which date it anchors to changed --- so `getWeeklyPanelData()` and
    every other caller needed no changes at all.
-   `getWeekLabel_(weekId)` --- re-derived from "Friday + 2 days =
    Sunday" instead of "Sunday + 6 days = Saturday," so a label now
    reads e.g. **"Week of Sep 11 - Sep 13, 2026"** (a 3-day span)
    instead of the old 7-day "Week of Sep 6 - Sep 12, 2026."
-   The "WEEK BOUNDARY" doc-comment block (originally added in the
    sixteenth round as an explicitly flagged, unconfirmed assumption)
    was rewritten to record this as a **CONFIRMED** decision dated
    2026-09-11, including the exact roll-forward convention, so a future
    reader doesn't have to re-derive or re-ask this.

**Verification**: `node --check` on `Code.gs`, plus a standalone Node
harness re-implementing the exact offset table and checking all 8
relevant dates around the Sep 2026 boundary (Fri Sep 11 through the
following Fri Sep 18) --- confirmed Fri/Sat/Sun (Sep 11-13) all resolve
to `WK-2026-09-11` / "Week of Sep 11 - Sep 13, 2026," and Mon-Thu (Sep
14-17) all roll forward to `WK-2026-09-18` / "Week of Sep 18 - Sep 20,
2026," exactly matching the confirmed design.

**Orphaned-data note**: any `weekId` values already recorded in
`Teacher_Weekly_Availability` / `Teacher_Star_Points` under the old
Sunday-anchor scheme (e.g. `WK-2026-09-06` for the week the user's own
example referenced) remain in the Sheet as historical data --- they are
simply never returned by `getCurrentWeekId_()` again going forward,
since no real calendar date now maps back to a stale Sunday anchor that
isn't also a valid Friday anchor for some other, unrelated week. If the
school has already recorded live availability/feedback this season under
the old scheme, that specific week's data won't resurface under "This
Week" and would need to be reviewed manually in the Sheet if it matters
--- flagging this here since it wasn't asked about directly, but no
action was taken since we have no way to know if any such data exists
yet.

## Sept 2026, twenty-second round: Parent Feedback / Survey link added, Student role only

Request: add a link to the school's external Parent Feedback survey
(`https://zfrmz.com/fkgKCAvTAQN7syz20M6O`) under the "Parent Feedback --
This Week" section, visible to Students only and never to Teachers.

`Dashboard.html`-only change; `Code.gs`/Sheets/server untouched --- this

-   Added inside `renderWeeklyInline(c)`'s **Student-role branch only**
    (`role === 'student'`) --- the same branch that renders the

-   New CSS: `.feedback-label`, `.feedback-survey-link` (added next to

Verified with `node --check` on the extracted `<script>` block before

## Sept 2026, twenty-third round: Default Country (first-login picker + "change" any time), fixed browser→Default Country fallback chain, and Class/Grade Change email narrowed to the student's APS email only

Four requests bundled into one round: (1) a per-user, persistent
**Default Country**, asked for once on first login and
reusable/changeable afterward; (2)/(3) the seventeenth round's
country-flag feature corrected so its priority chain (browser-detected →
Default Country → no flag) actually behaves as specified, plus a latent
bug fix that had silently kept the whole feature from ever running; (4)
the APS Class/Grade Change lifecycle email narrowed to the student's own
APS email address only. No existing
login/role/Classroom/chat/onboarding/knowledge-base functionality was
touched beyond what's described below.

### Latent bug fixed first (blocking everything else in this round)

`loadUserCountryFlag()` --- the seventeenth round's one-time
browser-country lookup --- was fully implemented but **never actually
called anywhere** in `Dashboard.html`; it wasn't wired into the "initial
page-load calls" the seventeenth round's own doc-comment claimed it was.
In practice this meant the header flag and the `recordViewerCountry()`
write it triggers had never fired for anyone. Fixed by adding one
`loadUserCountryFlag();` call at each of the two places dashboard access
is actually granted --- `apsFinishPermissionConfirm_()` (normal login)
and the `apsBootstrapSession()` remembered-session success handler ---
alongside the pre-existing `load()`/`loadSyncInfo()`/`loadChat(false)`
calls, exactly where the doc always said it ran. This is a bug fix, not
new scope; everything else in the seventeenth round's design
(once-per-session guard via `userCountryInfo !== null`, client-side-only
IP lookup, never a server-side lookup) is unchanged.

### 1. Default Country (`Code.gs`)

Reuses the exact same `USER_COUNTRY_PROP_KEY` Script Property /
`getUserCountryMap_()` map the seventeenth round already introduced for
the auto-detected "current login country" --- **no new storage
mechanism**, per the requirement to reuse existing storage before adding
a new one. Each per-email entry now optionally carries a second,
independent pair alongside the existing auto-detected one: -
`countryCode` / `countryName` / `updatedAt` --- auto-detected
(unchanged, still written only by `recordViewerCountry()`). -
`defaultCountryCode` / `defaultCountryName` / `defaultUpdatedAt` ---
user-chosen, sticky, written only by the new `setMyDefaultCountry()`.

An entry from before this round simply has no `defaultCountryCode` ---
fully backward compatible.

-   `getMyCountryPreference()` --- returns the CURRENT signed-in
    viewer's own
    `{ hasDefault, defaultCountryCode, defaultCountryName, defaultFlag, detectedCountryCode, detectedCountryName }`.
    Identity is always `Session.getActiveUser().getEmail()`, never a
    client-supplied email. Used by the client to decide, on the
    Permission Review screen, whether to ask for a country (only when
    `hasDefault` is false) --- and by the header flag's fallback path
    when browser detection is unavailable.
-   `setMyDefaultCountry(countryCode, countryName)` --- the one function
    that ever writes a default; validates a 2-letter code + non-empty
    name (same validation shape as `recordViewerCountry`), locks with
    `LockService`, and returns the fresh `getMyCountryPreference()`.
    Called from exactly two places client-side: the first-time picker,
    and the "Change Country" modal --- so there is one single write path
    for both.

### 1.1 First-time country selection, on the "Review Dashboard Permissions" screen (`Dashboard.html`)

A new block, `#apsCountryBlock`, was added inside the existing
`#apsScreenPermission` gate screen (right after the
Name/APSID/Email/Role summary, before the Cancel/Continue buttons) ---
**not** a new screen, so the existing login state machine
(`apsShowScreen()`, the mismatch/denied/error/cancelled screens, the
30-day/8-hour remembered-session bypass) is completely unchanged.

-   `apsHandleAuthResult()` now also calls the new
    `apsLoadCountryPreference()` right after showing the Permission
    screen. That function calls `getMyCountryPreference()`: if the
    signed-in email already has a Default Country, the country block
    stays hidden and "Continue to Dashboard" behaves exactly as before
    (asked once, never again, per the requirement). If it doesn't, the
    block is shown, "Continue to Dashboard" is disabled until a country
    is actually picked, and the search box is prefilled (as a
    convenience suggestion only, not an auto-selection) with the
    best-effort browser-detected country name if one is already known
    this session.
-   The picker itself is a plain, dependency-free searchable dropdown
    (`apsRenderCountryOptions()`), backed by a new `APS_COUNTRIES` array
    of ISO 3166-1 country codes + names (\~195 entries) --- flags are
    never hardcoded per country; they're derived on the fly by the
    existing `countryCodeToFlag()` Unicode trick, so both name and flag
    are shown per option, per the requirement.
-   `apsConfirmPermission()` was restructured (the actual "grant access"
    logic extracted into `apsFinishPermissionConfirm_()`): when the
    country block was shown, clicking Continue first calls
    `setMyDefaultCountry(code, name)` and only then proceeds to grant
    access --- best-effort (a save failure never blocks the person out
    of their own dashboard, matching this codebase's existing
    graceful-degradation convention elsewhere). When the block wasn't
    shown (a default already exists), Continue behaves exactly as it
    always did, with no extra round trip.
-   **Update/change later (1.1.6)**: the header's country flag
    (`#userCountryFlag`) is now clickable, opening a small "Change
    Country" modal (`#countryModalOverlay`) that reuses the same
    `APS_COUNTRIES` list/dropdown and calls the same
    `setMyDefaultCountry()`. This is the "existing authorized
    permission-management workflow" allowance from the request,
    implemented as the simplest available hook rather than a new admin
    screen --- the person is always changing only their own default, via
    the same trusted `Session.getActiveUser()` identity as everything
    else.

### 2/3. Priority chain fixed + tooltip source + "no flag" state (`Dashboard.html`)

The seventeenth round's header flag already existed but didn't implement
a fallback or the required tooltip wording, and defaulted to a generic
🌎 placeholder instead of hiding when nothing was known. Fixed, without
changing the underlying detection mechanism (client-side
`fetch('https://ipapi.co/json/')`, country-level only, no geolocation
permission prompt --- the same mechanism this domain already had, kept
per "don't use IP-based location unless the existing infrastructure
already supports it and it's appropriate for country-level detection"):

-   `loadUserCountryFlag()`: on success, `userCountryInfo` is tagged
    `source: 'browser'`. On failure/timeout/malformed response, it now
    calls the new `applyDefaultCountryFallback_()` instead of freezing
    on a placeholder --- which calls `getMyCountryPreference()` and, if
    a Default Country is on file, shows it tagged `source: 'default'`;
    otherwise the flag stays hidden (`source: 'none'`). This is exactly
    the requested `Browser-detected → Default Country → no flag` chain.
-   `applyUserCountryFlag()`: hides `#userCountryFlag` entirely
    (`display:none`, no text, no tooltip) whenever there's no flag to
    show --- never a placeholder globe --- and otherwise sets the
    tooltip to `"Country: <name>"` plus, on a second line,
    `"Source: Browser"` or `"Source: Default Country"` (omitted only in
    the unreachable case of a flag with no known source), matching the
    requested tooltip wording exactly.
-   `#userCountryFlag`'s initial HTML markup was changed from an
    always-visible `🌎` to empty + `display:none`, so a viewer never
    sees an incorrect/placeholder flag before detection resolves.
-   CSS: `.user-country-flag` gained `cursor:pointer` (for the "Change
    Country" modal above) --- no layout changes, so it still can't
    overlap the existing profile picture, role indicator, or top-right
    controls (unchanged `.viewer-badge` flex layout, still not
    `position:fixed`, still wraps normally on narrow screens).
-   Scope note: this round's flag-behavior fixes apply to the viewer's
    own header badge only --- the seventeenth round's separate
    per-roster-chip flags (`.person-flag`, other teachers'/students' own
    detected country) are untouched, since the request's "next to the
    existing Google profile picture" language is about the signed-in
    viewer, not other people's roster chips.

### 4. Class/Grade Change email narrowed to the student's APS email only (`Code.gs`)

`notifyGtrStudent_(request, message)` --- the single function behind
every Class/Grade Change lifecycle email to the requesting student
(submission, Stage-1 decision, final approval, processing errors,
cancellation notice) --- previously sent to both `request.studentEmail`
**and** `request.parentEmail`. It now sends to `request.studentEmail`
only (the student's own APS email, captured at submission time from
their authenticated `Session.getActiveUser()` identity --- see
`submitGradeChangeRequest()`/`submitTimingChangeRequest()`), per the
explicit requirement that this specific notification reach the student's
APS email address ONLY.

-   `parentEmail` is still collected at submission, still stored on
    every request row, and still shown to approvers inside
    `gtrEmailBody_()` --- nothing about the request data or the
    approver-facing view changed, only who receives this one lifecycle
    email.
-   `notifyGtrApprovers_()` (the separate email to all
    `GRADE_CHANGE_APPROVER_EMAILS` staff/approvers, used for the same
    lifecycle events) is untouched --- that's the "internal BCC/CC for
    operational purposes" the request's own exception clause allows,
    since approvers structurally need to know a request exists in order
    to act on it. It was never sending to a teacher, admin-as-bystander,
    or headmaster-as-bystander outside that approver list to begin with.

### Verification

`node --check` on `Code.gs` and on `Dashboard.html`'s extracted
`<script>` block, a duplicate function/variable-declaration scan (none
found), and an `id="..."` duplicate scan across the full HTML (none
found) --- all run before saving, matching this project's existing
verification convention.

## Sept 2026, twenty-fourth round: Country flag priority chain corrected for OTHER people's rosters + one shared `personFlagHtml()` helper across every Classroom-related listing

Follow-up to the twenty-third round's Default Country feature: that
round fixed the priority chain (browser-detected → Default Country →
none) for the **viewer's own** header badge, but the separate,
pre-existing (seventeenth-round) per-roster-person flags --- shown next
to every OTHER teacher/student's name on a class card --- still only
ever used that person's browser-detected country, with no fallback to
their own saved Default Country. This round closes that gap, and extends
the same flag consistently to the one other Classroom-related listing
that was missing it (the Student Onboarding Status page's Teacher
column), via one new shared helper on each side.

**`Code.gs`**: - `resolveCountryFlag_(entry)` --- a new, small pure
function that takes ONE already-fetched `USER_COUNTRY_PROP_KEY` map
entry and applies the requested priority chain: browser-detected
(`entry.countryCode`/`countryName`) → saved Default Country
(`entry.defaultCountryCode`/`defaultCountryName`) → no flag. This is the
reusable core both of the functions below call. -
`getUserCountryFlag(email)` --- a new top-level convenience wrapper
matching the exact helper name/shape the request asked for ("a reusable
helper function, such as `getUserCountryFlag(email)`"); does one
`getUserCountryMap_()` read for a single email. Meant for one-off
lookups, not a per-row loop. - `applyUserCountry_(courses)` --- now
calls `resolveCountryFlag_()` per person instead of reading
`entry.countryCode` directly, so every teacher/student's flag (shown to
OTHER viewers on class cards and the onboarding Teacher column) now
falls back to that person's Default Country exactly like the viewer's
own badge already did. Still reads the whole map from Script Properties
**exactly once per call**, regardless of how many people are in
`courses` --- no new per-row property reads or API calls, per the
requirement. Also now stamps a new `countrySource`
(`'browser'`/`'default'`/`''`) field alongside the existing
`countryCode`/`countryName`/`countryFlag`, for any future caller that
wants to distinguish the two (not currently rendered anywhere, to keep
this round's visible change minimal).

**`Dashboard.html`**: - `personFlagHtml(countryFlag, countryName)` ---
one new shared helper, used by every Google-Classroom-related
roster/listing that shows a country flag next to a Teacher/Student name.
Returns `''` (renders nothing) when neither a browser-detected nor a
Default Country is known --- never a placeholder/guessed flag. Tooltip
is exactly `"Country: <name>"`, per the request's example. -
`renderPeople()` (every class card's Teacher/Student roster --- the
primary place admin/HM/teacher already saw this) now calls
`personFlagHtml()` instead of building the flag `<span>` inline; visible
behavior is the same as before, except the tooltip text changed from a
bare country name to `"Country: <name>"` and the flag now also appears
(via the `applyUserCountry_()` fix above) for a person who has a Default
Country on file but was never detected by browser. -
`renderGroupTeachers()` (Student Onboarding Status page's Teacher
column) now also calls `personFlagHtml()` before each teacher's name ---
this column previously showed no flag at all. No new server call was
needed: `g.teachers[].countryFlag`/`countryName` were already present on
the same `allCourses` data this page already reads, via
`buildOnboardingGroups()`'s existing pass-through of each course's full
`teachers[]` array. - CSS: `.person-flag` was replaced by
`.aps-country-flag`, using the exact rule the request specified
(`font-size: 0.85em; margin-right: 4px; vertical-align: middle; cursor: help;`)
--- smaller than the adjacent name text, subtle, and inline; no
layout/height change to either the roster chip or the onboarding Teacher
column row. - Scope, per the request's own framing ("Google Classroom
class/member listings"): the Classes-view course-card rosters and the
Onboarding page's Teacher column are the two places a Teacher/Student is
actually listed as a Classroom member. The Class Change Requests cards
and the chat panel show a student's/sender's name too, but as part of a
request-workflow record or a chat message --- not a Classroom membership
listing --- so they were deliberately left out of this round; flagging
this here in case the school wants the flag there as well, since it
would need a small server-side enrichment step those two data sources
don't currently carry. - System/non-person accounts (hidden
admin/support co-teacher logins) never reach `personFlagHtml()` at all
--- they're already filtered out of every teacher roster upstream by the
existing `HIDDEN_TEACHER_NAMES`/`HIDDEN_TEACHER_NAME_PREFIXES` lists,
unchanged. - The viewer's own header badge (`#userCountryFlag`,
`.user-country-flag`) is untouched --- it already had the full priority

## Realtime status updates for all user-actioned statuses (Sept 14, 2026)

The realtime mechanism has been expanded so the same no-flicker behavior applies to **all user-actioned dashboard statuses**, not only Teacher NOT in Class and Needs Tech Support. The lightweight `getRealtimeStatusSnapshot()` endpoint now returns the Live-status map and manual Class Status override map in addition to the existing operational status maps.

Covered statuses:
- **Live / Mark Ended** — manual live changes are mirrored to every open dashboard.
- **Teacher NOT in Class** — all three stages are mirrored to every open dashboard.
- **Needs Tech Support** — all three stages are mirrored to every open dashboard.
- **Class Status** — Cancel Class, Reschedule Class, and Restore Automatic Status are mirrored to every open dashboard.

The client still polls every 2 seconds, but it updates only the affected card/status DOM elements. It does **not** replace the dashboard grid, reset scroll position, clear search text, or show the Loading classrooms screen.

The update applies regardless of whether the viewer is an **Admin, HM, Teacher, or Student**. Existing server-side permission rules remain unchanged; realtime synchronization does not grant any new permissions.

For automatic Meet/Classroom Live detection and the normal automatic Class Status state machine, the existing full dashboard refresh remains authoritative. The realtime endpoint only synchronizes the user-actioned status changes, keeping the polling request lightweight.

## Realtime status channel — all classroom/user activity statuses (Sept 14, 2026)

The latest release extends the lightweight 2-second realtime channel beyond the original operational classroom flags. The browser now polls one small Script-Property snapshot every 2 seconds and updates only the affected DOM elements; it does not call `getDashboardData()`, Classroom API, Meet API, or rebuild the full dashboard.

### Included in the 2-second channel

- Manual Live / Mark Ended status.
- Teacher NOT in Class stages.
- Needs Tech Support stages.
- Manual Class Cancelled / Rescheduled / Restore-to-Automatic status.
- Teacher Weekly Availability for the current Friday-Sunday planning week. Availability remains persisted in `Teacher_Weekly_Availability`; a small Script-Property mirror is updated at the same time so other open dashboards see the change on the next 2-second poll.
- Dashboard online heartbeat/presence.
- Cached Google Meet activity and Google Classroom activity timestamps, plus the permanent GC/GM/DB Last Login record. These are mirrored through the same 2-second channel after the normal Google activity sync updates the server cache.

### Google Meet / Google Classroom status definition

The dashboard must not claim to know whether a Google account is literally signed into Google Meet or Google Classroom, because Apps Script/Admin Reports does not expose a reliable instantaneous account-login boolean for that purpose. The displayed user status therefore means **activity detected**, not merely account sign-in:

- **Meet** = recent Google Meet activity detected by the Admin Reports API.
- **Classroom** = recent Google Classroom activity detected by the Admin Reports API.
- **Online** = dashboard heartbeat, or recent Meet/Classroom activity.

The existing server windows remain authoritative: Meet activity uses the configured `MEET_ACTIVE_WINDOW_MINUTES` window and Classroom activity uses `CLASSROOM_ACTIVE_WINDOW_MINUTES`. The 2-second channel only transports the already-cached result; it does not repeatedly query Google APIs every 2 seconds.

### Performance / no-flicker requirement

The realtime endpoint returns only small Script Property maps. Weekly availability is mirrored into a dedicated realtime property map when the authoritative Sheet is updated. Person-level Meet/Classroom activity is cached during the normal Classroom sync. The client replaces only status badges, weekly availability content, or the affected teacher/student roster DOM inside an existing card. Scroll position, search text, focus, and the rest of the dashboard are not intentionally reset by the realtime channel.

### Important freshness limitation

The **transport** is 2 seconds, but Google Meet/Classroom activity itself is only as fresh as the normal Admin Reports sync that populates the cache. Therefore the dashboard can mirror a newly cached Meet/Classroom activity state within approximately 0–2 seconds, but it cannot guarantee that a newly opened Meet/Classroom session is discovered within 2 seconds. Achieving true sub-second external-source presence would require a source that provides push/presence events rather than the current Apps Script/Admin Reports polling architecture.

## Reference Letter restore + Classes/Onboarding/Search enhancement round (Sept 17, 2026)

This round had two parts, done in this order:

1. **Restore feature parity with production.** The working copy of `Code.gs`/`Dashboard.html`
   had diverged from what's actually live (`CURRENT_PROD_CODE/`) — it was missing the entire
   **Reference Letter** feature (see `APS_Reference_Letter_Feature.md`) that production already
   has, while carrying its own not-yet-deployed On-Call-Teacher/User-Role-Controls work that
   production doesn't have yet. The Reference Letter module (27 functions in `Code.gs`, plus the
   `rl-`-prefixed tab/views/scripts in `Dashboard.html`) was ported back in **additively, verbatim,
   with nothing else rewritten** — this is exactly what that feature's own doc promises ("fully
   isolated, additive module"). Nothing about the working copy's own On-Call-Teacher / User-Role-
   Controls / Class-Status / Teacher-Availability / Student-Onboarding work was touched by this
   step.
2. **Audit + complete the 42-part enhancement request** (On-Call Teacher `tcs_` pattern, Teacher
   Availability, Classes Status filter, Student Onboarding redesign, bilingual English/Tamil
   search, responsive UI, role/permission preservation). Most of this was **already correctly
   implemented** in the working copy before this round started — see the item-by-item status
   below. The real gaps found and fixed were a production-breaking bug and an incomplete search
   integration; everything else was verification only.

### What was found already correct (no code change needed)

- **On-Call Named Teacher** (`ON_CALL_NAMED_TEACHER_EMAIL` / `ON_CALL_ADDITIONAL_NAMED_TEACHER_EMAILS`
  / `isOnCallTeacherEmail_()` in `Code.gs`): the original named account is preserved, every
  `tcs_*@avvaiyarpadasalai.org` address is recognized by prefix (case-insensitive, via
  `normalizeEmail_()`'s `trim()+toLowerCase()`), and `vsugadevsuperadmin@avvaiyarpadasalai.org` is
  already in the additional-names list. `isOnCallTeacherEmail_()` is the single, only place this is
  evaluated — there is no second/conflicting on-call check anywhere else in `Code.gs` or
  `Dashboard.html`.
- **Teacher Availability** (`setTeacherAvailabilityStatus()` in `Code.gs`, `renderAvailEditActions()`
  in `Dashboard.html`): server-side identity comes only from `Session.getActiveUser().getEmail()`
  via `getViewerRole_()` — never a client-supplied email/ID — and only that class's own teacher or
  an Admin/HM can call it successfully. The Confirm/Not-Available buttons are conditionally left out
  of the HTML entirely (`showConfirm`/`showNotAvailable` ternaries), not just `disabled`, so a hidden
  button is truly hidden. A successful update re-fetches `getWeeklyPanelData()` and re-renders just
  the grid (no page reload); a failed update leaves the previous state on screen and shows a toast.
  Status is persisted per-week in the `Teacher_Weekly_Availability` sheet, so it survives
  refresh/re-login. The Classes tab's Teacher-Availability filter reads the same
  `course.teacherAvailabilityStatus` value that this same board computes — one source of truth.
- **Classes Status filter**: the `#classStatusFilter` dropdown already exists, sourced from the same
  `CLASS_STATUS_LABELS` / `applyClassStatus_()` server-side computation used everywhere else status
  is shown (no second status system), combines with every other Classes filter (Teacher Availability,
  Live/No-students/Teacher-not-in-class/Needs-tech-support, and now bilingual search) in one AND'd
  predicate inside `render()`, and none of the filter change-handlers reset any other filter. Changing
  it never reloads the page.
- **Student Onboarding Status tab**: summary cards already show exactly **Total Students / Students
  Online / Teachers Online / Students Offline (Absent)** (`computeOnboardingSummary()` in
  `Dashboard.html`) — "Students Pending" and "Students Not Onboarded" are not shown. The table
  already has exactly the four required columns — **Class / Section, Teacher and HM Contact,
  Teacher, Students** (see the `<thead>` in `#onboardingView`) — with no `Status` column and no
  `Day: AllDay` filter (removed in an earlier round; see the comment above `onboardingGradeFilter`).
  Student de-duplication within a classroom is handled in `renderGroupStudents()`. Everything is
  derived client-side from the same already-loaded, role-filtered `allCourses` the Classes tab uses
  — no per-student or per-classroom API calls, no repeated Classroom/presence fetches, no full
  dashboard reload on filter/search.
- **Role/permission architecture** (`roleCan()` in `Dashboard.html`; `getViewerRole_()`,
  `requireDashboardMutationPermission_()`, `getDashboardRolePermissions()` /
  `saveDashboardRolePermissions()` in `Code.gs`): Admin/HM/Teacher/Student/`VCFO_AMCHSTS_BOD`/Super
  Admin are all preserved, `VCFO_AMCHSTS_BOD` remains read-only with no admin controls and no User
  Role Controls tab access, and every mutation path re-derives the caller's identity/role
  server-side rather than trusting the client. This is one single permission system — the new
  Status filter and Student Onboarding changes read from it (`roleCan('seeClassStatusFilter')`
  etc.), they don't add a second one.

### What was actually broken or incomplete, and the fix

1. **Critical bug — `debounceSearch` was called but never defined.** `Dashboard.html` wired the
   Student Onboarding search box with
   `document.getElementById('onboardingStudentSearch').addEventListener('input', debounceSearch(function (e) {...}))`,
   but no `function debounceSearch` existed anywhere in the file. Since this line runs synchronously
   inside the page's main setup IIFE — **before** the final login/session-validation call at the very
   end of that same IIFE — this would throw `ReferenceError: debounceSearch is not defined` on every
   page load and silently abort the rest of that IIFE, including the code that signs the viewer in.
   In other words: as committed, this would have broken the dashboard for every user on next deploy,
   not just the Onboarding search box. **Fixed** by adding a real `debounceSearch(fn, wait)`
   (trailing-edge debounce, default 300 ms) next to the other search utilities.
2. **Bilingual (English/Tamil) search existed as a solid utility, but two of the highest-traffic
   search boxes weren't actually using it.** `normalizeSearchText()` / `romanizeTamilForSearch()` /
   `personMatchesSearch()` were already correctly implemented (NFKC normalization, Tamil→Latin
   romanization for symmetric matching, partial/substring matching, memoized/bounded caches — see
   "Bilingual search implementation" below) and already wired into the Student Onboarding search box
   — but the main Classes search box (`#search`, placeholder already said "English or Tamil") and the
   separate "Find a Student" box inside Classes (`#studentSearch` / `studentQuery`) were still doing
   a **plain `.toLowerCase().indexOf()` substring check**, so a Tamil-script query would never have
   matched an English-stored name there (or vice-versa), despite the UI promising otherwise. **Fixed**
   by extracting the shared comparison primitive out of `personMatchesSearch()` into
   `bilingualTextMatches_(value, normalizedQuery, romanizedQuery)` (same rules, just reusable) and
   routing both boxes through it: course name + every teacher's name in the main search, and
   `personMatchesSearch()` (name/englishName/tamilName) for the per-class student-name search. The
   query's own normalize/romanize keys are computed once per `render()` call, not once per
   course/teacher, since the underlying functions are already memoized by raw input string anyway.
3. **The Classes search input wasn't debounced.** Added
   `document.getElementById('search').addEventListener('input', debounceSearch(render))` (300 ms) —
   consistent with the Onboarding search box and with the "debounce 250–400 ms, don't refilter every
   keystroke" performance requirement, now that the match itself does a bit more work than a plain
   substring check.
4. **No distinct empty-state message for the Status filter.** `render()` showed the same generic
   "No classes match." for every empty-result case. Added a `classStatusFilter`-specific branch that
   shows "No classes found for the selected status." when the Status filter is the active filter and
   nothing matches it.
5. **Minor responsive gaps.** `.toolbar` (Classes tab search + filter row) had `flex-wrap` but no
   ≤640px full-width-stacking rule the way `.report-filters` (Onboarding tab) already did — added a
   parallel rule so the Status/Teacher-Availability filters don't crowd into odd-width chips on a
   phone. `.view-tabs` had no overflow handling; with the two new Reference Letter tabs, a staff
   account can now see up to 8 tabs, which could overflow a narrow screen — added
   `overflow-x: auto` on the tab bar itself (with `flex: 0 0 auto; white-space: nowrap;` on each tab)
   so the **tab bar** scrolls horizontally on a phone instead of the whole page, or tabs
   wrapping/overlapping/getting clipped.

### Bilingual search implementation (English + Tamil), for reference

- **Normalization** (`normalizeSearchText()`): Unicode NFKC, lower-cased, curly quotes stripped,
  runs of punctuation/whitespace collapsed to one space, trimmed. Tamil code points
  (`஀`–`௿`) are preserved through this step.
- **Romanization** (`romanizeTamilForSearch()`): reduces Tamil script to a rough Latin comparison
  key (e.g. "ராஜலட்சுமி" → "rajalakshmi") so a Tamil-typed query can match a Latin-stored name and
  vice-versa, without needing two separately-maintained name fields. Deliberately collapses
  distinctions English spelling doesn't reliably preserve (ள/ல → l, ற/ர → r, ண/ந/ன → n) — this is a
  search comparison key only, never shown to anyone.
- **Priority**: the actual stored value(s) are always searched first — `person.name`,
  `person.englishName`, `person.tamilName` where a record has them. Nothing here invents or
  overwrites a name; transliteration only **expands what a query is compared against**, it never
  changes what's displayed. (Today, the Classroom roster only carries a single `name` per person —
  there is no separate stored Tamil-name field yet — so in practice this matches whichever script the
  account's real name happens to be in, in either typing direction, via the romanization step. If a
  separate authoritative Tamil-name field is added later, `personMatchesSearch()` already checks
  `person.tamilName` with no further change needed.)
- **Partial matching** is preserved (`String.indexOf()`, not an exact-match check), so "Raja" matches
  "Rajalakshmi" and "ராஜ" matches "ராஜலட்சுமி".
- **Deduplication**: matching is a boolean per-record test (`bilingualTextMatches_`/
  `personMatchesSearch` returns true/false for one record), so a record that matches through both
  its English and Tamil representations still contributes exactly one row/card — there's no
  intermediate result list where the same person could appear twice.
- **Performance**: everything is local/client-side against already-loaded data — no translation
  API call, no extra Classroom request, for any keystroke. Both `normalizeSearchText()` and
  `romanizeTamilForSearch()` memoize by their exact raw input string in a size-bounded cache
  (`SEARCH_CACHE_MAX`), and every free-typing search box now runs through `debounceSearch()`
  (300 ms default) so a fast typist re-filters once per pause, not once per keystroke.
- **Where it's wired**: `personMatchesSearch()` for the Student Onboarding search and the per-class
  student search inside Classes; `bilingualTextMatches_()` directly for the main Classes
  class-name/teacher-name search. This is one shared implementation, not a per-tab copy.

### Security

- No change to the security model. Every mutation in the ported Reference Letter module re-derives
  identity from `Session.getActiveUser().getEmail()` (never a client-supplied value) and re-checks
  role/approver-list membership server-side (`submitReferenceLetterRequest`,
  `submitAdminInitiatedReferenceLetter`, `decideReferenceLetterStage1`,
  `decideReferenceLetterFinalApproval`) — see `APS_Reference_Letter_Feature.md` §15 for the full
  model, none of which was altered by this port.
- The Reference Letter Approvals tab's client-side Admin check
  (`updateReferenceLetterTabVisibility()`) intentionally checks `role === 'admin'` only — **not**
  `'superadmin'` — because the module's own server-side checks
  (`getReferenceLetterRequestsForApprover()` / `submitAdminInitiatedReferenceLetter()`, both
  untouched, verbatim from production) only recognize `'admin'`. Widening the client-side check
  without a matching server-side change would just show a Super Admin a panel whose actions the
  server would then reject. This is a known, pre-existing scope limit carried over unchanged from
  production, not a regression introduced here.
- Bilingual search introduces no new attack surface: it's a pure client-side string comparison over
  data the viewer was already authorized to see; it never sends search text to a server or third
  party.

- `Code.gs` (merged, 5,467 lines): parsed successfully with `node --check` (as `.js`); function-name

- `appsscript.json`: valid JSON; already includes the `drive`/`documents` OAuth scopes the Reference

- `CURRENT_PROD_CODE/` was only ever read from, never written to, in this round — the production

- Diff-reviewed the final `Code.gs`/`Dashboard.html` against the pre-this-round working copy: the

## Sept 2026, twenty-sixth round: On-Call Teachers shown inside every classroom card

### What changed

Every classroom card now shows a new "On-Call Teachers:" roster row, positioned between the
existing "Teacher(s):" and "Students (...):" rosters — matching the ordering in the feature
request:

```
Teachers:
<photo> <flag> Sugadev Velayutham [APS8086] 09/17 19:21 (DB)

On-Call Teachers:
<photo> <flag> Vasali S [TCS] [APS8086] & 3+ Teachers(4 total)

Students (...):
<photo> <flag> JESWITHA EZHUMALAI [APS3250] 09/17 19:21 (DB)
```

The row shows one randomly-selected on-call teacher (their photo, country flag, name, and
`[APSID]`), a `[TCS]` badge when that person's own email starts with `tcs_`, and — only when more
than one on-call teacher exists — a trailing `& N+ Teachers(M total)` summary, where `M` is the
total on-call teacher count and `N = M − 1`. The whole row (including its section label) is omitted
entirely on any card when there is no on-call teacher configured at all, mirroring how the
pre-existing top-of-page on-call banner already hides itself.

### Design decision: dashboard-wide data, reused on every card (not computed per-course)

"On-call teacher" was already a dashboard-wide concept in this codebase, not a per-classroom one:
`getOnCallTeachers_()` reads one small Script-Property-cached directory (populated by
`syncClassroomData()` from every course's teacher list, deduplicated by email — see
`onCallTeacherCandidates` in `buildCourseRecord_()`), and `getDashboardData()` already picked ONE
random entry from it per request, exposing it dashboard-wide as `currentUser.onCallTeacher` /
`currentUser.onCallTeacherCount` for the existing top banner.

Rather than inventing a new, course-scoped notion of "on-call for this specific class" (which the
underlying data doesn't actually support — the on-call directory has never been tied to individual
courses), this round reuses that exact same single random pick on every card. This keeps the change
strictly additive and free of any new Classroom API calls, Sheet reads, or per-course computation —
consistent with the "strong focus on performance" instruction. If Avvaiyar Padasalai's actual intent
is a genuinely course-scoped on-call teacher (a different on-call roster per class), that is a
materially different feature — it would need on-call assignments to be recorded per-course
somewhere (a new Sheet column, most likely) — and is flagged below for a product decision rather
than guessed at silently.

### Code changes (both surgical additions to existing functions/files — nothing removed)

**`Code.gs`:**

- `buildCourseRecord_()`: the existing `onCallTeacherCandidates.push({...})` (already run per
  on-call teacher found in each course's roster, purely to build the sync-time dedup directory) now
  also captures `photo: fixPhoto_(t.profile.photoUrl)` — the photo URL was already being fetched two
  lines below for the normal teacher-roster entry, so this adds no extra API call, just carries the
  same value into the on-call candidate object too.
- `getDashboardData()`: right after the existing `ctx.onCallTeacher` random-pick logic, the single
  featured on-call teacher is now decorated with `countryCode`/`countryName`/`countryFlag` (via the
  same `resolveCountryFlag_()` + `getUserCountryMap_()` every other roster entry already uses — just
  applied to one person instead of iterating a whole course's rosters) and `isTcs` (true when
  `normalizeEmail_(email)` starts with `'tcs_'`, computed once server-side via the same pattern
  `isOnCallTeacherEmail_()` already uses, rather than re-deriving it from a raw email string on the
  client).

**`Dashboard.html`:**

- New CSS: `.person-tcs-badge` (small filled pill, styled consistently with the existing
  `.person-apsid` badge) and `.oncall-extra-count` (small italic gray text, styled consistently with
  the existing `.login-time` treatment).
- New `renderOnCallRoster()`: builds the single on-call teacher's avatar/flag/name/`[APSID]`/`[TCS]`/
  extra-count markup, reusing the existing `personFlagHtml()` and `escapeHtml()` helpers — kept as a
  dedicated function rather than folded into the shared `renderPeople()` roster renderer, so there is
  zero risk of changing the existing, working Teacher/Student roster output.
- New `renderOnCallRosterSection()`: wraps `renderOnCallRoster()` with its
  `<div class="section-label">On-Call Teachers:</div>` label, or returns `''` (label included) when
  there's no on-call teacher — so `renderCard()` can inline one call with no extra conditional at the
  call site.
- `renderCard()`: one new line inserted between the Teacher roster block and the Student roster
  block, calling `renderOnCallRosterSection()`. No existing line in `renderCard()` was changed.

### Caveat: photo may be blank until the next sync for on-call teachers already cached

Any `tcs_*` (or named) on-call account whose directory entry was written to the Script Property
cache by a `syncClassroomData()` run *before* this change is deployed will not have a `photo` field
yet (the cache only picks up the new field the next time that account is seen in a course roster
scan). The `<img onerror="this.style.visibility='hidden'">` already used everywhere else in this
codebase handles that gracefully — the row still renders with the flag/name/badges, just without an
avatar — and self-heals automatically on the very next scheduled sync (`SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES`) or an
immediate manual Force Sync. No action is required, but it's worth knowing this if the on-call row
looks slightly different for the first few minutes after deploying.

### Bug found and fixed while touching this code: two roles silently got no "This Week" panel

While updating the role-display code above, `renderWeeklyInline()` (the per-card "This Week — Class
Teacher Availability" block) was found to gate its entire body on
`role === 'admin' || role === 'headmaster' || role === 'teacher'` — omitting `superadmin` AND
`vcfo_amchsts_bod` entirely. Both of those roles fell straight through to the function's final
`return '';`, meaning a Super Admin or BOD-AMCHATS viewer saw **no** "This Week" panel on any card
at all. A nested `if (role === 'vcfo_amchsts_bod') { ... }` branch already existed just inside that
outer condition — clearly written to give BOD-AMCHATS a read-only, edit-actions-free version of the
panel — but could never run, since the outer condition excluded that very role. This is unreachable
dead code, not something newly introduced this round (confirmed absent from `CURRENT_PROD_CODE`
entirely — the whole `vcfo_amchsts_bod` role predates this codebase's production snapshot and was
added in an earlier working-tree round), but it sits squarely inside the role-handling code this
round touches, so it was fixed rather than left in place: the outer condition now also includes
`superadmin` and `vcfo_amchsts_bod`. Super Admin now gets the same full edit-actions view as
Admin/Headmaster/Teacher; BOD-AMCHATS gets the pre-existing (previously unreachable) read-only view.

### Design decision: Admin/Super Admin membership stays constant-only, not UI-assignable

The "Dashboard User Roles & Permissions" panel's role dropdown offers BOD-AMCHATS, Headmaster,
Teacher, and Student — deliberately **not** Admin or Super Admin. `saveDashboardUserRole()` also
explicitly rejects assigning `'admin'` or `'superadmin'` to any email not already on the
corresponding hardcoded list. This was already the case before this round and was kept as-is: letting
a spreadsheet row grant Admin or Super Admin access would be a privilege-escalation path that
defeats the point of hardcoding those two lists in `Code.gs` in the first place. The request's
phrasing ("add the email to VCFO_AMCHSTS_BOD_ROLE, admin, HEADMASTER") is satisfied for BOD-AMCHATS
and Headmaster via this UI; Admin (and Super Admin) membership is managed by editing `ADMIN_EMAILS` /
`SUPERADMIN_EMAILS` directly in `Code.gs` — which is exactly what this round did, from the literal
arrays supplied in the request.

### Google Classroom teacher/student fallback — confirmed unchanged

`getViewerRole_()`'s fallback order — Super Admin → BOD-AMCHATS → Admin → Headmaster → any
Sheet-configured role override → **Classroom-derived Teacher/Student** → Authorized APS user → none
— was already exactly what was requested ("other users get role from the google classroom") and was
not touched by this round; verified by reading the function in full before and after all edits above.

## Sept 2026, twenty-eighth round: On-Call Teachers roster now picks independently per classroom, with a tooltip listing who else is on call

### What changed

The previous round's per-card "On-Call Teachers:" roster (added twenty-sixth round) showed the exact
same single, dashboard-wide random pick on every classroom card — refreshing the page could change
who was shown, but at any given moment every card agreed. This round makes that pick independent
per course:

- **`Code.gs`'s `getDashboardData()`**: every entry in `getOnCallTeachers_()`'s small cached
  directory is now decorated with its country flag and `[TCS]` flag up front (previously only the
  one dashboard-wide `ctx.onCallTeacher` pick got this treatment). Then, for each course in
  `ctx.courses`, an independent `Math.floor(Math.random() * onCallTeachers.length)` pick sets
  `course.onCallTeacher`, `course.onCallTeacherCount`, and a new `course.onCallOtherNames` — the
  names of every OTHER on-call teacher besides the one picked for that course, for the client's new
  tooltip. The pre-existing dashboard-wide `ctx.onCallTeacher` / `ctx.onCallTeacherCount` pick is
  unchanged and still feeds only the original top-of-page banner — this round didn't touch that.
  Still zero extra Classroom API calls: everything here operates on the same small, already-cached
  on-call directory (a handful of entries), so the added cost is a handful of `Math.random()` calls
  and array filters per course — negligible even with a large number of classes.
- **`Dashboard.html`'s `renderOnCallRoster()`**: now takes the course object `c` and reads
  `c.onCallTeacher` / `c.onCallTeacherCount` / `c.onCallOtherNames` instead of
  `currentUser.onCallTeacher` / `currentUser.onCallTeacherCount` — so each card renders its own
  course's independent pick. The existing top-of-page banner (`renderOnCallTeachers()`, reading
  `currentUser.onCallTeacher`) is untouched and still shows the one dashboard-wide pick, as before.
- **Tooltip**: the "& N+ Teachers(M total)" pill now carries a `title` attribute — hovering it (or
  long-pressing on mobile) shows "Other on-call teachers: <name>, <name>, ..." for every on-call
  teacher besides the one shown on that card. Built server-side from `course.onCallOtherNames` so
  the client never needs the full on-call directory, just what's already on the course object.

### Design notes

- "Google profile and country details" — the on-call teacher's photo and name were already sourced
  from the real Google Classroom teacher profile (`t.profile.photoUrl` / `t.profile.name.fullName`
  in `buildCourseRecord_()`, unchanged since the twenty-sixth round), and country flag/name already
  went through the same `resolveCountryFlag_()` every other roster entry uses. Nothing needed to
  change there beyond what already existed — this round's actual work was making the pick
  per-course and adding the tooltip.
- The random pick is independent per course, not forced-distinct across cards. With typically only
  a handful of on-call teachers configured (5, as of the twenty-seventh round) against potentially
  dozens of classes, forcing every card to show a different person isn't meaningful — most cards
  would still have to repeat someone. "Random per classroom" was read as "each card independently
  samples the on-call pool," which is what's implemented; occasional coincidental repeats between
  two cards are expected, not a bug.
- Every course's pick (and the dashboard-wide banner pick) is re-rolled on every `getDashboardData()`
  call, i.e. every poll — so which on-call teacher shows on a given card can change between refreshes.
  This was already true of the dashboard-wide pick before this round; it now also applies
  independently per card.

### Validation performed this round

- `Dashboard.html`'s inline `<script>` block: re-parsed successfully with `node --check`.
- Full `Dashboard.html`: re-passed the tag-balance check.
- Function-name audit against `CURRENT_PROD_CODE`: zero new function names introduced this round
  (both edits are inside existing functions — `getDashboardData()` and `renderOnCallRoster()`/
  `renderOnCallRosterSection()`, which already existed from the twenty-sixth round); no duplicate
  function names in either file.
- `CURRENT_PROD_CODE/` was only read from again this round, never written to.

  if you'd rather it also show each person's `[APSID]` or `[TCS]` status inline in the tooltip text
  (not just on the one featured person), that's a small follow-up change to how
  `course.onCallOtherNames` is built.

## Sept 2026, twenty-ninth round: new "Alternative: On-Call Assigned" Class Teacher Availability status

### What changed

A fourth "Not Available" arrangement was added alongside the existing three (Parent-Teacher
Arranged, Sub-Teacher Arranged, Need HM Support): **"Alternative: On-Call Assigned"** — for the
specific case where the primary teacher is on leave, the Headmaster has talked to one of the on-call
teachers (the same VCFO_AMCHSTS_BOD_EMAILS / `tcs_*` on-call directory the per-classroom On-Call
Teachers roster reads from), and that on-call teacher has been assigned to cover this one class for
this week only.

- `Code.gs`'s `AVAILABILITY_ALTERNATIVE_LABELS` gained a fourth key, `on_call_assigned`. The
  validation error message in `setTeacherAvailabilityStatus()` was updated to list all four options.
- `Dashboard.html`'s `AVAIL_ALT_LABELS` gained the matching client-side entry, so it appears as a
  fourth button alongside the other three arrangement options once a class is marked "Not
  Available" and expanded.
- **Its own distinct badge color**, per the request ("different color code"): a new `--purple`
  CSS variable and `.avail-status-badge.st-oncall-assigned` class (🟣, `#7c3aed` on `#f3e8fd`). Every
  other "Not Available + arrangement" combination still shares the single amber
  `st-arranged`/🟡 badge they always have — only this new one gets its own color, so it stands out
  at a glance from the other three arrangements, not just from plain "Not Available"/"Available".
  `availabilityStatusInfo()` (client) special-cases `row.alternative === 'on_call_assigned'` ahead of
  the generic "any alternative → amber" fallback to pick this new color.

### Who can set it vs. who can see it — reused the existing gate, no new permission code

The request specified "HM, ADMIN, TEACHER only update this status, other all user roles should view
this status." This is already exactly how every Class Teacher Availability status/arrangement
change works in this codebase — nothing new needed to be built for permissions specifically:

- **Setting it** — `setTeacherAvailabilityStatus()` (server) already only allows staff
  (`isAdminOrHm_()`: Admin, Headmaster, or Super Admin) or that specific class's own Teacher
  (`isOwnClass`) to change ANY availability status or arrangement, this new one included. Super
  Admin wasn't named in the request but is included here for the same reason it's included in every
  other admin-tier check in this codebase (`isAdminOrHm_()`) — excluding just the highest-privilege
  role from something Admin can do would be an inconsistent, likely-unintended restriction, so it
  was left in rather than special-cased out.
  `roleCan('manageTeacherAvailability')` (client, a pure convenience mirror — the server above is
  the real gatekeeper) already matches: Admin/Headmaster/Super Admin, or Teacher for their own class.
- **Viewing it** — the status badge (icon + color + the "Alternative: On-Call Assigned" text itself,
  via `altLabel`) is built once in `renderWeeklyInline()`, BEFORE the function branches by role, and
  every branch that returns anything (Admin/HM/Teacher/Super Admin's full edit view, BOD-AMCHATS's
  read-only view, and Student's feedback-only view) includes that same badge. So every role that can
  see a class's "This Week" panel at all already sees this new status the same way — no additional
  client-side visibility change was needed.

`isOnCallTeacherEmail_()` already treats ANY email starting with `tcs_` as an on-call teacher

## Sept 2026, thirty-second round: Class Teacher Availability "set time" now shown in the school's fixed Eastern timezone, not the viewer's browser-local timezone

### Problem fixed

The user asked to "check the Class Teacher Availability set time." Investigation found the
timestamp shown for when a Class Teacher Availability status was last set/updated was being
formatted using the **viewer's browser-local timezone**, not the school's fixed timezone. Two
spots in `Dashboard.html` were affected:

1. `formatAvailabilityStamp(updatedByName, updatedAt, altText)` — built the compact "MM/dd
   HH:mm:ss" stamp shown under each class's availability badge using `new
   Date(updatedAt).getMonth()/.getDate()/.getHours()/.getMinutes()/.getSeconds()`, all of which
   read the browser/device's local clock and timezone.
2. The `statusTitle` tooltip built inside `renderWeeklyInline(c)` — used `new
   Date(weekRow.updatedAt).toLocaleString()`, same underlying problem (browser-local, and also
   locale-dependent formatting).

This meant a Teacher/HM/Admin viewing the dashboard from a different timezone than the school's
(America/New_York) would see an availability "set at" time that didn't match Eastern time — e.g.
a status set at 9:00 PM ET could display as a completely different hour to a viewer elsewhere.

This is the same class of bug the codebase already solved correctly elsewhere: `Last Login` times
are formatted **server-side** via `formatLastLoginTimestamp_()` (Code.gs) using
`Utilities.formatDate(d, LAST_LOGIN_TIMEZONE, 'MM/dd HH:mm')` with `LAST_LOGIN_TIMEZONE =
'America/New_York'`, and the client already has its own correct pattern for the exact same fixed
timezone via `isTodayInAPSTimezone()`, which uses `Intl.DateTimeFormat(..., { timeZone: APS_TZ
})` with `APS_TZ = 'America/New_York'` (both existed before this round; neither was touched).
Both availability-timestamp spots were simply written before that convention was consistently
applied to every timestamp in the app.

### Implementation

- Added one new shared helper in `Dashboard.html`, `formatAPSTimestamp_(isoOrDate, withYear)`,
  right above `formatAvailabilityStamp()`. It uses `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with `timeZone: APS_TZ`
  (the same existing constant `isTodayInAPSTimezone()` already relies on) to render a timestamp
  in the school's fixed Eastern time regardless of the viewer's own timezone, with `hour12: false`
  and a "24" → "00" midnight normalization for engines that report it that way. `withYear` toggles
  between a compact `MM/dd` (matches the availability footer's pre-existing format) and a full
  `MM/dd/YYYY` (matches what the tooltip's old `toLocaleString()` showed). The result is always
  suffixed `" ET"`, matching the app's existing convention for other Eastern-time displays (e.g.
  "Scheduled start: ... ET").
- `formatAvailabilityStamp()` now calls `formatAPSTimestamp_(updatedAt, false)` instead of doing
  its own browser-local date-math.
- The `statusTitle` tooltip line in `renderWeeklyInline(c)` now calls
  `formatAPSTimestamp_(weekRow.updatedAt, true)` instead of `new
  Date(weekRow.updatedAt).toLocaleString()`.
- This is purely a **client-side, additive** fix — no change to `Code.gs`. The raw `updatedAt`
  value the server already sends (an ISO timestamp) didn't need to change; only how the client
  renders it needed fixing, consistent with how `isTodayInAPSTimezone()` already handles the same
  kind of value client-side.

### Related bug noticed but NOT fixed this round (flagged for a future round if wanted)

While tracing every timestamp-formatting call site in `Dashboard.html`, `formatLoginTime(iso)`
(used by `renderStatusBadgeGroup()` for the "Live", "Teacher NOT in Class", and "Needs Tech
Support" status badges) was found to have the **exact same bug** — it also uses `new
Date(iso).getMonth()/.getHours()` etc., reading the viewer's browser-local timezone rather than
`APS_TZ`. This is a separate feature from Class Teacher Availability and outside what was asked
this round ("check the Class Teacher Availability set time" specifically), so it was left
untouched to keep this round's change surgical and scoped to exactly what was requested. Flagging
it here in case the user wants the same fix applied to those badges in a future round.

### Validation performed this round

- `Dashboard.html`'s longest inline `<script>` block extracted and re-parsed successfully with
  `node --check` (as `.js`) — zero syntax errors.
- Tag-balance check (Python `html.parser`-based open/close stack tracker) run against the full
  file: zero errors, empty stack at EOF.
- Function-name audit (`grep -oE 'function [A-Za-z0-9_]+'`) diffed against
  `CURRENT_PROD_CODE/current_dashboard.html`: the only genuinely new name introduced is
  `formatAPSTimestamp_` itself (the new shared helper); every other name in the diff is a
  pre-existing addition from earlier rounds in this session, not a new or duplicate function
  introduced now.
- Confirmed both call sites (`formatAvailabilityStamp()`, and the `statusTitle` line inside
  `renderWeeklyInline()`) were updated and no other Class Teacher Availability timestamp-display
  code path was missed (grepped every `updatedAt` reference in the file).
- `Code.gs` was not touched this round; `CURRENT_PROD_CODE/` was only read from, never written to.

  compact `MM/dd HH:mm:ss` shape (now with `" ET"` appended); the tooltip now shows a full
