## Sept 2026, thirty-third round: "Hide/Show" toolbar toggle for Headmaster/Admin/support-staff accounts on every classroom roster, plus GC/GM Last Login exclusion for those same accounts

### Request

Since these staff accounts are added to many Google Classrooms and Google Meets purely for
day-to-day oversight (not because they're that specific class's actual teacher), the user asked
for: (1) a Hide/Show button that hides a named list of staff accounts from every classroom's
Teacher/Student roster, for every viewer role; (2) for those same accounts, stop capturing their
Google Classroom ("GC") / Google Meet ("GM") activity in the "Last Login" record, while continuing
to capture their direct Dashboard ("DB") sign-ins normally; and (3) explicitly not to change the
existing `HEADMASTER_EMAILS`/`ADMIN_EMAILS` rosters — the supplied hide-list simply reuses those
emails plus five new ones.

### Who is hidden

`ROSTER_HIDDEN_STAFF_EMAILS` (Code.gs) = `HEADMASTER_EMAILS` (6, unchanged) + `ADMIN_EMAILS` (5,
unchanged) + `ROSTER_HIDDEN_STAFF_ADDITIONAL_EMAILS` (5 new support-staff accounts:
`akarunambikai_aps774@…`, `kalaivani_aps884@…`, `parthanvu_aps620@…`, `anithav_aps822@…`,
`geetha_aps629@…`) — 16 accounts total. This concatenates the existing constants directly rather
than hand-copying their addresses into a third list, so editing `HEADMASTER_EMAILS`/`ADMIN_EMAILS`
later automatically keeps this feature's hide-list in sync — there's no second place to remember
to update. The Super Admin account (`vsugadevsuperadmin@avvaiyarpadasalai.org`) was NOT included —
the user's supplied list didn't name it, so it stays fully visible everywhere as before.

### Implementation — roster Hide/Show

- **Toggle, not a permanent hide.** Unlike the pre-existing `isHiddenTeacherName_()`/
  `HIDDEN_TEACHER_*` mechanism (baked into the Classroom-sync cache at `buildCourseRecord_()` time,
  permanent, no way to turn it back on without editing code and re-syncing), this is a genuine
  Hide/Show **toggle**: a single persisted flag (`ROSTER_HIDDEN_STAFF_VISIBLE_PROP_KEY`, a Script
  Property, default = hidden) read fresh by `getRosterHiddenStaffVisible_()` and flipped by
  `setRosterHiddenStaffVisible(visible)` (Admin/Super Admin only — same `isAdminRole_()` gate as
  "Assign Classroom"/"Deployment Info").
- **Request-time filter, not sync-time.** `applyRosterHiddenStaffFilter_(courses)` runs inside
  `getDashboardData()`, immediately after courses are read from the cache and BEFORE
  `applyLivePresence_`/`applyLastLogin_`/`applyUserCountry_` decorate every person — so when the
  toggle is set to "Hide" (the default), a hidden account's roster entry is filtered out before any
  of that per-person decoration work even runs on it. This is the ONLY way to support a true,
  instant toggle button: baking the filter into the sync cache instead would mean "Show" couldn't
  take effect without a Force Sync (which consumes Classroom API quota and is explicitly marked
  "DO NOT USE" except for tech support). Toggling costs zero Classroom API calls either direction.
- `applyRosterHiddenStaffFilter_()` recomputes `noTeacher`/`noStudents`/`studentCount` (derived
  purely from the filtered array lengths) so those badges match what's actually displayed, but
  deliberately does NOT touch `live`/`liveSource`/`studentsInMeetCount` (computed once at
  Classroom-sync time from the FULL roster) or `onCallTeacherCandidates` (already stripped before
  the cached record is written). **Design decision flagged below.**
- O(1) lookup: `ROSTER_HIDDEN_STAFF_EMAIL_SET_`, a plain object keyed by normalized email, built
  ONCE at script-load time from `ROSTER_HIDDEN_STAFF_EMAILS` — `isRosterHiddenStaffEmail_(email)`
  is a single object-key check, not an array `.some()`/`.indexOf()` scan repeated for every
  teacher/student on every course on every request. Given the "strong focus on performance"
  request, this was deliberately chosen over reusing the existing `isInEmailList_()` helper (which
  is `O(n)` per call and is fine for the small, rarely-called role checks it's used for elsewhere,
  but would add up here — this filter runs across every teacher+student, on every course, on every
  `getDashboardData()` call, which fires on every dashboard load and every 1-minute quiet refresh
  for every open dashboard).
- `getDashboardData()`'s returned `ctx` now also carries `ctx.rosterHiddenStaffVisible` (the
  current toggle state) — piggy-backed onto the payload every call already returns, rather than a
  separate `google.script.run` round trip just to read one boolean.
- **Dashboard.html**: a new toolbar button, `toggleHiddenStaffBtn`, placed right after "Force Sync"
  — visible only to Admin/Super Admin (`updateHiddenStaffToggleVisibility()`, same `isStaff` rule
  as `updateForceSyncVisibility()`, called from both `load()` and the quiet-refresh handler so the
  button's visibility/label stay current even during a background poll). Its label toggles between
  "🙈 Staff Hidden From Rosters (click to Show)" and "👁️ Staff Shown In Rosters (click to Hide)"
  (`renderHiddenStaffToggleLabel()`), driven by `currentUser.rosterHiddenStaffVisible` — no extra
  round trip needed just to render the button correctly. Clicking it calls
  `setRosterHiddenStaffVisible(nextVisible)` then re-runs `load()`, so every already-open card
  reflects the new state immediately, for that user; every OTHER open dashboard picks it up on its
  own next `load()`/quiet-refresh (up to ~1 minute later, same latency as every other Script
  Property-backed toggle in this app — e.g. the Teacher NOT in Class / Needs Tech Support flags).

### Implementation — GC/GM Last Login exclusion, DB unchanged

- `getMeetPresenceMap_()` and `getClassroomActivityMap_()` (Code.gs) each build a
  `{ email: latestTimestamp }` candidate map before calling `mergeLastLoginActivity_(candidates,
  'gm'|'gc')` — the single place either source ever writes into the persistent, cross-source Last
  Login record (`LAST_LOGIN_PROP_KEY`). Both now skip any email in `ROSTER_HIDDEN_STAFF_EMAILS`
  (via `isRosterHiddenStaffEmail_()`) before building that candidate map, so their GC/GM activity
  is never merged into the Last Login record at all — one `if (isRosterHiddenStaffEmail_(email))
  return;` guard added to each of the two existing `Object.keys(...).forEach(...)` loops that were
  already building those candidate maps; no new loop, no new API call.
- The `presence`/`activity` maps those two functions RETURN (used for the per-course "in Meet" /
  "in Classroom" badges and `isLive` auto-detection) are NOT filtered — only the separate Last
  Login merge is. So a hidden account's Meet/Classroom presence still legitimately marks a class
  "Live" if that's genuinely what's happening; only their Last Login timestamp stops being polluted
  by that same activity. **Design decision flagged below.**
- `recordHeartbeat_()` (the 'db' slot) was NOT touched — it already unconditionally records every
  Dashboard visit regardless of who it is, which is exactly "CAPTURE DB details" with zero code
  change needed.

### Design decisions flagged for confirmation

1. **"Hide from roster" does not mean "exclude from Live detection."** A hidden account's genuine
   Meet/Classroom activity still counts toward a class showing "Live" — hiding them from the
   visible Teacher list is a display/privacy choice, not a claim that their presence never
   happened. If the intent was instead "these accounts' activity should never make a class look
   Live," that's a different, larger change (touching `buildCourseRecord_()`'s sync-time
   `autoLiveMeet`/`autoLiveClassroom` computation) and wasn't made here — flagging for explicit
   confirmation either way.
2. **Toggle gated to Admin + Super Admin**, not Super-Admin-only. Unlike the twenty-seventh round's
   role/permission-management panel (explicitly restricted to Super Admin only, per that round's
   request), this toggle follows the same, more common `isAdminRole_()` gate already used by
   "Assign Classroom" and "Deployment Info" — a routine operational display switch, not a
   security-sensitive role assignment. Happy to narrow it to Super-Admin-only if that's preferred.
3. **Filters both `teachers` AND `students` arrays**, even though every one of the 16 listed
   accounts is realistically a staff/oversight account rather than an actual student. Kept
   symmetric (cheap, no behavior risk) since the request said "hide … from the APS dashboard for
   all the users" generically, not "from the Teacher roster" specifically.
4. **Quiet-refresh latency for OTHER open dashboards.** The user who clicks the button sees the
   change instantly (an explicit `load()` right after the toggle call succeeds); everyone else's
   already-open dashboard picks it up on its own next quiet refresh (currently every 1 minute) —
   same behavior as every other Script-Property-backed live toggle already in this app.

### Validation performed this round

- `Code.gs`: re-parsed successfully with `node --check` (as `.js`).
- `Dashboard.html`'s longest inline `<script>` block: re-parsed successfully with `node --check`.
- Tag-balance check (Python `html.parser`-based open/close stack tracker): zero errors, empty
  stack at EOF.
- Function-name audit (`grep -oE 'function [A-Za-z0-9_]+'`) diffed against
  `CURRENT_PROD_CODE/current_prod_code.gs` and `current_dashboard.html`: the only genuinely new
  names introduced this round are `applyRosterHiddenStaffFilter_`, `getRosterHiddenStaffVisible_`,
  `isRosterHiddenStaffEmail_`, `setRosterHiddenStaffVisible` (Code.gs) and
  `renderHiddenStaffToggleLabel`, `updateHiddenStaffToggleVisibility` (Dashboard.html); every other
  name in the diff is a pre-existing addition from earlier rounds this session, not a new or
  duplicate function introduced now. Zero duplicate top-level `function` declarations in either

- Confirmed via `sed`/`grep` that `ADMIN_EMAILS` and `HEADMASTER_EMAILS` are byte-for-byte
  unchanged from before this round, per the explicit "dont change" instruction.
- Ran a standalone Node.js harness reproducing `ROSTER_HIDDEN_STAFF_EMAILS`/
  `ROSTER_HIDDEN_STAFF_EMAIL_SET_`/`normalizeEmail_` to confirm: the combined list is exactly 16
  emails (6 + 5 + 5); the trailing-space `'principal@avvaiyarpadasalai.org '` variant from the
  pasted list normalizes and matches correctly; and the Super Admin account correctly does NOT

- `CURRENT_PROD_CODE/` was only read from again this round, never written to.

### Self-review — flag before shipping

- The three design decisions above (Live-detection interaction, Admin+SuperAdmin gate rather than

## Sept 2026, thirty-fourth round: REGRESSION FIX — Teacher Weekly Availability showing "Not Set" for every teacher (wrong spreadsheet)

### Problem reported

Every teacher's Class Teacher Availability status was displaying as "Not Set", even though the
user confirmed the school's spreadsheet (`1rlFMiXDMVaBcZS89AL0OC5TYeXz4PIZyXXboYoDGzX0`) visibly
has data in its `Teacher_Weekly_Availability` tab. The user pasted the exact line they suspected:

```javascript
var TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID = PropertiesService.getScriptProperties().getProperty('TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID');
```

### Root cause

Confirmed by diffing against `CURRENT_PROD_CODE` (the read-only production reference this project
always compares against): production's equivalent line is the plain hardcoded literal —

```javascript
var TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID = '1rlFMiXDMVaBcZS89AL0OC5TYeXz4PIZyXXboYoDGzX0';
```

— while the working tree had that hardcode commented out and replaced with a
`PropertiesService.getScriptProperties().getProperty('TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID')` lookup. That Script
Property was never actually set in the live Apps Script project, so `TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID`
evaluated to `null`/empty at runtime. `getWorkbook_()` (Code.gs) branches on exactly this value:
when it's truthy it opens that spreadsheet; when it's falsy, it silently falls through to its OTHER
branch — reusing (or auto-creating) a completely different spreadsheet via the separate
`CACHE_SHEET_ID_KEY` property. Every Sheet-backed tab this project uses (`Courses` cache,
`Teacher_Weekly_Availability`, `Dashboard_Chat_Window`, `WhatsApp_Group_Links`,
`Dashboard_User_Roles`, etc.) is read/written through this one `getWorkbook_()` call, so this one
`null` silently redirected ALL of them to the wrong spreadsheet.

**Why only Teacher Weekly Availability looked broken, and nothing else did:** the `Courses` cache
tab in that OTHER (wrong) spreadsheet still looked "fine" because `syncClassroomData()` keeps
refreshing it straight from the Classroom API every `SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES`, into whatever
workbook `getWorkbook_()` currently resolves to — so classes/rosters kept working normally, just
silently pointed at a different underlying spreadsheet than the one the school actually looks at.
Teacher Weekly Availability, by contrast, is USER-ENTERED data — a teacher clicking Confirm/Not
Available. Every one of those clicks was being written into that same wrong spreadsheet, while the
REAL spreadsheet's `Teacher_Weekly_Availability` tab kept only whatever historical data was already
there from before this regression — so reading the CURRENT week from the real spreadsheet correctly
found nothing for anyone, and defaulted to "Not Set" for every teacher, every class, exactly as
reported. (This was NOT a bug in `getCurrentWeekId_()`'s Friday-Sunday week-boundary math, which was
double-checked and confirmed still correct — the lookup key was fine; it was looking in the wrong
spreadsheet entirely.)

### Fix

Restored `TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID` to the literal hardcoded ID — byte-for-byte identical to
`CURRENT_PROD_CODE`'s line, and matching the exact sheet ID the user confirmed directly. Removed
the `PropertiesService`-based indirection entirely rather than keeping it as a fallback/override:
matching production exactly is the safest fix here, since that indirection is what caused the
regression and there's no known reason (no round in this session's history added it deliberately)
for the school to need a per-deployment override. `getWorkbook_()` itself, `CACHE_SHEET_ID_KEY`,
and `getCacheSheetUrl()` were NOT touched — they're correct as they stand; only the one value
feeding into them was wrong.

### Validation performed this round

- `Code.gs`: re-parsed successfully with `node --check` (as `.js`).
- Confirmed via `grep` that the restored line is now byte-for-byte identical to
  `CURRENT_PROD_CODE/current_prod_code.gs`'s equivalent line.
- Confirmed via `grep` that no other reference to
  `getProperty('TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID')` remains anywhere in `Code.gs` or `Dashboard.html` (only a
  doc-comment mentioning the removed pattern, for the historical record).
- Function-name audit against `CURRENT_PROD_CODE`: zero new or duplicate function names (this was
  a single variable-value fix — no functions added, removed, or renamed).
- `Dashboard.html` was not touched this round (this bug and its fix are entirely server-side).
- `CURRENT_PROD_CODE/` was only read from again this round, never written to.

### Self-review — flag before shipping

- **This fix only affects requests made AFTER redeploying this file.** Any availability clicks
  teachers made while the regression was live were written into the OTHER (wrong, auto-created or
  reused-via-`CACHE_SHEET_ID_KEY`) spreadsheet, not into
  `1rlFMiXDMVaBcZS89AL0OC5TYeXz4PIZyXXboYoDGzX0`. Those clicks are NOT automatically recovered by
  this fix — if any teacher availability responses were submitted during the regression window and
  are missing from the real spreadsheet now, they may still exist in that other spreadsheet. I
  don't have a way to identify which spreadsheet that was from here (it depends on whatever
  `CACHE_SHEET_ID_KEY` in Script Properties pointed to, or a fresh auto-created one, on the live
  Apps Script project) — happy to help track it down if the user can check Script Properties /
  the list of spreadsheets the script's Google account has recently created, or if they can say how
  long they believe this has been happening (e.g. by checking the earliest date any of the OTHER
  Sheet-backed features look unexpectedly "reset").
- Given how this one regressed, it may be worth the user double-checking their live Apps Script
  project's Script Properties for a leftover `TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID` entry from whenever this got
  introduced — it's now completely unused by this restored code either way, but I can't see or
  clear that property from here (no access to the live Apps Script project, only these files).

## Sept 2026, thirty-fifth round: TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID made self-healing (Script Property, with a guaranteed default)

### Request

Following the thirty-fourth round's regression fix (which restored `TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID` as a
plain hardcoded literal), the user asked to go back to reading it from a Script Property, and to
have the sheet ID actually saved into that property — i.e. keep the configurability of a Script
Property, but this time make sure it's never silently unset the way it was before.

### Implementation

`TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID` is now computed by a new function, `getTargetSpreadsheetId_()`:

1. Reads the `'TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID'` Script Property.
2. If it's already set (non-blank), returns it as-is — this is what lets an Admin later point the
   project at a different spreadsheet (e.g. a separate TEST spreadsheet) just by editing that one
   Script Property in the Apps Script editor's Project Settings, with no code change or redeploy.
3. If it's missing or blank — exactly the failure mode that caused the thirty-fourth round's bug —
   it immediately **saves** `TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID_DEFAULT_` (the same sheet ID confirmed directly
   by the school, matching `CURRENT_PROD_CODE`) into that Script Property, and returns it.

This runs once per script execution, at module load (`var TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID =
getTargetSpreadsheetId_();`), so the very next time this Web App is opened or a trigger fires
after this file is deployed, the Script Property gets durably set — no manual step required in
the Apps Script editor, and no risk of it silently staying unset the way it did before. This
makes the specific failure mode from the thirty-fourth round (a Script Property that's never set,
with `getWorkbook_()` silently falling through to an auto-created spreadsheet) structurally
impossible going forward: there is always either an explicit configured value, or this
known-correct default — never a blank one.

`getWorkbook_()`, `getCacheSheetUrl()`, and every other existing reader of the module-level
`TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID` variable were NOT touched — they still just read that one variable, which
is now guaranteed non-blank by construction.

### Validation performed this round

- `Code.gs`: re-parsed successfully with `node --check`.
- Function-name audit against `CURRENT_PROD_CODE`: the only genuinely new function is
  `getTargetSpreadsheetId_` — no duplicates, nothing else new.
- Ran a standalone Node.js harness with an in-memory `PropertiesService` stand-in to confirm the
  three cases: (1) property unset → returns and saves the known-correct default; (2) property now
  set (from case 1) → returns it without writing again; (3) property manually set to a different
  value (simulating an Admin override, e.g. a TEST spreadsheet) → that override is respected, not
  overwritten.
- `Dashboard.html` was not touched this round — this change is entirely server-side, same as the
  thirty-fourth round's fix.
- `CURRENT_PROD_CODE/` was only read from again this round, never written to.

### Self-review — flag before shipping

- The self-heal only fires the first time this deployed file actually runs (any Web App request or
  trigger firing). It does not retroactively fix anything from before this round — but there's
  nothing to fix retroactively here, since the thirty-fourth round's hardcoded-literal fix was
  already correctly resolving the sheet ID in the meantime; this round only changes HOW that value
  is sourced going forward.
- If the user ever wants to point this at a different spreadsheet (e.g. for testing), they can now
  do that by editing the `TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID` Script Property directly in the Apps Script
  editor (Project Settings > Script Properties) — no file change needed. I still can't see or edit

## Sept 2026, thirty-sixth round: bilingual (English/Tamil) search made consistent everywhere, and the classroom list now always displays in Ascending order

### Request

"All search button should search both english and tamil and sort result by default to Ascending
order. Example: Search String 'Raja' has to search 'Raja' and 'ராஜா' and sort result by Ascending.
Always display all the google classroom in Ascending Order."

### Investigation

The dashboard's bilingual matching primitives (`normalizeSearchText`/`romanizeTamilForSearch`/
`bilingualTextMatches_`/`personMatchesSearch` in `Dashboard.html`) were already correct — traced
the "Raja" → "ராஜா" example character-by-character through the transliteration table and confirmed
a match already succeeds wherever this shared utility is actually called. Auditing every name
search box in the dashboard against that utility found:

- **Main Classes search** (`#search`) — already uses `bilingualTextMatches_` directly. OK.
- **Find a Student** (`#studentSearch` → `studentQuery`) — already uses `personMatchesSearch`. OK.
- **Student Onboarding Status search** (`#onboardingStudentSearch`) — already uses
  `personMatchesSearch`. OK.
- **Assign Classroom student search** (`#assignmentStudentSearch` →
  `renderAssignmentStudents()`) — **was the one genuine gap.** It used a plain
  `.toLowerCase().indexOf()` substring match on `s.name`/`s.email` only, so "Raja" would never find
  a student whose Google account name was stored as "ராஜா". The doc comment above
  `bilingualTextMatches_` claiming this utility already backs "Assign Classroom" was inaccurate.
- `apsCountrySearchInput` / `countryModalSearchInput` (country pickers) and `kbSearch` (Knowledge
  Base video title/description search) are not person-name searches and were left as-is — out of
  scope for this request.

Separately, on ordering: the main classroom grid's order came entirely from the server
(`getDashboardData()` in `Code.gs`), which sorted Live classes first, then No-Students classes
first, and only used the class name as a final tie-breaker — not pure ascending. The client's
`render()` filters `allCourses` for search/filter but never re-sorts, so this server order was
exactly what got displayed by default and for every search result.

### Implementation

- **`Dashboard.html` — `renderAssignmentStudents()`**: now filters via
  `personMatchesSearch(s, qRaw) || s.email.toLowerCase().indexOf(qLc) > -1` instead of the old
  English-only substring check on `s.name`, so it matches the same English/Tamil rules as every
  other name search box. The email substring match is kept as-is (email addresses are never
  Tamil-script). Results are also now explicitly sorted ascending with the existing
  `naturalCompare()`.
- **`Code.gs` — `getDashboardData()`**: `courses.sort()` now reads
  `courses.sort(function (a, b) { return naturalCompareJs_(a.name, b.name); });` — **replacing**
  the previous Live-first / No-Students-first prioritization entirely, per the user's explicit,
  repeated instruction ("Always display all the google classroom in Ascending Order"). Reuses the
  existing numeric-aware `naturalCompareJs_` (already shipped in production for other lists) so
  e.g. "NILAI - 10" still sorts after "NILAI - 2" rather than before it.
- **`Dashboard.html` — `render()`**: added a defensive `list.sort(function (a, b) { return
  naturalCompare(a.name, b.name); });` immediately after the search/filter chain and before
  rendering. The server already returns ascending order, so this is redundant today — it exists so
  the grid can never silently drift out of Ascending order even if a future code path ever feeds
  `render()` courses in a different order.
- **`Code.gs` — `getAdminClassroomAssignments()`**: its existing `students`/`classes` sorts were
  upgraded from plain `localeCompare` to `naturalCompareJs_`, for the same numeric-awareness and
  consistency with the rest of the dashboard's Ascending-order lists. This wasn't reported broken;
  it's a consistency pass while already touching Assign Classroom.

### Validation performed this round

- `Code.gs`: re-parsed successfully with `node --check` (via a temporary `.js` copy, since Apps
  Script's `.gs` extension isn't a Node-recognized module type).
- `Dashboard.html`: HTML tag-balance re-checked (Python `html.parser`-based checker) — balanced.
  The inline `<script>` block's JS was extracted and re-parsed successfully with `node --check`.
- Function-name audit against `CURRENT_PROD_CODE_REF`: no functions added or removed this round —
  every function touched (`getDashboardData`, `getAdminClassroomAssignments`,
  `renderAssignmentStudents`, `render`) already existed; only their sort/filter logic changed. The
  diff against production shows only the same accumulated set of prior-round additions as before
  (e.g. `applyRosterHiddenStaffFilter_`, `getTargetSpreadsheetId_`, etc.) — nothing new, nothing
  missing.
- Ran a standalone Node.js harness re-implementing the exact bilingual-match and natural-sort logic
  to confirm: (1) "Raja" matches a student stored as "ராஜா"; (2) "Raja" does NOT falsely match an
  unrelated student; (3) the reverse direction also works — typing "ராஜா" matches a student stored
  as "Raja Kumar"; (4) the Assign Classroom email substring match still works independently of the
  name match; (5) natural/ascending sort correctly orders "NILAI - 2" before "NILAI - 10" and
  "Grade 9" before "Grade 10". All five checks passed.

### Self-review — flag before shipping

- **Behavior change, not just a bug fix**: the main Classes grid no longer bubbles Live classes or
  No-Students classes to the top. Every classroom now appears in one continuous alphabetical (well,
  natural-numeric) list. This was a deliberate removal of an earlier, undocumented-in-this-round
  prioritization, done because the user's wording was explicit and repeated ("Always... Ascending
  Order"), not because the old behavior was a bug. If Live-first was actually still wanted
  alongside Ascending naming (e.g. Live classes first, then alphabetical within each group), that's
  a different, narrower request — let me know and I'll adjust.
- The Assign Classroom fix only helps because student records only ever populate `.name`
  (`englishName`/`tamilName` are not actually used anywhere server-side despite
  `personMatchesSearch()`'s doc comment implying they might be) — so the fix is "route through the
  same single-name bilingual matcher," not "backfill separate English/Tamil name fields." This
  matches how every other search box in the dashboard already works.
- As with every prior round, this is untested against the live Google Classroom/Sheets data — it's
  only been validated by static analysis and a standalone logic harness that mirrors the real
  functions line-for-line. Please redeploy (Deploy > Manage deployments > Edit > New version) and
  spot-check: the Assign Classroom student search with a Tamil-named student, and the main Classes
  grid's default order, before considering this round done.

## Sept 2026, thirty-seventh round: Nilai + Class Time dropdown filters added to the Classes tab

### Request

Add two new dropdown filters to the Classes tab — Nilai (12 exact values: All, MUNMAZHALAI,
MAZHALAI, NILAI 1–8, THULIR(துளிர்)) and Class Time (6 exact values: All + the 5 fixed weekly
slots) — combined via AND with every existing Classes-tab filter, with no change to existing
sorting, permissions, performance, or mobile behavior.

### Investigation — how Nilai/Class Time actually live in the data today

Before writing any matching logic, traced every existing per-course field this school's data
already has:

- `course.name` and `course.section` come straight from the Google Classroom API, untouched
  (`buildCourseRecord_` in `Code.gs`: `name: course.name, section: course.section || ''`).
- `course.section` is **not** a reliable source for Class Time. A prior round (see "Display Google
  Classroom Section values..." above) repurposed this school's Section field as school-entered free
  text (e.g. an HM contact line) — it can hold anything, not necessarily a time.
- `parseCourseSchedule_(rawName)` (existing, used for Class Status) already reads the day/time out
  of `course.name` — e.g. `"NILAI 99 - SA | TUE 11:30 AM - 12:30 PM EST | AY26-27"` — but returns
  parsed `{dayOfWeek, start:{hour,minute}, end:{hour,minute}, timezoneRaw}` components for status
  math, not a ready-made exact display string to compare against a dropdown value.
- `buildOnboardingGroups()` (Student Onboarding Status tab, `Dashboard.html`) groups by
  `c.name`/`c.section` under the labels "grade"/"time", but per the point above, `c.section` is no
  longer a dependable time source dashboard-wide — this existing grouping was left completely
  untouched (out of scope; it wasn't reported broken).

Conclusion: there is no existing structured Nilai/Class-Time field to reuse, so — per the request's
own fallback instruction — both values are safely derived from `course.name`, independently of
`parseCourseSchedule_()` (neither function calls the other; `parseCourseSchedule_()`'s behavior is
completely unchanged).

### Implementation

**`Code.gs`** — four new functions, added together right after the existing
`parseCourseSchedule_()`/`inferMissingMeridiem_()` cluster (same "derive from course.name" family),
plus one new call in the existing `getDashboardData()` pipeline:

- `NILAI_FILTER_OPTIONS` / `CLASS_TIME_FILTER_OPTIONS` — the exact dropdown value lists, in the
  exact required order, as the single source of truth both the extraction functions and the (by-hand
  mirrored) `Dashboard.html` `<option>` lists are checked against.
- `extractNilaiFromCourseName_(rawName)` — reads the segment of the course name before the first
  `"|"` (the same convention `parseCourseSchedule_()` already relies on for the segment *after* it).
  Exact-match safety, in order: (1) a literal Tamil `"துளிர்"` match short-circuits to
  `"THULIR(துளிர்)"` first; (2) whitespace/punctuation is stripped to a compact uppercase token so
  `"MUN MAZHALAI"` and `"MUNMAZHALAI"` compare equal; (3) `"MUNMAZHALAI"` is checked **before** the
  plain `"MAZHALAI"` substring check, so `"MUNMAZHALAI"` (which contains `"MAZHALAI"` as a substring)
  can never be mis-tagged as plain `"MAZHALAI"`; (4) an English `"THULIR"` check; (5) a
  `/NILAI(\d+)(?!\d)/` match — the trailing `(?!\d)` means `"NILAI 1"` can never absorb an extra
  digit and get confused with `"NILAI 10"` — and the captured number is only accepted if
  `"NILAI " + number` is one of the 8 valid dropdown values (so e.g. `"NILAI 99"` correctly yields no
  match rather than a fabricated one).
- `normalizeClassTimeText_(raw)` — normalizes en/em-dash/minus-sign characters to a plain hyphen and
  collapses whitespace (including around the dash), so `"FRI  6:30–8:00   PM EST"` and
  `"FRI 6:30 - 8:00 PM EST"` compare equal. Never touches letters or digits.
- `extractClassTimeFromCourseName_(rawName)` — checks whether one of the 5 exact
  `CLASS_TIME_FILTER_OPTIONS` strings (both sides normalized the same way) appears **verbatim** in
  the segment between the first two `"|"` characters (falling back to the whole name, same
  fallback `parseCourseSchedule_()` already uses). Because the whole day+start+end+meridiem+timezone
  string must match exactly, there is no partial/similar-time match path at all — this is the
  request's own "no partial/similar time" requirement satisfied structurally, not by extra
  bookkeeping.
- `applyNilaiAndClassTimeFilters_(courses)` — the new decoration pass, in the same style as the
  existing `applyClassStatus_`/`applyLastLogin_`/etc.: attaches `course.nilai` and
  `course.classTime` to every course, read-only from `course.name`, no Classroom/Sheets/API call.
  Wired into `getDashboardData()` right after the existing `applyWhatsAppLinks_(courses);` line, one
  new line only: `applyNilaiAndClassTimeFilters_(courses);`. Nothing else in `getDashboardData()` —
  including the round-36 Ascending sort immediately below it — was touched.
- `getAdminClassroomAssignments()`'s existing `courses.map(...)` → `getViewerContext_()` plumbing
  passes course objects straight through by reference, so `nilai`/`classTime` reach the client on
  every course exactly like `classStatus`/`teacherAvailabilityStatus` already do — confirmed by
  reading `getViewerContext_()` end to end; no serialization step strips unlisted fields.

**`Dashboard.html`**:

- Two new `<select>` elements, `#classesNilaiFilter` and `#classesTimeFilter`, added to the Classes
  tab's `.toolbar` immediately after `#search` — matching the requested
  `Search | Nilai | Class Time | Existing Filter 1 | ...` layout. Options are the exact required
  values, in the exact required order, hardcoded (not built from data) exactly as specified. Visible
  to every role (no `roleCan()` gate, unlike `#classStatusFilter`/`#teacherAvailabilityFilter`) since
  the request didn't ask for role restriction.
- Two new state variables, `classesNilaiFilter`/`classesTimeFilter` (both `''` = "All"), declared
  next to the existing `classStatusFilter`/`teacherAvailabilityFilter`.
- Two new lines in `render()`'s existing filter chain: `if (classesNilaiFilter && (c.nilai || '') !==
  classesNilaiFilter) return false;` and the equivalent for `classesTimeFilter` — added right after
  the existing `teacherAvailabilityFilter` check, ANDed with every other check in the same chain
  exactly like every filter already there. This is a pure additive filter on the existing, already-
  loaded `allCourses` array (`Array.filter()`), so it costs nothing extra: no new server call, no
  new dataset copy, and — critically — `Array.filter()` only ever removes non-matching elements
  without reordering the survivors, so the round-36 Ascending order (or any future sort) is
  automatically preserved through this filter with zero extra code.
- Two new `change` event listeners (mirroring the existing `classStatusFilter`/
  `teacherAvailabilityFilter` listeners exactly), and both new filters added to the existing
  `#clearFilters` click handler (reset to `''`, select `.value` reset to `''`) — no second/duplicate
  reset mechanism created.
- `updateRealtimeCardDom()` (the lightweight per-card DOM patch that runs after every 2-second
  real-time status poll) was deliberately **not** touched: it only needs to re-check filters whose
  underlying value can change via that poll (`live`, `classStatus`, `teacherAvailabilityStatus`) —
  `course.nilai`/`course.classTime` are derived once from the immutable course name and never change
  between full `render()` calls, so there is no case where this function needs to reconsider them.
- CSS: one new rule, `.toolbar select { padding: 8px 10px; border: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-radius: 8px; background: white; cursor: pointer; font-size: 13px; }`, matching the existing
  `.report-filters select` look. This also fixes up the two pre-existing, previously-unstyled
  `#classStatusFilter`/`#teacherAvailabilityFilter` selects to match — a small, intentional visual
  consistency improvement, not a functional change. No new media query was needed: the existing
  `@media (max-width: 640px) { .toolbar input[type="text"], .toolbar select, .toolbar button {
  flex: 1 1 100%; min-width: 0; } }` rule already targets every `.toolbar select`, so the two new
  dropdowns inherit the existing "stack to full width, no horizontal overflow" mobile behavior
  automatically.

### Validation performed this round

- `Code.gs`: re-parsed successfully with `node --check` (temporary `.js` copy).
- `Dashboard.html`: HTML tag-balance re-checked — balanced. Inline `<script>` JS extracted and
  re-parsed successfully with `node --check`.
- Function-name audit against `CURRENT_PROD_CODE_REF`: zero functions removed relative to
  production; exactly 4 new functions added (`applyNilaiAndClassTimeFilters_`,
  `extractClassTimeFromCourseName_`, `extractNilaiFromCourseName_`, `normalizeClassTimeText_`) —
  nothing else changed name or disappeared.
- Ran a standalone Node.js harness (21 checks, all passing) re-implementing
  `extractNilaiFromCourseName_`/`extractClassTimeFromCourseName_`/the combined-filter logic
  line-for-line, covering: every course-name example given in the request; the explicit
  anti-confusion cases (`NILAI 1` vs `NILAI 10`, `MAZHALAI` vs `MUNMAZHALAI`, `THULIR` in both
  scripts, an out-of-range `NILAI 99`); Acceptance Tests 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 from the request, run as
  actual assertions against a small simulated course list; and that filtering a pre-sorted list
  never reorders the survivors (`Array.filter()` semantics).
- Tests 5 (combined with every other existing filter), 7 (mobile) and 8 (refresh) were verified by
  code review rather than a runtime harness (this environment has no live Classroom data or
  browser): Test 5 holds because the two new checks are two more ANDed lines in the exact same
  filter chain every existing filter already uses — nothing about how they combine differs from
  `classStatusFilter`/`teacherAvailabilityFilter`. Test 7 holds because the new selects are plain
  `<select>` children of `.toolbar`, already covered by the pre-existing mobile stacking rule. Test 8
  holds because `course.nilai`/`course.classTime` are recomputed fresh on every `getDashboardData()`
  call (same as every other decoration), so a refresh/reload re-derives them from whatever
  `course.name` currently is — nothing is cached or left stale from a prior load.

### Self-review — flag before shipping

- **Assumption, stated explicitly**: `NILAI 9` and above (only 1–8 are in the required dropdown)
  and any course name that doesn't match this school's `"<GRADE> | <DAY> <TIME> | <SUFFIX>"`
  convention simply gets `course.nilai = ''`/`course.classTime = ''` — such a course stays visible
  under "All" but will never appear under a specific Nilai/Class-Time selection. This matches the
  request's own instruction to derive safely from the existing naming convention rather than
  guessing, but means any course whose title doesn't follow that convention (a typo, a one-off
  differently-named class) is effectively unfilterable by these two new dropdowns until its name is
  corrected in Google Classroom. This is a data-quality dependency, not a code bug.
- The Nilai/Class Time filters are visible to every role, including Teacher/Student (who typically
  only see their own 1–2 courses anyway, since `getViewerContext_()` already scopes `courses` per
  role before these filters ever run) — the request didn't ask for role gating, so none was added,
  unlike the Admin/HM-only `classStatusFilter`/`teacherAvailabilityFilter`. Easy to add a
  `roleCan()` gate later if that turns out to be unwanted.
- As with every prior round, this has been validated by static analysis and a standalone logic
  harness only — please redeploy (Deploy > Manage deployments > Edit > New version) and spot-check
  the two new dropdowns against real class names, especially any course whose title doesn't
  perfectly follow the `"NILAI - N - SECTION | DAY TIME EST | AYxx-xx"` convention.

Move the existing Live Only / No Students Only / Teacher NOT in Class / Needs Tech Support /

toggle controls — no logic, counts, permissions, or sorting changes, and no duplicate controls.

### Implementation — `Dashboard.html` only (`Code.gs` untouched this round)

**HTML**: the single `.toolbar` div (Classes tab) was split into two. Row 1 keeps `search`,
`classesNilaiFilter`, `classesTimeFilter`, `teacherAvailabilityFilter`, `classStatusFilter`, and
`clearFilters`. Row 2 (`<div class="toolbar classes-status-toolbar">`) got the 7 controls named in
the request, moved — not duplicated — out of Row 1: their exact same `id` attributes, `title`
attributes, and `style="display:none;"` role-gating hooks came with them unchanged. Confirmed by
grep that every one of the 7 ids still appears in the HTML exactly once, and every one still has
exactly one `addEventListener` registration, both unchanged from before this round.

Row 2 keeps the `toolbar` class alongside its own new `classes-status-toolbar` class specifically so
every pre-existing `.toolbar`-scoped rule (button/select sizing, `flex-wrap`, and — most importantly
— the existing `@media (max-width: 640px)` mobile-stacking rule) keeps applying to it automatically,
with zero new mobile-specific CSS needed.

**Visual separation**: `.classes-status-toolbar` is a `var(--card)` (white) panel with a
`var(--border)` outline and rounded corners, sitting on the page's `var(--bg)` background — the same
"card floats on bg" contrast `.summary .chip` already uses elsewhere in this file, reused rather
than inventing a new visual language. Row 1's own `.toolbar { margin-bottom: 18px; }` already
supplies the vertical gap between the two rows.

**Color coding** (`:root` — 7 new tint variables added: `--green-bg`, `--red-bg`, `--amber-bg`,
`--purple-bg`, `--blue-bg`, `--gray-bg`, plus one new solid `--neutral-dark: #3c4043` since no
existing variable was dark enough for the requested "Neutral/Dark gray"). Every other color is the
EXISTING `--green`/`--red`/`--amber`/`--purple`/`--blue`/`--gray` variable — nothing new was invented
where an existing one already fit, per the request's own instruction:

| Control | Assigned color | Inactive (subtle) | Active (strong) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Live Only | green | `--green-bg` tint, `--green` border/text | solid `--green`, white text (unchanged from before) |
| No Students Only | amber | `--amber-bg` tint, `--amber` border/text | solid `--amber`, white text (**changed from red**) |
| Teacher NOT in Class | red | `--red-bg` tint, `--red` border/text | solid `--red`, white text (unchanged from before) |
| Needs Tech Support | purple | `--purple-bg` tint, `--purple` border/text | solid `--purple`, white text (**changed from blue**) |
| Refresh | blue | n/a (one-shot action) | solid `--blue`, white text — already exactly this via the pre-existing `.primary` class; untouched |
| DONOTUSE($$) | neutral dark gray | n/a (one-shot action) | solid `--neutral-dark`, white text (**changed from a hardcoded inline red `#d93025`**) |
| Hide/Show HM-ADMIN | gray/slate | `--gray-bg` tint, `--gray` border/text | solid `--gray`, white text (**new — was completely unstyled before**) |

No Students Only and Needs Tech Support's *active*-state colors were changed (amber and purple,
replacing red and blue) directly in the two pre-existing
`.toolbar button#filterNoStudents.active`/`#filterNeedsTechSupport.active` rules — same selectors,
same `.active` class `updateFilterButtons()` already toggles, only the color values changed. Live
Only and Teacher NOT in Class needed no change; they already matched the requested colors.
`#forceSync`'s hardcoded inline `style="...background:#d93025;..."` was removed from the HTML
entirely and replaced with the new `.classes-status-toolbar #forceSync` CSS rule — the element's
`style="display:none;"` attribute (the one piece `updateFilterButtons`'s sibling function actually
toggles via `el.style.display = ...`) was kept, since a CSS class rule and one remaining inline
`display` property don't conflict.

**Active/inactive without relying on color alone**: every one of these controls already carries a
persistent text label (e.g. "Live only", or "👁️ Hide HM/ADMIN" vs "🙈 Show HM/ADMIN" — two DIFFERENT
strings, not just a recolored dot), so the color coding above is a visual reinforcement layered on
an already-accessible state indicator, never the only signal. For the 4 filter-toggle buttons, the
active/inactive CSS split on the EXISTING `.active` class costs zero new JS — `updateFilterButtons()`
was not touched. For Hide/Show HM-ADMIN specifically (which had no `.active` class before), one line
was added to the existing `renderHiddenStaffToggleLabel()`: `btn.classList.toggle('active',
!visible);` — "active" (strong gray fill) means hiding is currently ON, matching the same toggle
pattern the other four buttons already use; the actual hide/show behavior in that function was not
touched.

**CSS specificity, verified rather than assumed**: the new base-state rules
(`.classes-status-toolbar #filterLive`, etc. — 1 class + 1 id) and the pre-existing/updated
`.active` rules (`.toolbar button#filterLive.active` — 2 classes + 1 id + 1 element) both match a
button when it's active; the `.active` rule is unconditionally more specific (2 classes beats 1) so
it always wins and shows the solid color, regardless of source order in the stylesheet. When NOT
active, the `.active` rule's selector simply doesn't match at all, so only the base tint rule
applies. This was worked out by specificity arithmetic, not by trial and error.

### Validation performed this round

- `Dashboard.html`: HTML tag-balance re-checked — balanced. Inline `<script>` JS extracted and

- Grepped every one of the 7 moved-control ids: exactly one HTML occurrence and exactly one

- `Code.gs`: untouched this round (confirmed via checksum) — this was a pure `Dashboard.html`

- Manually re-derived the CSS specificity of the old `.active` rules vs. the new base-tint rules

"Also show the filter to all the user roles BOD,SuperAdmin,Admin,HM. For student role display only

Read `roleCan()` and `updateFilterButtons()` end to end before changing anything, to avoid

  (`filterLive`/`filterTeacherNotInClass`/`filterNeedsTechSupport`) were **already** gated to

## Sept 2026, forty-first round

**Request (verbatim):** "All 6:30 PM EST Classes are started and running in google meet. but
status is displayed as Yet to Start. live status also not captured."

This is a bug report, not a spec — so this round started with diagnosis, not a code change.

### Diagnosis

Built a standalone Node.js harness that re-implements `parseCourseSchedule_`,
`inferMissingMeridiem_`, `parseClockTime_`, `easternDayOfWeek_`, `easternWallTimeToDate_`, and
`computeAutomaticClassStatus_` line-for-line (using `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with
`timeZoneName: 'shortOffset'` to emulate Apps Script's DST-aware `Utilities.formatDate`), and ran
it against the exact course-name format this school uses — `"NILAI - 8 - XX | FRI 6:30 - 8:00 PM
EST | AY26-27"` — at a simulated "now" of Friday 7:00 PM Eastern (mid-class). Result: the schedule
parsed correctly (`{dayOfWeek:5, start:{hour:18,minute:30}, end:{hour:20,minute:0}}`), the Eastern
UTC offset resolved correctly (`-04:00`, EDT), and `computeAutomaticClassStatus_` correctly returned
`{code:'started'}` when `anyoneInMeet=true` and `{code:'yet_to_start'}` when `anyoneInMeet=false`.
All 5 checks passed. **Conclusion: the day/time/DST parsing logic is correct and is not the cause.**
The bug is upstream of that function, in whatever feeds `anyoneInMeet` — i.e. in Meet-presence
detection.

Traced `anyoneInMeet` (in `applyClassStatus_`) back to `c.teachers[].inMeet` /
`c.students[].inMeet`, which are stamped in `buildCourseRecord_` from `getMeetPresenceMap_()`'s
presence map. Two structural facts matter here:

1. **`getMeetPresenceMap_()` is only called from `syncClassroomData()`** (the time-driven sync
   job), never from the per-request `getDashboardData()`. So "who's in Meet" is only as fresh as
   the last sync cycle — `SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES = 15` — not recomputed live on every dashboard
   view. (I initially wondered whether the web app's `"executeAs": "USER_ACCESSING"` setting could
   make this call run as a non-admin viewer and silently fail on permissions — checked and ruled
   that out: time-driven triggers always execute as the trigger's owner/authorizer, regardless of
   the web app's `executeAs` setting, which only governs `doGet`/`google.script.run` calls.)
2. **`getMeetPresenceMap_()` previously swallowed every exception silently** — `catch (e) { return
   {}; }` — so an auth error, a disabled API, a quota issue, or anything else would produce an
   empty presence map (everyone shows "not in Meet") with zero visibility into why.

I can't reach this school's live Apps Script Executions log or Workspace Admin console from here,
and several distinct external causes are all consistent with the symptom: the `syncClassroomData`
trigger not currently installed/firing; the account that owns/authorized the trigger not (or no
longer) being a Workspace Super Admin (the Admin Reports API's `userKey='all'` query requires it);
Meet audit-log reporting being disabled for the domain in the Workspace Admin console; or an
inherent reporting lag in Google's own Admin Reports API (a Google platform limitation, not
something this code can control). Rather than guess at which one applies and "fix" the wrong thing,
this round adds **diagnostics only**, so the next occurrence is actually checkable.

### Implementation — `Code.gs` only, diagnostic-only, no behavior change

- New constant (near `MEET_ACTIVE_WINDOW_MINUTES`): `var MEET_PRESENCE_DIAGNOSTIC_KEY =
  'meetPresenceDiagnostic';`
- `getMeetPresenceMap_()`'s catch block now also logs via `console.error(...)` (visible in the
  Apps Script Executions log) and writes `{at, ok:false, error}` to this Script Property before
  returning `{}` — **the return value and every other behavior is completely unchanged.**
- On the success path, it now also writes `{at, ok:true, accountsWithRecentMeetActivity}` to the
  same property.
- Readable any time from the Apps Script editor's **Project Settings → Script Properties**, without
  digging through logs, to see at a glance whether the last sync's Meet-presence lookup succeeded
  and roughly how much activity it saw.

This does **not** fix an unknown external cause — it makes the next failure (or the current one,
once the next sync runs) visible instead of silent.

- Function-name diff against `CURRENT_PROD_CODE_REF` — zero functions removed or renamed (this
  round only adds one constant and extends one existing function body).
- Standalone Node.js harness (described above) proving the parsing/DST logic is correct — 5/5
  checks passed.

### Self-review — flag before shipping

- **This is diagnostics, not a fix.** The status will very likely still show "Yet to Start"
  incorrectly for the next several sync cycles until the underlying Meet-detection issue is found

## Sept 2026, forty-second round

**Request (verbatim, sent mid-turn while the forty-first round's diagnostics were in progress):**
"I want to update the google classroom status for each claasess 'Class Started' and live status as
per current flow Either any one of the Student or teacher status is (GM) or (GC/GM) in the google
meet. I want to mark class status as 'Class Started' and" [live status captured the same way].

### What was actually found

Re-reading `applyClassStatus_` (Code.gs) turned up something the forty-first round's harness had
already exercised without calling out explicitly: **`anyoneInMeet` — the signal that drives "Class
Started" vs. "Yet to Start" — was already `(teachers).some(inMeet) || (students).some(inMeet)`**,
i.e. it already used the "either the teacher OR any student is in Meet" rule the request asks for.
Class Status needed no change.

**"Live" status was the one place still using the old, narrower rule.**
`buildCourseRecord_`'s `autoLiveMeet` — which drives the green "Live"/"Live (Meet)" badge and the
`Live Only` filter — was `teachers.some(function (t) { return t.inMeet; })`: **teacher-only**, never
checking students. So a class where only students had joined the Google Meet call (teacher not yet
in, or joined from a different device/account not matched to their roster email) would correctly
show "Class Started" but would NOT show as "Live" — exactly the kind of inconsistency the request is
describing ("Either any one of the Student or teacher status is ... in the google meet ... mark
class status ... and [live status]"). Dashboard.html has its own client-side mirror of this same
computation (`updateRealtimePeopleDom`'s `autoMeet`, used for the 1-minute realtime poll without a
full page reload) — it had the identical teacher-only gap.

### Implementation

- **`Code.gs`** — `buildCourseRecord_`: `autoLiveMeet` now reads
  `teachers.some(t => t.inMeet) || students.some(s => s.inMeet)` (was teacher-only). `students` was
  already built earlier in the same function with its own `inMeet` flag (sourced from the same
  `getMeetPresenceMap_()` presence map as teachers), so this is a one-line logic change, no new
  data plumbing. Everything downstream (`isLive`, `liveSource`, `autoLiveClassroom`'s fallback,
  the manual-toggle path) is untouched. Updated the doc comment above `AUTO_LIVE_DETECTION` (which
  previously said "when its teacher is in an active Google Meet call") to describe the corrected
  teacher-OR-student rule and note that it's now intentionally kept identical to
  `applyClassStatus_`'s `anyoneInMeet`.
- **`Dashboard.html`** — `updateRealtimePeopleDom()`: `autoMeet` gets the same fix (`|| (c.students
  || []).some(s => s.inMeet)`), so the 1-minute client-side realtime refresh doesn't regress back to
  teacher-only between full page loads. The separate client-side Class Status mirror
  (`anyoneInMeet` inside the schedule-recompute helper) already had the correct teacher-OR-student
  logic and was not touched.
- No changes were needed to Class Status anywhere (server or client) — it already implemented the
  rule being asked for.

### Validation performed this round

- `node --check` on temp copies of both the `Code.gs` file and the extracted inline `<script>` from
  `Dashboard.html` — both passed.
- HTML tag-balance check on `Dashboard.html` — balanced (0 mismatches).
- Function-name diff of `Code.gs` against `CURRENT_PROD_CODE_REF` — zero functions removed/renamed.
- Standalone Node.js harness reproducing `buildCourseRecord_`'s new `autoLiveMeet` logic with 5
  cases: (1) student-only in Meet (the reported bug) → now correctly Live via 'meet'; (2)
  teacher-only in Meet → still Live via 'meet' (regression check); (3) nobody in Meet but teacher
  has recent Classroom activity → still Live via 'classroom' (regression check, unaffected by this
  round); (4) nobody active → not Live (regression check); (5) one of several students in Meet →
  still Live. All 5 passed.

### Self-review — flag before shipping

- Same underlying data-freshness caveat as round 41: `inMeet` (both teacher and student) is only as
  current as the last 15-minute `syncClassroomData()` run, and — until whatever round 41's
  diagnostics surface gets resolved — is subject to the same "silently empty presence map" risk if
  the Reports API call is failing. This round fixes the teacher-vs-student asymmetry in how that
  presence data is used; it does not change how fresh or reliable the underlying presence data is.
- "(GM)" / "(GC/GM)" in the request refers to the Last Login display labels (`LAST_LOGIN_SOURCE_LABELS`)
  — a slightly different (historical, ever-recorded) signal from the live `inMeet` flag (current,
  within the 180-minute active window as of the last sync). I used `inMeet` here because that's the
  exact signal `anyoneInMeet`/Class Status already keys off of, so Live and Class Status stay
  driven by the same underlying presence data and can't disagree with each other going forward. If
  what's actually wanted is for the Last Login "(GM)"/"(GC/GM)" *label itself* to independently drive
  Live/Class Status, that would be a different, larger change — flagging this interpretation in case

## Sept 2026, forty-third round

**Request (verbatim):** "lets build simple solution to find list Google Classroom is started or
not. if either Teacher or Student Status is DM or DM/DC or DM/DB update the status to Class Started
and Mark as 'Live' current code is displaying this expected result. built simple and power option
to hand this feature." (Read as: "GM" / "GM/GC" / "GM/DB" — the Last Login source labels — and:
the Status column already displays this correctly, so drive Class Started/Live off that same,
already-working signal.)

This followed directly from the screenshot shared earlier in this session: five FRI 6:30-8:00 PM
classes all showing "Yet to Start" with no Live badge, roughly an hour into their scheduled period —
but several people, including one class's own teacher (Farhana Mohideen, "09/18 18:36 (GM)"), had a
Meet event captured just 6 minutes into class. That timestamp proved Google's Reports API access
was working and had captured real Meet activity for this class — yet Class Started/Live never
fired, even after 3+ fifteen-minute sync cycles.

### Root cause, finally isolated

`getMeetPresenceMap_()`'s `presence` map (the thing that actually drives `anyoneInMeet` in
`applyClassStatus_` and `autoLiveMeet` in `buildCourseRecord_`) required a person's **single most
recent Meet event, by timestamp, to be exactly `call_started`** — treating an unmatched, presumed-
still-ongoing call as the only valid "in Meet" signal. Meanwhile, the Last Login "GM" badge (which
the admin was actually looking at) is fed by the exact same underlying event data but merges **any**
event type (`call_started` OR `call_ended`) and never un-sets it. So it's entirely possible — and,
per the screenshot, apparently common — for a person's *visible* GM badge to show fresh activity
from minutes into class while the *specific* event Google's Reports API is currently surfacing as
"latest" for that person is a `call_ended`, not a `call_started` — whether because of a real brief
disconnect, or simply because the API hasn't yet surfaced their newer, still-ongoing `call_started`
(a documented Google-side reporting lag for Meet audit data). Either way, the stricter rule meant
the class could sit on "Yet to Start" for its *entire* period despite obvious, visible Meet activity.

### Implementation — `Code.gs` only, one function

In `getMeetPresenceMap_()`, the `presence` map is now built from **any** recent Meet event
(`call_started` OR `call_ended`) within the existing `MEET_ACTIVE_WINDOW_MINUTES` (180-minute)
lookback — previously it only counted a person whose latest event was specifically `call_started`.
Concretely: the `if (lastEventByEmail[email].type === 'call_started')` guard was removed, so
`presence[email]` is now set unconditionally from `lastEventByEmail[email].time` for every email
with any qualifying event in the window. This is now **the same exact data** already merged into
the Last Login 'gm' slot (both come from the same `lastEventByEmail`), so the Last Login "GM" badge
and the Class Started/Live badges can no longer disagree with each other — which is exactly the
"simple" fix requested: reuse the signal already proven correct on screen, rather than a separate,
stricter detection path.

No other function changed. `buildCourseRecord_`'s `autoLiveMeet`/`applyClassStatus_`'s
`anyoneInMeet` (both already teacher-OR-student as of Round 42) needed no changes at all — they
already consume `presence` as-is, so broadening what feeds `presence` automatically broadens both.
Updated `getMeetPresenceMap_()`'s doc comment and the `MEET_ACTIVE_WINDOW_MINUTES` doc comment to
describe the corrected semantics.

Dashboard.html needed no change this round: its realtime 1-minute poll (`applyRealtimePersonActivity`)
was, on inspection, already computing `meetActive` from the Last Login `gm` timestamp directly (any
event type, same as the badge) rather than from the stricter server-side `presence` rule — so the
client-side path was already implementing the "simple" version being asked for; only the
server-side canonical value (used on full page load and by the 15-minute sync's cached Sheet
record) still had the stricter, narrower rule. This round brings the two into agreement.

### Validation performed this round

- `node --check` on a temp copy of `Code.gs` — passed.
- Function-name diff against `CURRENT_PROD_CODE_REF` — zero functions removed/renamed (one
  conditional deleted inside an existing function; two doc comments updated).
- Standalone Node.js harness reproducing the exact screenshot scenario: a person whose visible
  latest event is `call_ended` 6 minutes into a scheduled class. Confirmed: (1) the OLD logic
  excludes them from `presence` (reproducing the reported bug exactly); (2) the NEW logic includes
  them; (3) a regression case (latest event genuinely `call_started`) is unaffected under both old
  and new logic; (4) feeding the NEW presence value through the existing `anyoneInMeet`/`autoLiveMeet`
  rules confirms both Class Started and Live now flip true for this class. All 6 checks passed.

### Self-review — flag before shipping

- This makes "in Meet" detection deliberately more permissive: a person is now counted as "in Meet"
  for the *entire* 180-minute lookback after ANY Meet event, including one where they've already
  left. In practice this mostly matters for detection to *start* — once a class is marked "Started"
  the existing `CLASS_STARTED_MARK_PROP_KEY` latch already keeps it Started until the 90-minute
  completion mark regardless, so this round mainly widens the *first* trigger, not how long it holds.
  The one edge case worth knowing about: if a teacher or student had an unrelated Meet call earlier
  in the same 180-minute window (e.g. a previous back-to-back class), that stale activity could
  cause a *different, later* class to show as Started/Live a few minutes early, before anyone has
  actually joined the new one. This mirrors an already-accepted, documented limitation of this
  same feature ("can't tell WHICH course a person's meeting belongs to") — not a new kind of risk,
  just a slightly wider version of one already on record.
- This does not touch or improve the underlying Reports API reporting lag itself — it just no
  longer requires the *freshest visible* event to specifically be a start, which is what was
  actually blocking detection in the reported case.
- Not yet viewed against the real Workspace environment. Please redeploy (new Web App version) and
  confirm, at the next class period, that Class Started/Live now appears promptly and matches what
  the Last Login "GM" badges show for that class's roster.

Properties/config (`TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID`'s self-healing pattern, `LAST_LOGIN_TIMEZONE` =
`America/New_York`); timezone helpers (`easternDayOfWeek_`, `easternWallTimeToDate_` — both DST-aware
and reused verbatim); Sheets helpers (`getWorkbook_`, the `getOrCreateXSheet_` idiom, the
batched-read/batched-write convention used throughout, e.g. `writeCache_`,
`readAllReferenceLetterRequests_`); role/permission checks (`getViewerRole_`, `isAdminOrHm_`,
`requireDashboardMutationPermission_`); the roster cache (`readAllCoursesFromCache_()` already returns
every course's full teacher/student list with emails, pre-fetched by the existing 15-minute
`syncClassroomData()` trigger — reused directly so this feature makes **zero** additional Classroom
API calls); the concurrency-safe ID-counter pattern (`generateReferenceLetterRequestId_`'s
`LockService` usage, reused for AWK-number assignment); and the existing trigger bootstrap
(`createSyncTrigger()`'s idempotent install-a-timer pattern, mirrored for this feature's own trigger).
The APS Reference Letter module (its own clearly-banner-commented "fully isolated, additive" section)
was used as the structural template for this new module's isolation discipline.

### Google API / configuration required — not yet in place (identified, not assumed)

1. **The Google Meet API itself is not enabled** for this project's Cloud project, and its required
   scope, `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/meetings.space.readonly`, was not in `appsscript.json`.
   Both are needed for real join/leave data. Added to `appsscript.json` this round (along with
   `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/script.external_request`, required because Apps Script's implicit
   scope detection is bypassed once a manifest explicitly lists `oauthScopes`, and this feature calls
   the Meet REST API directly via `UrlFetchApp` — Meet has no Apps Script Advanced Service). Enabling
   the Meet API itself happens in Google Cloud Console, for this Apps Script project's backing Cloud
   project — that step cannot be done from inside the script and needs a Workspace/Cloud admin. Every
   user will see one new consent-screen line the first time they use the dashboard after this
   redeploys.
2. **The Classroom API's `Course` resource has no field exposing a course's Meet link or space**
   (confirmed against the resource's current schema — `id`, `name`, `section`, `room`,
   `alternateLink`, `calendarId`, etc., nothing Meet-related). There is no way to derive "this
   course's recurring Meet" automatically from Classroom data alone. This round adds a small
   Admin-maintained mapping instead — a new "Course ↔ Meet Link" panel on the new Attendance tab
   where an Admin/HM pastes each course's Meet link (or bare code) once; it's stored in a
   `Course_Meet_Link_Map` sheet and reused every sync, the same "assign once, persist forever"
   philosophy the spec itself asked for the Course→AWK mapping. Until a course is mapped, its full
   roster is still recorded every sync (0 minutes / ABSENT, per requirement 11) with a diagnostic
   note, rather than silently skipped.
3. **Even with the scope and the mapping in place, whether the account this script executes as has
   visibility into every teacher's Meet conference records is a real, untested Workspace question.**
   Google's Meet API generally scopes participant data to spaces the calling identity organized or
   has explicit access to. There is no live Workspace domain or Meet data reachable from this
   environment to verify this end-to-end — if `conferenceRecords.list` comes back empty for a mapped,
   currently-meeting course, that access question is the first thing to check via
   `getAttendanceSyncDiagnostics()`, not assumed to be a bug in this code.
4. **Participant identity resolution**: the Meet API's `Participant.signedinUser.user` field is a
   People-API-style `users/{id}` reference, not a raw email (confirmed against the API reference).
   This round resolves it via `AdminDirectory.Users.get(id)` — the **same** Advanced Service and scope
   (`admin.directory.user.readonly`) this project already uses elsewhere (e.g. its staff display-name
   lookup) — so no *additional* Directory-side setup is needed beyond item 1 above. A participant the
   API can't resolve to a real email (phone/anonymous join) is fetched but not attributable to a
   roster member, and is skipped rather than guessed at.

### What was built

**Code.gs** — one fully isolated, additive module appended after the existing Reference Letter
module (same banner-comment discipline; nothing above it touched):
- Config: `ATTENDANCE_SPREADSHEET_ID`, `ATTENDANCE_SHEET_PREFIX = 'AWK'`, `APS_TZ` (aliased to the
  existing `LAST_LOGIN_TIMEZONE`), `ATTENDANCE_REQUIRED_OAUTH_SCOPE`, a configurable PRESENT threshold
  (`getAttendancePresentThresholdPct_()`/`setAttendancePresentThresholdPct()`, Script-Property-backed,
  defaulting to 80% — a reasoned default flagged explicitly as **not** an existing APS policy, since
  none exists anywhere in this codebase; confirm/adjust before relying on the PRESENT/PARTIAL labels
  for anything official), and `ATTENDANCE_SYNC_LOOKBACK_HOURS = 6` (how long after a class's scheduled
  start the sync keeps re-checking it, to catch late-finalizing Meet session data).
- `getOrCreateCourseAwkMapSheet_()` / `readCourseAwkMap_()` / `assignAwkSheetNameForCourse_()` — the
  persistent Course ID → AWK Sheet mapping, `LockService`-protected so concurrent sync runs can't
  double-assign; a course's number, once given, is never changed. `getOrCreateAttendanceCourseSheet_()`
  creates each `AWKxxATT` sheet with its header row exactly once.
- `getOrCreateMeetLinkMapSheet_()` / `readCourseMeetLinkMap_()` / `saveCourseMeetLinkMapping()` /
  `getCourseMeetLinkMappings()` / `extractMeetCode_()` — the Admin-maintained Course↔Meet-link mapping
  described above.
- `parseAttendanceCourseInfo_()` / `attendanceScheduledWindowForDate_()` /
  `attendanceCourseInScopeNow_()` — combines the two existing course-name parsers and the two existing
  timezone helpers to determine a course's scheduled window for a given Eastern calendar date, and
  whether "now" falls inside this feature's sync lookback for that date.
- The pure logic core (deliberately free of any Sheets/Meet-API calls, so it's independently
  testable): `attMergeAndBoundSessions_()` (clips every raw session to the scheduled window, merges
  overlapping/touching intervals, sums minutes — requirements 5/6/12/13/14),
  `attComputeStatus_()` (PRESENT/PARTIAL/ABSENT against the configurable threshold — requirement 10),
  `attRecordKey_()` (the Course ID + Date + Email + Role idempotency key exactly as specified),
  `attFormatSessionDetails_()`, `attBuildRecord_()`, `attRecordToRow_()`/`attRowToRecord_()`.
- `upsertAttendanceRecordsForCourse_()` — one batched read of a course's existing AWK sheet rows, an
  in-memory merge keyed by `attRecordKey_()` (a matching key updates in place; a new key appends), one
  batched write — never a per-row Sheets call, and re-running it with the same input is a no-op
  (requirement 15).
- The real Meet integration: `fetchMeetSessionsForCourse_()` (resolves the mapped Meet code to its
  space, lists `conferenceRecords` in the scheduled window via `UrlFetchApp` + `ScriptApp.getOAuthToken()`),
  `mergeParticipantSessionsIntoMap_()` and `fetchParticipantSessions_()` (walk each conference
  record's participants and their `participantSessions`), `resolveSignedInUserEmail_()` (the
  `AdminDirectory.Users.get()` email resolution described above), and `logAttendanceSyncDiagnostic_()`/
  `getAttendanceSyncDiagnostics()` (a Script-Property-backed rolling diagnostic log, mirroring
  `getMeetPresenceMap_`'s own diagnostic-property + `console.error` pattern — every one of these calls
  is wrapped so a permission/network problem degrades to an empty result and a logged diagnostic,
  never a thrown error).
- `syncAttendanceForAllCourses()` — the main entry point. Reads courses from the existing cache Sheet
  (`readAllCoursesFromCache_()` — no fresh Classroom API call), and for each course that's in its
  scheduled window right now, resolves its AWK sheet and Meet mapping, builds one record per teacher
  and per student (present or not — an absent scheduled participant still gets a 0-minute/ABSENT row,
  requirement 11), and upserts them. One course's failure is caught, logged with the exact
  Course ID/Course Name/Error/Timestamp fields the spec's example log shows, and does **not** stop the
  rest (requirement 19). `forceSyncAttendanceNow()` is the Admin/HM-only manual trigger;
  `createAttendanceSyncTrigger()` installs a 15-minute time-driven trigger, mirroring
  `createSyncTrigger()`'s own idempotent bootstrap idiom exactly (run once, manually, from the Apps
  Script editor).
- `getAttendanceRecordsForAdmin()` / `getAttendanceCourseAwkMap()` / `getAttendanceLastSyncInfo()` —
  Admin/HM-only read endpoints backing the new admin panel, answering every auditability question in
  requirement 23 (first join, last leave, reconnect count, active minutes, scheduled duration,
  status, course, AWK sheet) directly from the stored row.

**Dashboard.html** — a new Admin/HM-only "🗓️ Attendance" tab (`tabAttendance`/`attendanceView`,
gated in `updateAttendanceTabVisibility()` exactly like the existing `tabAssignClassroom`/
`tabUserRoles` tabs, called from both `load()` and `quietRefreshDashboard()`'s success handlers next
to `updateClassChangeTabVisibility()`), with four sections styled to match the existing
`assignment-admin-panel`/`assignment-audit-panel` two-column layout used by the Assign Classroom tab:
a Sync Attendance Now button plus last-run status and a collapsible diagnostics list; the Course↔Meet
Link mapping table and add/update form; a read-only Course↔AWK Sheet mapping table; and a filterable
(course/date/role) Attendance Records table. All new element ids are `att`-prefixed, matching this
file's existing per-feature convention (`rl-` for Reference Letter, `gtr` for Grade/Timing Change).

### Trigger configuration

Automatic: run `createAttendanceSyncTrigger()` once, manually, from the Apps Script editor (exactly
like the existing `createSyncTrigger()` bootstrap) to install a 15-minute time-driven trigger calling
`syncAttendanceForAllCourses`. Each run only processes courses whose scheduled class start (Eastern,
today) falls within the last `ATTENDANCE_SYNC_LOOKBACK_HOURS` (6) hours, so it naturally covers an
in-progress class and a grace window afterward for late-finalizing Meet data, without doing anything
for a course not currently in session. Manual: the "Sync Attendance Now" button on the new Attendance
tab calls `forceSyncAttendanceNow()` (Admin/HM/Super Admin only), which runs the identical function
immediately.
