### Self-review — flags

- **The biggest open question is access, not code**: whether the Meet API will actually return
  conference/participant data for every course once the scope, Cloud-project enablement, and Course↔
  Meet-link mappings are all in place depends on a Workspace-level access question (item 3 above) this
  environment cannot test. Please run `forceSyncAttendanceNow()` for one already-mapped, currently-
  meeting course first, then check `getAttendanceSyncDiagnostics()` before assuming a wider rollout is
  ready.
- **The PRESENT threshold (80%) is a placeholder**, not a school policy — there was no existing
  attendance policy anywhere in this codebase to inherit. Please confirm or change it via
  `setAttendancePresentThresholdPct()` before these labels are used for anything official.
- **`Session Count` counts raw Meet sessions (how many times someone actually joined/reconnected),
  not merged intervals** — e.g. two overlapping raw sessions merge into one continuous attendance
  block but still report `Session Count: 2`. This reads requirement 23's "how many times did they
  reconnect" literally; flagging in case a merged-block count was intended instead.
- **A participant whose Meet identity can't be resolved to an email (phone dial-in, or an
  `AdminDirectory.Users.get()` lookup failure) is silently excluded from that person's attendance
  contribution** — their session data simply isn't attributed to anyone, rather than being guessed at.
  This could under-count a legitimate dial-in participant; flagged rather than silently accepted.
- **`getAttendanceRecordsForAdmin()` has no pagination** and reads every mapped course's full AWK
  sheet on every call — reasonable at today's volume, worth revisiting after a school year of data.
- **This round intentionally left the other working copy's Attendance/Bulk-Fill/Audit-Log module
  out**, per your explicit answer. If that work should still ship at some point, it would need to be
  re-evaluated against *this* file's actual current state (not assumed compatible), since the two
  diverged before that module was ever built.

#### Round 44 addendum: missing `userinfo.email` scope broke login after redeploy

After redeploying with this round's `appsscript.json`, login failed with: `Exception: Specified
permissions are not sufficient to call Session.getActiveUser. Required permissions:
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email`. This project's manifest has always used an
**explicit** `oauthScopes` list (confirmed in the original, unmodified `Current_appsscript.json` — it
already listed 10 scopes before this round touched it). Once a manifest declares `oauthScopes`
explicitly, Apps Script grants *only* what's listed — nothing is auto-added for implicit calls like
`Session.getActiveUser().getEmail()`, which the login flow (`getAuthenticatedGoogleEmail`,
`getViewerRole_`, etc.) has always depended on. `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email` was
never in that list. It's likely this exact gap was latent before this round too (whatever allowed it
to work previously — an already-granted broader consent from an earlier authorization, or a
difference between the live deployment's actual manifest and the `Current_appsscript.json` backup
snapshot — is outside what this environment can inspect), and this round's redeploy (needed either
way, to pick up the two new Meet-related scopes) is what surfaced it.

**Fix**: added `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email` to `oauthScopes` (now first in the
list). Validated as well-formed JSON; no other file changed. This still requires a **new deployment
version** and everyone re-authorizing ("Review Access Again," approving the one additional
permission line) — adding a manifest scope never applies to an existing deployment/session without
that step, same as the two Meet-related scopes already required it. If the same exception recurs
after this fix and a fresh authorization, the next thing to check is whether the *live* Apps Script
project's actual manifest (Project Settings, or the online editor's own `appsscript.json`) matches
what's in `ATTENDANCE_FEATURE_ROUND44/appsscript.json` at all — a hand-edited or partially-pasted
manifest in the live editor would explain a mismatch this backup-snapshot comparison can't see.

### Sept 2026, forty-fifth round — Attendance role-based visibility, Teacher edit rights, audit log

**Trigger**: after confirming Admin/HM could reach the Attendance tab, the user reported Teacher and
Student needed it too, plus three specific access-control requirements: (1) a Teacher should view
*and edit* the Weekly Attendance of the students in the classes they teach; (2) a Teacher should be
able to view *only their own* captured attendance ("My Attendance"), separate from that student-edit
view, and separate from the pre-existing, unrelated "Weekly Class Teacher Availability" (self-reported
confirm/not-available) feature; (3) Admin/HM/SuperAdmin/Teacher edits to a student's attendance must
be logged to an audit trail; (4) a Student should see only their own weekly attendance, read-only.

Before writing any code, three genuinely ambiguous, permission-sensitive design questions were put to
the user directly (AskUserQuestion) rather than assumed. All three recommended (safest/most
consistent-with-existing-patterns) options were chosen:

1. **Teacher edit scope** — a Teacher may edit attendance only for students in courses **they
   teach** (not every student at APS). Matches the `courseHasTeacherEmail_` scoping pattern already
   used everywhere else in this codebase (Teacher Availability, Class/Grade Change approvals, etc.).
2. **Editable fields** — an edit changes **Status only** (PRESENT/PARTIAL/ABSENT). The Meet-captured
   Active Minutes and session timestamps are never hand-edited by anyone, keeping the raw captured
   numbers trustworthy; an edit is a correction of the final classification, not the underlying data.
3. **Self-edit** — a Teacher can **never** edit their own (TEACHER-role) attendance row, even though
   they can edit their students' rows. Only Admin/HM/SuperAdmin could ever correct a teacher's own
   row. Prevents a teacher from marking themselves present/absent.

#### A) Files changed
- `Code.gs` — additive only; nothing in the original Attendance module (Round 44) or any earlier
  round's code was modified or removed.
- `Dashboard.html` — the Attendance tab's markup and script were extended (see D/below); every
  pre-existing view/tab/panel in this file is untouched.
- `dashboard-architecture-and-config.md` — this addendum.

#### B) New functions (Code.gs)
- `getAttendanceRecordsForViewer(filters)` — the new, role-aware read endpoint every recognized role
  calls from the Attendance tab. `getAttendanceRecordsForAdmin(filters)` (Round 44) is **left
  completely unchanged** and is simply no longer called by the client — kept in place rather than
  removed, in case anything else ever depends on its exact original Admin/HM-only contract.
  Server-side scope per role (never trusts a client-supplied filter to widen access):
  - `admin`/`headmaster`/`superadmin`: every course, every role — identical to
    `getAttendanceRecordsForAdmin`.
  - `teacher`: STUDENT-role rows for courses this teacher teaches by default; with
    `filters.scope === 'mine'`, only this teacher's own TEACHER-role rows ("My Attendance"),
    always `editable:false`.
  - `student`: only rows whose Email is their own, within courses they're enrolled in, always
    `editable:false`.
  Each row carries an `editable` flag the client uses to decide whether to render an Edit button —
  a display convenience only; the real enforcement is server-side in the next function.
- `editAttendanceRecordStatus(courseId, dateStr, email, role, newStatus, reason)` — edits **only**
  the Status column (plus Last Updated) of one existing AWK row, identified by the same
  Course ID + Date + Email + Role key used for idempotent sync upserts. Allowed for
  Admin/HM/SuperAdmin (any row) or a Teacher editing a STUDENT-role row in a course they teach
  (never their own row, never another course). Throws server-side for anyone else, regardless of
  what the client sends. A no-op edit (new status === old status) returns `{unchanged:true}` without
  writing anything or logging an audit entry.
- `getOrCreateAttendanceAuditLogSheet_()` / `appendAttendanceAuditLogEntry_(entry)` — get-or-create
  and append-only write helpers for the new `Attendance_Audit_Log` sheet (same spreadsheet as the
  AWK sheets — `ATTENDANCE_SPREADSHEET_ID`). Columns: Edited At, Edited By Email, Edited By Role,
  Course ID, Class Name, Attendance Date, Person Name, Person Email, Person Role, Old Status,
  New Status, Reason. Every successful `editAttendanceRecordStatus` call appends exactly one row;
  nothing ever edits or deletes an existing audit row.
- `getAttendanceAuditLog(filters)` — Admin/HM/SuperAdmin-only read of the audit log, most recent
  first, optionally filtered to one course, capped to the 500 most recent entries **on read only**
  (the sheet itself keeps every entry forever).

#### C) Modified functions
None. Every Round 44 function (`getAttendanceRecordsForAdmin`, `upsertAttendanceRecordsForCourse_`,
`attBuildRecord_`, the Meet API integration, the sync trigger functions, etc.) is byte-for-byte
unchanged.

#### Self-review flags (things worth your explicit confirmation, not assumed)
- **"Teacher should view and edit all the student Weekly Attendance" was read as "all the students
  in the classes this Teacher teaches,"** not literally every student at APS — this was the specific
  question put to you and confirmed. If any Teacher account is also, unusually, supposed to have
  broader reach (e.g. a lead teacher overseeing other classes), that account would need to be an
  Admin/HM/SuperAdmin instead, or this scoping rule would need to change.
- **The "(my Attendance) capture from Weekly Class Teacher Availability" phrase** was interpreted as:
  keep the new "My Attendance" (Meet-captured presence) view clearly separate and distinctly labeled
  from the existing, unrelated "Teacher Weekly Availability" feature (self-reported
  confirmed/not-available per week) — NOT as a request to merge the two features' UI or data
  together. Nothing about the existing Teacher Weekly Availability panel (`getWeeklyPanelData`,
  `setTeacherAvailabilityStatus`, the "This Week" panel) was touched. If you actually meant "My
  Attendance" should live inside that existing Weekly panel rather than as a toggle inside the
  Attendance tab, that's a UI-placement change, not a data/permission change — flag it and it can be
  moved.
- **Editing is Status-only, by your confirmed choice** — if a sync later re-runs for the same
  Course ID + Date (e.g. a corrected Meet link, or a later sync catching a session Google was still
  finalizing), `upsertAttendanceRecordsForCourse_`'s idempotent upsert (Round 44, unchanged) will
  overwrite that row — including a manually-edited Status — with whatever the sync recomputes. A
  manual Status edit is therefore not permanently "sticky" against a future sync of the same
  date/course; only the Audit Log preserves a permanent record that the edit happened. Flagging this
  since it wasn't explicitly asked about — if edited rows should be protected from being overwritten
  by a later sync, that would need a follow-up change (e.g. skipping upsert for rows with a
  matching manual-edit marker).

### Sept 2026, forty-sixth round — stop leaking internal IDs in user-facing error messages

**Trigger**: "In the error and warning message dont show confidently information like sheet_id
instead of show display generic messages." Prompted by Round 45's expansion of the Attendance tab
to Teacher/Student — an error that used to only ever reach Admin/HM (who already know the internal
spreadsheet ID from the AWK mapping panel) can now reach every role, including Student.

#### A) Files changed
`Code.gs` only — no HTML change was needed; the client already just displays whatever `err.message`
the server throws (`showToast(err.message, true)` / the error-row fallback in each table renderer),
so sanitizing the thrown text at the source fixes every display surface at once.

#### B) What was found and fixed
A full sweep of every `throw new Error(...)` in `Code.gs` that interpolates a variable, specifically
looking for internal identifiers (spreadsheet IDs, sheet names) being concatenated into user-facing
text, found three:
1. **`getAttendanceWorkbook_()`** — used to throw `'Could not open the Attendance spreadsheet (ID
   "' + ATTENDANCE_SPREADSHEET_ID + '"). ... Original error: ' + e.message`, exposing the raw
   Attendance spreadsheet ID and Google's own underlying exception text to whoever triggered the
   failure — now any recognized role. **Now**: logs the full detail via `console.error` (visible to
   Admin/HM/SuperAdmin in Stackdriver) and `logAttendanceSyncDiagnostic_()` (visible in the existing
   "Recent diagnostics" panel on the Attendance tab, Admin/HM/SuperAdmin only), and throws a generic
   `'Could not open the Attendance data right now. Please try again, or contact an Administrator if
   this continues.'` to every caller.
2. **`editAttendanceRecordStatus()`** — used to throw `'Attendance sheet "' + awkSheet + '" was not
   found.'`, exposing the internal AWK sheet name (e.g. `"AWK01ATT"`) — reachable by a Teacher (this
   function is now callable by Teacher, per Round 45). **Now**: logs the sheet name + course ID via
   `console.error`, throws the generic `'Could not find the attendance data for that class.'`
3. **`getWorkbook_()`** (pre-existing, not part of the Attendance module — backs the *entire*
   dashboard's Courses/chat/availability data cache, and has always been reachable by every role) —
   used to throw `'Could not open TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID "' + TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID + '". ...
   Original error: ' + e.message`. Same fix: `console.error` server-side, generic `'Could not load
   classroom data right now. Please try again, or contact an Administrator if this continues.'`
   thrown to the caller. This one predates every round in this engagement — it's flagged here
   because it's the same class of bug and directly responsive to what was asked, not because
   anything about it changed behaviorally before now.

#### C) What was deliberately left alone
Every OTHER `throw new Error(...)` in the file was reviewed and left as-is because it either (a) is
a permission message that names a ROLE, not an internal identifier (e.g. "Only Admin/Headmaster/
Super Admin can..."), (b) echoes back the user's OWN input (e.g. "Unknown attendance status: " +
newStatus), (c) is already generic (e.g. "No attendance has been captured yet for that class."), or
(d) is a `processingNotes`/error field shown ONLY on an Admin/HM-only approver panel (Class Change,
Reference Letter), where the extra internal detail is intentional and helpful for staff
troubleshooting, not a leak to a broader audience.

**Known remaining limitation, flagged rather than silently left**: `callWithBackoff_()` (used for
retrying transient Google API failures) re-throws Google's OWN original exception object unmodified
if it isn't retryable. In rare cases Google's own error text can itself mention a resource
identifier. Fully closing that would mean wrapping every single Sheets/Classroom/Drive/Meet API call
site in this ~7,000-line file with its own generic-message translation — a much larger change than
what was asked, and one that would also strip detail Admin currently relies on in several places.
Not done in this round; flagging so it's a known, deliberate scope boundary rather than an oversight.

#### D) Test results
`node --check` on the full file — passes. Duplicate top-level function/`var` name scan — zero
duplicates. Manual review of both new `console.error(...)` calls confirms they run server-side only
(Stackdriver Logging, plus the Attendance one also feeds the existing Admin/HM-only diagnostics
panel) and never reach `google.script.run`'s return value or a thrown `Error`, so nothing sensitive
crosses back to the client. NOT independently testable beyond that in this environment (no live
Sheets access to actually trigger a real open-spreadsheet failure).

### Sept 2026, forty-eighth round — login-error root-causing, Reference Letter tab click fix, Reference Letter eligibility for dual-hat teachers

**Trigger**: a screenshot of the "APS authorization could not be completed" gate screen ("few users
getting this... if users are able to login without any error") followed by "fix this error. make
sure all the user able to login. Also Enable referece letter request to all the teachers. also fix
Reference letter tab click is not working."

#### A) Files changed
`Code.gs` and `Dashboard.html`. No manifest change.

#### B) New functions
- **`openSpreadsheetByIdWithRetry_(id, logPrefix)`** (`Code.gs`) — wraps `SpreadsheetApp.openById()`
  with up to 3 attempts and a short doubling backoff (300ms, then 600ms; no sleep after the final
  attempt), logging each failed attempt via `console.error` before re-throwing the last error once
  every attempt is exhausted. Mirrors the existing `callWithBackoff_()` pattern used for Classroom API
  calls, but shorter — this sits on the blocking login path, so a long retry schedule would just turn
  a fast failure into a slow one.
- **`apsClassifyServerError_(err)`** (`Dashboard.html`) — pattern-matches a thrown error's message
  against the specific generic/sanitized strings `getWorkbook_()`/`getAttendanceWorkbook_()`
  deliberately throw for an ordinary data-load failure (`/could not (load|open) .*(right now|data
  right now)/i`), returning `'temporary_error'` for those and `'authorization_failure'` for
  everything else (including a genuine Apps Script authorization exception, or no message at all).

#### C) Modified functions

**Code.gs**
1. **`getWorkbook_()`** — both `SpreadsheetApp.openById()` calls (the hardcoded
   `TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID` branch and the auto-created-cache-sheet branch) now go through
   `openSpreadsheetByIdWithRetry_()` instead of a bare, unretried call. The `TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID`
   branch's catch block wording was updated ("after retrying") to reflect that reaching it now means
   every retry already failed, not just a single attempt.
2. **`getAttendanceWorkbook_()`** — same treatment, for consistency and the same underlying risk
   (this one isn't on the login path, but shares the identical unretried-open pattern that was
   causing the login issue).
3. **`getDashboardData()`** — added `ctx.isClassroomTeacher = courses.some(c =>
   courseHasTeacherEmail_(c, ctx.email))`, computed from the `courses` array already read for this
   call (no extra Sheet/Classroom read). Surfaces to the client as `currentUser.isClassroomTeacher`.
4. **`submitReferenceLetterRequest()`** — gate widened from `if (viewer.role !== 'teacher') throw ...`
   to `if (viewer.role !== 'teacher' && !isClassroomTeacher) throw ...`, where `isClassroomTeacher` is
   computed the same way, inline, from the request's own already-read `courses`.
5. **`getMyReferenceLetterRequests()`** — identical widening, so a dual-hat viewer who can now submit
   a request can also see it afterward in "My Reference Letter Requests".

**Dashboard.html**
1. **Missing click listeners — the tab-click bug.** Every other view tab (`tabClasses`,
   `tabOnboarding`, `tabKb`, `tabClassChange`, `tabAssignClassroom`, `tabUserRoles`, `tabAttendance`)
   had a `document.getElementById(...).addEventListener('click', ...)` wired up in the tab-listener
   block near the end of the file. `rl-tab` and `rl-approvals-tab` were fully built (markup,
   show/hide logic in `updateReferenceLetterTabVisibility()`, `switchView()` cases) but had **no
   click listener at all** — so clicking either tab silently did nothing. Added the two missing
   listeners (`switchView('referenceLetter')` / `switchView('referenceLetterApprovals')`) alongside
   the others.
2. **`apsShowAuthError(code, err)`** — added a `'temporary_error'` branch with calmer, accurate copy
   ("We couldn't load your account right now... this is usually a brief, temporary issue... not a
   problem with your permissions") and no "Execute as" deployment guidance, since that guidance is
   actively misleading for this case. The retry button's label now also updates dynamically ("Try
   Again" vs "Review Access Again") depending on which screen is shown.
3. **`apsSubmitLogin()`** and **`apsBootstrapSession()`** — both now retry their `google.script.run`
   call once, silently, with a 900ms delay, before showing any error to the user. Both call sites'
   final failure handler now calls `apsShowAuthError(apsClassifyServerError_(err), err)` instead of
   hardcoding `'authorization_failure'`.
4. **`updateReferenceLetterTabVisibility()`** — `isTeacher` widened from `currentUser.role ===
   'teacher'` to `(currentUser.role === 'teacher' || currentUser.isClassroomTeacher)`. This one
   variable already drives `rl-tab`'s visibility, the `referenceLetter` view-switch guard, and
   `rl-teacher-section`'s visibility, so widening it here was sufficient for all three.
5. **`loadReferenceLetterView()`** — its own separate early-return guard widened identically (it
   wasn't derived from `updateReferenceLetterTabVisibility()`'s local variable, so it needed its own
   fix).

#### D) Root cause explanation (for the login-error report)
The "APS authorization could not be completed / Review Access Again / Execute as: User accessing the
web app" screen is a client-side bucket (`apsShowAuthError('authorization_failure', err)`) that
Dashboard.html previously showed for **any** exception thrown by the login/session-check
`google.script.run` calls (`authorizeDashboardAccess()` for an explicit login,
`validateApsSession()` for the automatic, silent revalidation that runs on every page load for a
returning visitor with a saved session) — not only a genuine OAuth/authorization problem. The
screenshot's own "Details:" line showed the real thrown message: `"Could not load classroom data
right now. Please try again, or contact an Administrator if this continues."` — the exact sanitized
string `getWorkbook_()` throws (Round 46) when `SpreadsheetApp.openById(TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID)`
fails. That call had no retry at all, unlike every Classroom API call in this file. A single
transient Sheets-service hiccup — plausible given the volume of concurrent access this workbook gets
(every open dashboard tab polls it, the chat sheet polls every 8s, and the 15-minute Classroom-sync
trigger periodically rewrites the same "Courses" tab) — would throw immediately for whichever
request happened to land in that window, explaining "a few users" rather than everyone, and why
retrying (clicking "Review Access Again", which just re-submits the login form) usually worked. This
round fixes both halves: the underlying open now retries before giving up
(`openSpreadsheetByIdWithRetry_`), the client also retries once silently before ever showing an
error, and if an error does still reach the user after both retries, it's now labeled accurately
instead of pointing them at a deployment setting that was never actually the problem.

#### E) Sheet configuration
No change.

#### F) Trigger configuration
No change.

#### G) Test results (only what was actually executed)
- `node --check` on the full, updated `Code.gs` — passes.
- Python `HTMLParser`-based tag-balance check on the full, updated `Dashboard.html` — no
  mismatched/unclosed tags.
- Duplicate static `id="..."` scan across `Dashboard.html` — zero duplicates.
- Duplicate top-level `function`/`var` name scan across both files — zero duplicates.
- `openSpreadsheetByIdWithRetry_()` re-verified against the exact shipped function body (extracted
  via `sed`, wrapped with mocked `SpreadsheetApp`/`Utilities` via `new Function(...)`) — confirmed:
  opens immediately with no retry when the first attempt succeeds; recovers and succeeds on the 2nd
  attempt when the 1st attempt throws (the "few users" scenario this round targets); still throws
  after exhausting all 3 attempts when every attempt fails (a genuinely broken ID/permission is not
  silently swallowed); sleeps only between attempts, never after the last one.
- The `isClassroomTeacher` widening logic (identical in all three call sites) was re-verified against
  a reimplementation using the shipped `courseHasTeacherEmail_()` semantics: a dual-hat Admin who also
  co-teaches a course is now allowed through the Reference Letter gate; a plain Admin with no course
  at all is still rejected; a plain classroom Teacher and a Student behave exactly as before. 16/16
  checks passed.
- `apsClassifyServerError_()` re-verified directly (function is short enough to test standalone):
  both of `getWorkbook_()`/`getAttendanceWorkbook_()`'s exact generic messages classify as
  `'temporary_error'`; a real Apps Script authorization-exception message, an unrelated custom error
  message, and a missing message all correctly classify as `'authorization_failure'` (never silently
  reclassified away from the guidance that's actually needed for a real deployment problem). 5/5
  checks passed.
- NOT independently testable in this environment (no live Google Workspace/Sheets access): whether
  the retry actually eliminates the reported login failures in production, since that depends on the
  real, currently-unknown frequency/cause of the underlying transient Sheets errors. This is a
  mitigation for a class of failure that was previously unguarded at all, not a guarantee that no
  login failure can ever occur (a Sheets outage longer than 3 retries × 2 attempts of backoff, for
  example, would still eventually surface — now correctly labeled as a temporary/data problem
  instead of an authorization one).

#### Self-review flags
- **"Enable reference letter request to all the teachers" — interpretation.** Read as: fix the
  specific case where a person who actually co-teaches an active Classroom course cannot request a
  Reference Letter because their overall Dashboard role (Admin/Headmaster/BOD/SuperAdmin — which

  (`submitAdminInitiatedReferenceLetter()`, per `APS_Reference_Letter_Feature.md` §9), or an Admin
  manually assigning the `teacher` Dashboard role to that email via the User Roles & Permissions
  panel (`configuredRoles`, checked ahead of the Classroom-derived role in `getViewerRole_()`, so it
  already grants full `teacher`-role access including Reference Letter once set). If "all the
  teachers" was actually meant to include people with no current course assignment at all, that's a
  different, larger change (there's no durable "was ever a teacher" roster kept anywhere in this
  project — only currently-active Classroom courses are cached) and should be confirmed before
  building.
- **Login-error fix is a mitigation, not a proof of elimination.** As noted in §D/§F above, retries
  make the specific class of failure seen in the screenshot much less likely to reach a user, but
  cannot guarantee zero login failures ever (a sufficiently long real Sheets outage would still
  surface, now correctly labeled). If login failures continue after this round ships, the next
  diagnostic step is checking the Apps Script Executions log (Stackdriver) around the affected
  timestamps for the `[Dashboard] open attempt N/3 failed...` log lines this round adds — they will
  show whether retries are actually firing/succeeding, and how often.
- **Reference Letter click-handler bug scope.** Only `rl-tab`/`rl-approvals-tab` were missing a click
  listener — every other tab's listener (Classes, Onboarding, Knowledge Base, Class Change, Assign
  Classroom, User Roles, Attendance) was checked and already present. No other tab exhibits this
  bug.

### Sept 2026, forty-ninth round — login error, part 2: distinguish a persistent per-account sharing gap from a transient blip

**Trigger**: a follow-up screenshot showing the SAME user still hitting a failure after Round 48
shipped — but now correctly displaying Round 48's new, calmer `"We couldn't load your account right
now"` / `"Try Again"` copy instead of the old scary "Execute as" screen. This confirmed Round 48's
error-classification fix was live and working as designed, but also proved the underlying data-load
failure itself was not resolved by that round's retries — the same "Details: Could not load
classroom data right now..." message was still showing up.

#### A) Files changed
`Code.gs` and `Dashboard.html`. No manifest change.

#### B) New functions
- **`isPermissionDeniedError_(e)`** (`Code.gs`) — pattern-matches an exception's message against the
  text Apps Script/Drive throw for a genuine sharing/permission failure (`/you do not have
  permission|permission denied|requested document|not authorized to access/i`).

#### C) Root cause, part 2
Round 48's retries (3 server-side attempts + 1 silent client-side retry) all failed **identically**
for this user rather than eventually succeeding — the signature of a **persistent** failure, not a
one-off transient Sheets-service blip. This Web App is deployed "Execute as: User accessing the web
app" (confirmed intentional per the code's own long-standing comments — see e.g.
`getAuthenticatedGoogleEmail()`), which means `SpreadsheetApp.openById(TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID)` runs
under **that individual user's own Google account and Drive permissions**, not the script owner's.
If the shared "Data Cache" spreadsheet (`1rlFMiXDMVaBcZS89AL0OC5TYeXz4PIZyXXboYoDGzX0`) isn't shared
with a particular authorized user's actual Google account, opening it fails for them **every single
time** — retried or not — while it keeps succeeding for every other user whose account does have
access. That matches both reports: "a few users" (whoever's account lacks sharing) and "still
happening after the retry fix" (retrying a permission gap can't ever help).

**Action needed from an Administrator, outside of code**: open
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1rlFMiXDMVaBcZS89AL0OC5TYeXz4PIZyXXboYoDGzX0/edit and check
its Share settings. If it's shared only with specific individual accounts rather than the whole
`avvaiyarpadasalai.org` domain (or whatever group every authorized Dashboard user belongs to), any
authorized-by-email-list user whose account isn't also individually shared on the Sheet itself will
hit exactly this failure, consistently, regardless of any retry logic. Sharing it with "Anyone in the
organization can view" (or explicitly adding the affected users) is the actual fix for those specific
accounts; this round's code change (below) is about making the SYMPTOM accurate and actionable when
that gap exists, not a substitute for closing the gap itself.

#### D) Modified functions

**Code.gs**
1. **`openSpreadsheetByIdWithRetry_()`** — now checks each caught error with the new
   `isPermissionDeniedError_()` and, if it matches, stops retrying immediately (`break`) instead of
   burning through all 3 attempts with backoff delays. A persistent per-account sharing gap fails
   exactly the same way on every attempt, so retrying it only makes the affected user wait longer for
   a guaranteed failure; a genuinely transient error (not permission-shaped) still gets the full
   3-attempt retry treatment exactly as Round 48 shipped it.
2. **`getWorkbook_()`**, **`getAttendanceWorkbook_()`** — their catch blocks now call
   `isPermissionDeniedError_(e)` and throw a distinct, actionable message
   (`"Your Google account does not currently have access to the APS Dashboard's shared data. Please
   ask an Administrator to share it with your account, then try again."` — and the Attendance
   equivalent) instead of the generic "temporary" message, when the underlying failure is a
   permission error. The generic "Could not load classroom data right now..." message is now used
   only for genuinely non-permission failures.

**Dashboard.html**
1. **`apsClassifyServerError_(err)`** — added a `/does not currently have access/i` check ahead of
   the existing temporary-error pattern, returning a new `'permission_error'` code.
2. **`apsShowAuthError(code, err)`** — added a `'permission_error'` branch: title "Your account
   doesn't have access to APS Dashboard data yet", body text explaining the actual cause and fix
   (contact an Administrator to be shared on the workbook) rather than the `'temporary_error'`
   branch's "this is usually brief, please wait and try again" — which would be actively misleading
   for a permission gap that "Try Again" can never resolve on its own.

#### E) Sheet configuration
No sheet schema change. Flagging (see §C above) that the actual fix for the reported symptom is a
Drive **sharing** change on the existing Data Cache spreadsheet — outside what code can do — which an
Administrator needs to make.

#### F) Trigger configuration
No change.

#### G) Test results (only what was actually executed)
- `node --check` on the full, updated `Code.gs` — passes.
- Python `HTMLParser`-based tag-balance check on the full, updated `Dashboard.html` — no
  mismatched/unclosed tags.
- Duplicate static `id="..."` scan and duplicate top-level `function`/`var` name scan — zero
  duplicates in both files.
- `isPermissionDeniedError_()` / `openSpreadsheetByIdWithRetry_()` re-verified against the exact
  shipped function bodies (extracted via `sed`, wrapped with mocked `SpreadsheetApp`/`Utilities` via
  `new Function(...)`) — 13/13 checks passed, confirming: a real permission-error message is
  correctly classified and a generic transient/quota message is not; a persistent permission error
  fails on the very first attempt with zero wasted sleep calls, and the original error message is
  preserved for the caller; a transient (non-permission) error still gets the full retry-and-recover
  treatment unchanged from Round 48; and a mixed sequence (transient failure, then a permission error
  on the next attempt) correctly stops retrying as soon as the permission error appears.
- `apsClassifyServerError_()` re-verified directly — the new permission messages from both
  `getWorkbook_()` and `getAttendanceWorkbook_()` classify as `'permission_error'`, the existing
  generic message still classifies as `'temporary_error'`, and a real authorization exception / no
  message still classify as `'authorization_failure'`. 5/5 checks passed.
- NOT independently testable in this environment (no live Google Workspace/Drive access): whether
  the affected user's account is in fact missing Drive sharing on the Data Cache spreadsheet (this is
  inferred from the retry-survives-identically pattern in the two screenshots, not confirmed directly
  against Drive's actual sharing list) — an Administrator checking that spreadsheet's Share dialog is
  the way to confirm this directly and is the real fix for the reported symptom, per §C.

#### Self-review flags
- **This round assumes the root cause is a Drive-sharing gap, not a spreadsheet ID misconfiguration
  or a broader outage.** The evidence (identical failure surviving every retry, only "a few users"
  affected, everyone else logs in fine) fits a per-account sharing gap best, but it's an inference
  from two screenshots, not a direct read of the spreadsheet's Share settings or the Apps Script
  Executions log. If checking Share settings on
  `1rlFMiXDMVaBcZS89AL0OC5TYeXz4PIZyXXboYoDGzX0` shows every affected user already has access, the
  next diagnostic step is the Stackdriver/Executions log around the failure timestamp for the new
  `"... with a PERMISSION error (not retrying further)"` log line this round adds — its absence would
  mean the failure isn't actually permission-shaped and needs a different explanation.
- **The permission-vs-transient text match is necessarily heuristic.** `isPermissionDeniedError_()`
  matches on the specific wording Google Apps Script/Drive are known to use for a sharing failure. If
  Google ever changes that wording, or a different, less common permission-error phrasing occurs, it
  would fall through to the generic "temporary" bucket instead — not incorrect (the user still gets a
  message and a retry), just less specific than intended. This is a soft heuristic on top of the
  underlying fix, not a load-bearing classification the security model depends on.

### Sept 2026, fiftieth round — Group Sync Report: closing the sharing gap Round 49 diagnosed

**Trigger**: a follow-up screenshot of the actual Google Drive Share dialog for the underlying
workbook ("APS School - Live Dashboard", `1rlFMiXDMVaBcZS89AL0OC5TYeXz4PIZyXXboYoDGzX0`), confirming
Round 49's inference directly: **People with access** = `info@avvaiyarpadasalai.org` (Owner) only.
**General access** = the Google Group "American Charitable Tamil Society", Editor, "Anyone in this
group with the link can edit." So every authorized Dashboard user's access to the shared workbook
runs entirely through that one Group's membership — and the Group's membership isn't guaranteed to
track who the Dashboard's own role logic currently authorizes, which is exactly the gap Round 49
diagnosed. Two remediation paths were presented: (1) loosen sharing to "Anyone in the organization
with the link," or (2) keep it Group-restricted but make the Group's membership match reality. The
user explicitly chose (2): **"Keep it Group-restricted, but make the Group match reality."** A
follow-up question (via AskUserQuestion) resolved *how* to keep the Group in sync: build a full
Admin Directory API auto-sync, or generate a report the Super Admin pastes into the Group manually.
The user chose the manual, report-only option — safer (no new Directory-write scope, no risk of an
automated process silently removing someone), simpler to reason about, and puts the actual Drive
membership change in a human's hands where it already belongs.

Note on why Editor-level access was kept, not narrowed to Viewer: this Web App runs "Execute as: User
accessing the web app" (see Round 49 §C), so every write a user makes — including everyday actions
like `postChatMessage()` appending a row to this same workbook — happens under that user's own Drive
permissions. Downgrading the Group's access to Viewer would break those write paths for every
ordinary authorized user, not just tighten security for a few. This round is about narrowing *who* is
authorized, not what an authorized user can do to the shared data once they are.

#### A) Files changed
`Code.gs` and `Dashboard.html`. No manifest change.

#### B) New functions

**Code.gs**
- **`getAuthorizedEmailsForGroupSync()`** — SuperAdmin-only (gated by the existing
  `requireSuperAdminViewer_()`, same as every other function in the User Roles & Permissions panel).
  Computes every email the Dashboard's own logic currently treats as authorized, from sources that
  can actually be enumerated from data already cached/available to the app:
  - **Static role lists**: `SUPERADMIN_EMAILS`, `VCFO_AMCHATS_BOD_EMAILS`, `ADMIN_EMAILS`,
    `HEADMASTER_EMAILS`.
  - **Configured role overrides**: whatever `readConfiguredUserRoles_()` currently has on file (the
    same data source the User Roles table above this report already displays).
  - **Classroom teachers and students**: every teacher/student email across every course this
    SuperAdmin's `courses` list includes.

  Each of the four sources is deduplicated within itself (so, e.g., a teacher on two courses is
  listed once in the `teachers` bucket), and the function then unions all four buckets into a single
  sorted, globally-deduplicated `allEmails` array — the one meant to be pasted directly into the
  Group's "Add people" box. The per-bucket breakdown (`buckets` in the return value) and per-bucket
  counts are also returned, in case a future round wants to show them, though the current UI (below)
  only surfaces the summary counts and the flat paste-ready list.

  **Deliberately excluded**: the broad "authorized" role fallback — any email at one of the four
  `APS_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` with no other specific role. That population can't be enumerated from
  anything this Dashboard has cached; the only way to list it would be a full Workspace Directory
  query across all four domains, which is a materially bigger and more sensitive capability than what
  the user asked for, and was explicitly the automated-sync option the user turned down. The UI
  surfaces this limitation directly to the Super Admin (see below) rather than silently omitting
  those people with no explanation.

#### C) UI: Group Sync Report section
Added to the bottom of the existing "Dashboard User Roles & Permissions" panel in `userRolesView`
(already SuperAdmin-only — gated the same way as the rest of that view, via `roleCan('seeUserRoleTab')`
→ `role === 'superadmin'` — so no additional client-side role check was needed for the new section).

- A **"Generate Group Sync Report"** button calls `getAuthorizedEmailsForGroupSync()` and renders: a
  summary line (total unique count, broken down by static/configured/teacher/student counts, plus the
  generation timestamp), and a read-only, monospace `<textarea>` listing every email one per line.
- A **"Copy All Emails"** button (hidden until a report has been generated, and only shown if the
  list is non-empty) selects the textarea's full contents and calls `document.execCommand('copy')`.
  There was no existing copy-to-clipboard pattern anywhere in this codebase to reuse (checked via
  grep before building this). `document.execCommand('copy')` was used rather than the modern
  `navigator.clipboard` API because this UI runs inside an Apps Script HTML Service iframe, where
  `navigator.clipboard` cannot reliably get the secure-context/permission handshake it needs; even if
  the automatic copy silently fails for some reason, the textarea is left selected, so the Super Admin
  can always fall back to a manual Ctrl+C / Cmd+C — the button's status message says exactly that.
  Because the source `<textarea>` stays visible and selectable regardless of outcome, this is a
  guaranteed-working baseline even in an environment where `execCommand('copy')` behaves unexpectedly.
- An explanatory note under the report reiterates, in the Super Admin's own view (not just this doc),
  that the list excludes the domain-fallback population and that they should also review the Group's
  *current* membership for anyone who should be removed — this report only tells them who to make
  sure is *in* the Group, not who might need to be taken out.

#### D) Modified functions
None — this round is purely additive (one new server function, one new UI section). No existing
function's behavior changed.

#### E) Sheet configuration
No sheet schema change. The actual Drive Group-membership update this report enables is a manual
step an Administrator performs outside the Dashboard, in the Google Group's own "Add people" UI,
using the pasted list.

#### F) Trigger configuration
No change.

#### G) Test results (only what was actually executed)
- `node --check` on the full, updated `Code.gs` — passes.
- Python `HTMLParser`-based tag-balance check on the full, updated `Dashboard.html` — no
  mismatched/unclosed tags.
- Duplicate static `id="..."` scan and duplicate top-level `function`/`var` name scan across both
  files — zero duplicates.
- `getAuthorizedEmailsForGroupSync()` verified against its exact shipped function body (extracted via
  `sed` from `Code.gs`, run together with the real `normalizeEmail_()`, with `requireSuperAdminViewer_()`
  and `readConfiguredUserRoles_()` mocked via `new Function(...)`) — 28/28 checks passed, covering:
  SuperAdmin gating (throws and returns nothing when the auth check fails, rather than silently
  returning a partial/empty report); correct per-bucket counts with no cross-bucket dedup bleed (a
  person who is both a static Admin and a Classroom teacher appears once in each of those two
  buckets, but only once in the deduplicated `totalUnique`/`allEmails`); correct within-bucket dedup
  (the same teacher on two different courses is counted once in `teachers`); blank/whitespace-only
  entries in a static list are skipped rather than producing an empty-string "email"; a fully empty
  input (no static roles, no configured overrides, no courses) still returns a well-formed, empty
  report rather than throwing; `allEmails` is always sorted and free of duplicates; `generatedAt` is
  a valid, parseable timestamp; and each bucket's rows carry their expected extra fields (`role` for
  static/configured rows, `name` for teacher/student rows).
- NOT independently testable in this environment (no live Google Workspace/Drive access): the actual
  end-to-end paste into the "American Charitable Tamil Society" Group's "Add people" box, and whether
  Google Groups accepts a large newline-separated paste of emails in one action (this is a reasonable
  assumption based on how that UI is commonly described to work, not something verified against the
  live Group here). The Super Admin performing the paste is the only way to confirm this directly.

#### Self-review flags
- **This report can go stale between generation and paste.** It's a snapshot at the moment
  `getAuthorizedEmailsForGroupSync()` runs — if a teacher/student roster changes or a role is
  reassigned between generating the report and actually pasting it into the Group, the pasted list
  won't reflect that change. Regenerating right before pasting minimizes this, but nothing in the UI
  currently warns if the report is "old" (e.g., generated several minutes/hours earlier in the same
  session). A future round could add a simple "generated N minutes ago, consider regenerating" nudge
  if this proves to matter in practice.
- **This only ever grows the Group's intended membership — it never tells the Super Admin who to
  remove.** The report lists who *should* be in the Group; it deliberately does not diff that against
  the Group's actual current membership (doing so would require an Admin Directory API read, which is
  exactly the additional scope/capability the user chose not to take on this round). So someone who
  left the school, or whose access should have been revoked, stays in the Group until a Super Admin
  manually notices and removes them — the in-UI note says to check for this, but nothing enforces it.
  If stale-membership removal becomes a real operational problem, that's the natural next round, and
  would need the same manual-vs-automated tradeoff conversation this round already had.
- **The domain-fallback "authorized" population is invisible to this report by design, not by
  oversight.** Anyone whose only claim to Dashboard access is "their email is at one of the four
  allowed domains, with no other specific role" will not appear anywhere in this report's output, and
  if their account isn't already covered by the Group some other way, they will still hit the Round 49
  permission error even after this round's Group sync is done. This is the direct, known consequence
  of the user's explicit choice to avoid the Admin Directory API automation that would have been
  needed to enumerate that population — documented here so a future round doesn't mistake this for a
  bug.

### Sept 2026, fifty-first round — login broken for ALL users: ground-truth Drive sharing check finds the real cause (no code change)

**Trigger**: "All the user are facing login issue. revisit all the user login issue. give me final one
working soluation." — an escalation from Round 49/50's "a few users" framing to everyone being locked
out. This round is diagnostic and operational only — **no `Code.gs`/`Dashboard.html` changes were
needed or made**; the Round 48-50 code (retry logic, permission-error detection, the honest error
message, the Group Sync Report tool) is all still correct and was re-confirmed working as designed.

#### What changed from Round 49/50's assumption
Round 49 diagnosed a per-account Drive-sharing gap from a user's Share-dialog screenshot, read as
"General access: the Google Group 'American Charitable Tamil Society', Editor." This round queried
the **live Drive permissions** for both spreadsheets the Dashboard depends on, via the Google Drive
connector now available in this session (`get_file_permissions`/`get_file_metadata`) — actual
ground truth, not a screenshot read at a glance:

```
TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID  ("APS School - Live Dashboard"):
  { type: "domain", emailAddress: "amchats.org", role: "writer" }
  { type: "user",   emailAddress: "info@avvaiyarpadasalai.org", role: "owner" }

ATTENDANCE_SPREADSHEET_ID ("Attendance" workbook):
  { type: "domain", emailAddress: "amchats.org", role: "writer" }
  { type: "user",   emailAddress: "info@avvaiyarpadasalai.org", role: "owner" }
```

Both are **`type: "domain"`, not `type: "group"`** — there is no Group grant on either file right now.
General access is restricted to accounts on the single domain `amchats.org`, plus the owner
(`info@avvaiyarpadasalai.org`) who always has access regardless of sharing. Whatever the Share dialog
displayed at the time of the Round 49 screenshot, this is what Drive's API reports as the actual
permission set today, on both files identically.

#### Why this explains "ALL users," not just "a few"
`SUPERADMIN_EMAILS`, every entry in `ADMIN_EMAILS`, and every entry in `HEADMASTER_EMAILS` are on
`avvaiyarpadasalai.org` — not one of them is on `amchats.org`. Since the entire login flow
(`authorizeDashboardAccess` → `getAuthenticatedAPSUser` → `readAllCoursesFromCache_` →
`getOrCreateCacheSheet_` → `getWorkbook_` → `SpreadsheetApp.openById(TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID)`) opens
this exact spreadsheet under the **calling user's own Google identity** (the app is deployed "Execute
as: User accessing the web app" — see Round 49 §C), and Classroom teacher/student accounts almost
certainly also carry `avvaiyarpadasalai.org` addresses (matching the `_apsNNN@avvaiyarpadasalai.org`
pattern `extractAPSID_()` looks for), essentially the entire real user population — SuperAdmin, every
Admin, every Headmaster, every teacher, every student — has zero Drive access to a workbook the
login flow cannot function without. Only the small number of people (if any) with an `amchats.org`
Google account, plus the file owner, can currently log in. That matches "ALL users" far better than
Round 49's per-account read did.

This is not a regression from Round 48/49/50's code — `isPermissionDeniedError_()` /
`openSpreadsheetByIdWithRetry_()` / `getWorkbook_()`'s catch block are doing exactly what they were
built to do: failing fast and returning the honest, actionable "Your Google account does not
currently have access to the APS Dashboard's shared data" message instead of a misleading generic
one. The code was never the problem; the Drive sharing underneath it is.

#### Why a same-Workspace "domain" share can't be the permanent fix here
`APS_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` spans four separate email domains (`avvaiyarpadasalai.org`, `amchats.org`,
`namaps.org`, `apsamerica.org`). Google Drive's `type: "domain"` sharing only grants access within a
single Workspace customer's domain(s) — it cannot be used to grant "anyone at domain X" access for a
domain that isn't part of the same Workspace account as the file owner. If these four domains are
separate Workspace tenants (as the current single-domain grant scoped to `amchats.org` alone — not
all four — suggests), no amount of domain-type sharing tweaks can cover all four; either every
individual account must be shared explicitly (what the Round 50 "Group Sync Report" tool was built to
support, via a Google Group with individually-added cross-domain members — Groups, unlike domain
shares, can hold external members from any domain), or general link-based access removes the
domain/group dependency entirely.

#### The fix (operational, outside code — no deployment needed once done)
Recommended to the user: change **General access** on both spreadsheets (main "APS School - Live
Dashboard", ID `1rlFMiXDMVaBcZS89AL0OC5TYeXz4PIZyXXboYoDGzX0`, and the Attendance workbook, ID
`1GtV0M2_BP3XDj5bzVKhu4BRq3c6EnP8-nl809pSqFxE`) to **"Anyone with the link" → Editor**, replacing the
`amchats.org`-only domain restriction. This is the only option that structurally covers all four
domains permanently with zero ongoing maintenance, and is safe in this app's specific context because
end users never see or use the raw spreadsheet link — they only ever interact through the Apps
Script Web App, whose own login gate (`isApsEmailAllowed_` against `APS_ALLOWED_DOMAINS`, then
`getViewerRole_`) remains the actual access boundary a real visitor experiences. The alternative —
finish wiring up the Round 50 Group-based approach with a Group whose members are added individually
across all four domains — was offered as the tighter-but-higher-maintenance option, with the caveat
that adding external-domain members to a Group can itself be blocked by Workspace admin policy and
would need to be verified. No `share_file` call was made by Claude in this session; the change was
left to the user (or their explicit go-ahead) since it grants broad new access and is exactly the
kind of action this session treats as requiring the user's own confirmation.

#### G) Test results (only what was actually executed)
- `mcp__Google_Drive__get_file_permissions` and `get_file_metadata` called directly against both
  `TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID` and `ATTENDANCE_SPREADSHEET_ID` — live ground truth, not inferred from a
  screenshot. Both confirmed identical: `type: "domain"`, `amchats.org`, `writer`, plus the owner.
  No `type: "group"` or `type: "anyone"` permission present on either file.
- Re-read the full login call chain in `Code.gs` (`doGet`, `authorizeDashboardAccess`,
  `validateApsSession`, `getAuthenticatedAPSUser`, `getViewerRole_`, `readAllCoursesFromCache_`,
  `getOrCreateCacheSheet_`, `getWorkbook_`, `openSpreadsheetByIdWithRetry_`,
  `isPermissionDeniedError_`) end-to-end to confirm every path converges on opening
  `TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID` under the caller's own identity, with no alternate route that could
  succeed independent of this file's sharing.
- Cross-checked `SUPERADMIN_EMAILS`/`ADMIN_EMAILS`/`HEADMASTER_EMAILS` domain distribution (all
  `avvaiyarpadasalai.org`) against the live `amchats.org`-only grant to confirm the "ALL users, not
  just a few" scope is consistent with the evidence rather than assumed.
- No code was changed this round, so no `node --check`/tag-balance/duplicate-id re-verification was
  needed — `Code.gs` and `Dashboard.html` are unchanged from Round 50's delivered/verified state.
- NOT verified: whether the user has actually applied the sharing change yet, and whether an
  affected (non-`amchats.org`) account can log in once it is. That confirmation can only happen after
  the user makes the Drive change and a real affected user reloads the Dashboard.

#### Self-review flags
- **This diagnosis supersedes, rather than contradicts, Round 49's.** Round 49 was correct that *some*
  Drive-sharing gap was the cause; it just hadn't yet had ground-truth Drive API access to confirm the
  gap was a domain-vs-domain mismatch affecting essentially everyone, rather than a handful of
  individual accounts missing from an otherwise-correct Group. Both rounds' code changes (retry logic,
  honest error classification, the Group Sync Report tool) remain correct and useful regardless of
  which sharing model the user ultimately picks.
- **If the user instead completes the Group-based route**, the Round 50 "Generate Group Sync Report"
  tool's output remains exactly what's needed to populate that Group's membership — this round doesn't
  make that tool obsolete, it just clarifies that a Group grant (not a domain grant) is what has to
  replace the current `amchats.org`-only permission for the Group route to actually work.
- **Claude did not execute the sharing change.** Per this session's own rules, broadening a file's
  general access is treated as requiring the user's explicit go-ahead rather than being done
  proactively, even though the Drive connector available in this session is technically capable of
  making the change directly. If the user confirms, Claude can apply it directly rather than the user
  doing it by hand in the Drive UI.

### Sept 2026, fifty-second round — Owner-execution migration: the underlying Sheets/Classroom data is no longer shared with any visitor's own Google account (implementation)

**Trigger**: "convert this project to web app and dont want to share any data with user. Give me
design to implement this his avaiable google resource", followed by "create a working code to
implement this design and we want to run the test environemnt before moveing to prod." This round
closes the entire class of bug Rounds 48-51 fought (a visitor's OWN Drive access to
`TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID`/`ATTENDANCE_SPREADSHEET_ID` gating whether they could log in at all) by
removing the dependency completely, rather than continuing to manage it via Drive sharing. The design
doc (`dashboard-owner-execution-migration-design.md`, delivered earlier this round) covers the
options considered; this entry documents the actual implementation.

#### The architectural change
The Web App's `executeAs` moves from `USER_ACCESSING` (each visitor's own Drive/Classroom identity is
used — the source of every Round 48-51 sharing bug) to `USER_DEPLOYING` ("Execute as: Me" — every
Sheets/Classroom/Drive call always runs as the script owner, regardless of who is visiting). No
visitor's Google account is ever given access to the underlying spreadsheets again; the Dashboard is
the only surface that ever touches them.

The tradeoff `USER_DEPLOYING` forces: `Session.getActiveUser().getEmail()` no longer reliably
identifies the VISITOR server-side — it resolves to the owner's identity (or blank) for everyone else.
The previous login flow (`authorizeDashboardAccess`/`validateApsSession`, which trusted
`Session.getActiveUser()` as the source of truth once a typed email was checked against it) cannot
work under this model and has been removed entirely. It is replaced by:

1. **Google Sign-In (Google Identity Services) client-side** — the visitor authenticates with their
   own Google account via a standard "Sign in with Google" button (declarative `#g_id_onload`/
   `.g_id_signin` markup in `Dashboard.html`'s login screen; no manual `google.accounts.id.*` init
   call, avoiding a load-order race with the GIS script tag in `<head>`). This produces a signed
   Google **ID token** — cryptographic proof of identity from Google itself, not a client-side claim.
2. **Server-side verification** (`Code.gs`, new): `establishSession(idToken)` verifies the ID token
   against Google's `tokeninfo` endpoint (`verifyGoogleIdToken_()` — checks `aud` against
   `OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` and `email_verified`), resolves the verified email to a role via the EXISTING
   `getViewerRoleForEmail_()` logic (the `getViewerRole_(courses)` role-resolution rules themselves —
   static role lists, Classroom teacher/student membership, the four-domain fallback — are unchanged;
   only what supplies the email changed), and — if authorized — issues an opaque, random session token
   (`Utilities.getUuid()`) stored in `CacheService.getScriptCache()` for up to 6 hours
   (`SESSION_TTL_SECONDS`).
3. **Session-token RPC on every other call.** Every other client-facing function now takes that
   session token as its first argument and calls `requireValidSession_(sessionToken)` (throws
   `SESSION_EXPIRED: ...` if missing/expired/unknown) before doing anything else. Client-side,
   `Dashboard.html`'s new `apsScriptRun` wrapper (a `Proxy` around `google.script.run`) transparently
   injects the current session token as the first argument of every call routed through it, so none of
   this file's 72 real `google.script.run` call sites — including the two dynamic
   `[handlerName](...)` dispatch sites for Class/Grade-Change and Reference-Letter approvals — needed
   their own argument lists touched. `apsScriptRun` also intercepts a `SESSION_EXPIRED` failure from
   ANY call and quietly routes the visitor back to the Login screen instead of surfacing a raw error
   to whatever success/failure handler happened to be attached to that particular call.
   `establishSession(idToken)` itself is the one function still called on plain `google.script.run` —
   it is what PRODUCES the token, so there is nothing to inject yet.
4. **Returning-visitor resume, not re-typed each visit.** The session token (not a bare email claim)
   is cached client-side in `localStorage` (`apsDashboardSession_v2` — a new key, distinct from the
   pre-migration `v1` format, so a stale v1 entry is never mistaken for a live session) with a 30-day/
   8-hour-idle local expiry on top of the server's own 6-hour token TTL. On page load,
   `apsBootstrapSession()` resumes silently via `getAuthenticatedAPSUser()` — a genuinely expired
   server-side token surfaces as `SESSION_EXPIRED` and is caught by `apsScriptRun`'s own interception,
   the same code path a mid-session expiry uses.

#### `PropertiesService.getUserProperties()` — a latent bug this round also had to fix
Found via a targeted sweep, not part of the original design doc: `getStudentLoginNoticeStatus()`/
`acceptStudentLoginNotice()` used `PropertiesService.getUserProperties()` to remember, per student,
whether the onboarding notice had been accepted. Under `USER_ACCESSING` this correctly keys per
visitor; under `USER_DEPLOYING` it would silently resolve to the OWNER's properties for every visitor
(properties are keyed by *effective user*, which becomes the owner for everyone once the deployment
changes) — every student would appear to share one acceptance record. Fixed by switching both
functions to `PropertiesService.getScriptProperties()` with the verified email embedded directly in
the property key (`STUDENT_NOTICE_PROP_PREFIX + email + '_' + ...`), which is correct under any
execution mode since it never depends on "whose properties am I in."

#### Implementation — `Code.gs`, `Dashboard.html`, `appsscript.json`
- **`Code.gs`**: the old identity block (`getAuthenticatedGoogleEmail`, `authorizeDashboardAccess`,
  `validateApsSession`) is replaced by `verifyGoogleIdToken_`, `establishSession`,
  `requireValidSession_`, `endSession`, `buildAuthenticatedUserPayload_`, and a rewritten
  `getAuthenticatedAPSUser(sessionToken)`. `getViewerRole_(courses)` is now a thin, LEGACY-ONLY
  wrapper around a new pure `getViewerRoleForEmail_(email, courses)` (identical role logic, explicit
  email argument) — its one remaining caller is `doGet()`'s cosmetic browser-tab title, which already
  tolerates degrading to role `'none'` for anyone but the owner and must never be used for real
  authorization. Every one of the ~66 other client-facing functions (every `google.script.run` target
  in `Dashboard.html`, plus 2 currently-unreachable/orphaned functions migrated for consistency —
  `setAttendancePresentThresholdPct`, `getAttendanceRecordsForAdmin`) now takes `sessionToken` as its
  first parameter and starts with `requireValidSession_(sessionToken)` instead of reading
  `Session.getActiveUser()` directly.
- **`Dashboard.html`**: the "type your APS email" login screen and its `apsScreenMismatch` "Google
  Account Mismatch" screen (meaningless once there is no typed-email-vs-Google-identity comparison to
  make) are removed. The login screen is now a Google Sign-In button. The `apsScriptRun` wrapper and
  its supporting `apsSessionToken`/`apsIsSessionExpiredError_`/`apsHandleSessionExpired_` helpers are
  new, placed near the top of the script. `apsShowAuthError()`'s deployment-hint copy, which used to
  tell an Admin to set "Execute as: User accessing the web app" (now actively WRONG advice under this
  architecture), is rewritten to point at `OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` configuration instead. `OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`
  itself is read into the page from `Code.gs` via a single GAS template scriptlet
  (`<?= OAUTH_CLIENT_ID ?>` on the `#g_id_onload` div) rather than being duplicated as a second,
  driftable constant in the HTML file.
- **`appsscript.json`**: `webapp.executeAs` changed `USER_ACCESSING` → `USER_DEPLOYING`;
  `webapp.access` changed `DOMAIN` → `ANYONE` (required for `USER_DEPLOYING`; the real access boundary
  a visitor experiences is still `isApsEmailAllowed_`/role resolution inside `establishSession()`, not
  this setting — `ANYONE` here only means "anyone can load the login page," not "anyone can see data").
  `oauthScopes` unchanged (`script.external_request`, needed for `UrlFetchApp.fetch()` to reach
  `oauth2.googleapis.com/tokeninfo`, was already present from a prior round).

### Sept 2026, fifty-third round — Google Sign-In button replaced with a redirect flow, after live testing found it structurally incompatible with Apps Script

**Trigger**: after the user finished the fifty-second round's setup (created a standard GCP project,
configured the OAuth consent screen, created an OAuth Client ID) and registered `https://script.google.com`
under Authorized JavaScript origins as instructed, sign-in failed with **"Error 401: invalid_client —
no registered origin."** This round traces the actual cause (using the browser tool, connected to the
user's own linked computer, to inspect the live deployment directly — not guessed at), and replaces the
Round 52 client-side Google Identity Services button with a server-side OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code
redirect flow.

#### Root cause, found by inspecting the live deployment
Navigating to the real `/exec` URL and reading `window.location`/the page's DOM directly (rather than
reasoning about it in the abstract) showed:
```
topOrigin: "https://script.google.com"          <- what the address bar shows
iframe#sandboxFrame src origin:
  "https://n-epgcby64lzjtlpdnck265f7ppnn3owa2ctf2kdy-0lu-script.googleusercontent.com"
```
Apps Script renders EVERY Web App's actual content — Dashboard.html, in this case — inside a sandboxed
iframe on a `*.script.googleusercontent.com` subdomain, even for a completely ordinary, non-embedded
direct visit. This is not something `setXFrameOptionsMode()` controls (that only governs whether a
THIRD PARTY can iframe this Dashboard elsewhere) — it's how Apps Script serves Web App content,
unconditionally. Google Cloud Console explicitly refuses to let a `googleusercontent.com` address be
registered as an OAuth "Authorized JavaScript origin" ("Invalid Origin: uses a forbidden domain"),
since that domain hosts many different users' content and allowing it would let anyone impersonate an
authorized origin. GIS's "Sign in with Google" button checks the page's OWN origin (i.e., the
sandboxFrame's origin, not the visible address bar) against the OAuth Client's registered origins — so
it can never succeed for an Apps Script Web App, with no configuration able to fix it. Round 52's self-
review flagged "GIS inside an iframe" as a risk but incorrectly assumed it only applied to third-party
embedding; it applies to every deployment, always. See the correction added to that round's self-review
section above.

#### The fix: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow (redirect-based), not the GIS button
Replaced entirely with the older, more classical OAuth pattern, which several other Apps Script Web
Apps use for exactly this reason:
1. **Login screen is now a plain link**, not a script-rendered button: `<a target="_top" href="...">`
   (the file's existing `<base target="_top">` makes this work — anchor `target="_top"` navigation out
   of an iframe is a basic, always-permitted browser primitive, unlike scripted cross-origin
   `window.top.location` access, which is largely blocked). The href is a Google OAuth consent-screen
   URL Code.gs's `doGet()` builds fresh on every render (`buildGoogleAuthUrl_()`), including a
   single-use `state` nonce (`OAUTH_STATE_CACHE_PREFIX_`, 10-minute `CacheService` entry) for
   best-effort CSRF/replay protection — Apps Script has no simple per-visitor cookie/session mechanism
   to bind this more strongly before the visitor is identified, so the nonce is looked up BY its own
   value as the cache key, which is the practical option available here.
2. Google redirects the browser back to the Web App's OWN `/exec` URL with a one-time `code` (this
   redirect target is what has to be registered — under **Authorized redirect URIs**, an exact-URL-match
   mechanism, NOT the origin-check "Authorized JavaScript origins" field GIS needed. `script.google.com`
   addresses are explicitly permitted there).
3. `doGet(e)` (`Code.gs`) now does double duty: on this callback visit (`e.parameter.code` present), it
   exchanges the code for tokens entirely server-side (`exchangeCodeForTokens_()`, a POST to
   `oauth2.googleapis.com/token` using a new `OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` constant — the one place in the whole
   app that secret is used, and it never reaches the browser since it's server-side-only Apps Script
   source), verifies the resulting `id_token` (reusing Round 52's `verifyGoogleIdToken_()` unchanged),
   and resolves the session (a new shared helper, `establishSessionForVerifiedClaims_()`, factored out
   of Round 52's `establishSession(idToken)` body so both the old direct-token path — kept, unused by
   the client now, but harmless — and this new redirect path share the identical role-resolution/
   session-issuance logic). The resulting session token/user (or a failure code) is baked directly into
   THIS SAME render of Dashboard.html as `APS_BOOT_SESSION_TOKEN`/`APS_BOOT_USER`/`APS_BOOT_ERROR`
   template values — no second round trip needed, since the server already has everything it needs to
   render the fully-logged-in page in one shot.
4. `Dashboard.html`'s `apsBootstrapSession()` checks these boot values FIRST, before its existing
   remembered-localStorage-session check: if present, it calls `apsHandleAuthResult()` — the exact same
   function Round 52 built for the button flow's success/failure handling — so the Permission Review
   screen, country picker, and denied/error screens all work identically to before with zero UI changes.
   A `cancelled` code (visitor clicked "Cancel" on Google's own consent screen, surfaced via
   `e.parameter.error`) quietly returns to the Login screen rather than showing an error. Reloading the
   page while `?code=...` is still in the URL correctly fails gracefully (Google's codes are single-use)
   with a "couldn't complete the sign-in, try again" message rather than a crash.
5. The Round 52 GIS script tag, `#g_id_onload`/`.g_id_signin` markup, and `apsHandleGoogleCredential()`
   are all removed from `Dashboard.html`. `establishSession(idToken)` remains in `Code.gs` as a directly-
   callable RPC (harmless, unused by the current client) in case a future, different client ever wants
   to hand it an already-obtained ID token directly.

#### What the user needs to change in their OAuth Client (both TEST and production)
- Remove/ignore any **Authorized JavaScript origins** entry from Round 52 — it was never going to work
  and Google won't accept the `googleusercontent.com` one that would actually be needed.
- Add the Web App's exact `/exec` URL (the FULL path, not just the origin) under **Authorized redirect
  URIs**.
- Copy the Client ID **and now also the Client Secret** into `Code.gs`'s `OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`/
  `OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` constants (both were previously requested from the user and are now filled in
  directly in the delivered `Code.gs`, rather than left as placeholders, since implementing and testing
  this round required them).
- `test-environment-setup-guide.md` and this doc's fifty-second-round "One-time setup" section have
  both been corrected to describe this flow instead of the abandoned one.

- `node --check` on both `Code.gs` and the extracted `Dashboard.html` `<script>` body (with GAS

  `<?!= ... ?>` scriptlet syntax isn't valid JavaScript on its own) — both passed.
- Full-file duplicate top-level `function`/`var` scan on both files — zero duplicates.
- HTML tag-balance check on `Dashboard.html` — zero mismatches, empty stack at EOF.
- Cross-referenced every `apsScriptRun` terminal call target in `Dashboard.html` against `Code.gs`'s

- Confirmed via grep that `Code.gs`'s `OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`/`OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` constants no longer contain

- NOT verified (cannot be, from this session, even with browser access): a full click-through of the
