  end-to-end themselves; this round's testing confirmed the DIAGNOSIS (via live DOM inspection) and the
  CODE's correctness (syntax, structure, cross-references) but not a live successful sign-in, since the
  OAuth Client's redirect URI had not yet been updated at the time this round's code was written.

#### Self-review flags
- **This round is itself a correction of an incomplete verification gap in Round 52** — flagged
  directly in that round's own self-review update above, rather than glossed over. The lesson carried
  forward: for any browser-facing auth mechanism on an unfamiliar hosting platform (Apps Script's
  iframe-sandboxing behavior here), a real live click-through against an actual deployment is not
  optional polish — it is the only thing that would have caught this, and neither the Node.js harness
  nor any static check could have.
- **The CSRF/replay `state` nonce check in `doGet()` is deliberately best-effort, not strict.** Apps
  Script Web Apps have no simple mechanism to bind a nonce to a specific visitor's browser BEFORE they
  are identified (no easy pre-auth cookie/session primitive), so the nonce is checked by looking itself
  up as a cache key rather than being tied to anything more specific — this provides real protection
  against a replayed/guessed `state` value being reused after its 10-minute window, but not the full
  guarantee a cookie-bound nonce would provide. Given the actual authorization `code` itself is single-
  use and short-lived (Google's own protection), and the whole exchange still requires
  `OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` to complete, this residual gap was judged an acceptable trade-off for an Apps
  Script app with no cookie/session infrastructure to build on, rather than a reason to invent one.
- **`establishSession(idToken)` and its GIS-era doc comments are now vestigial** — kept in `Code.gs` for
  API completeness (nothing currently calls it, but it is harmless and correctly shares logic with the
  new path via `establishSessionForVerifiedClaims_()`), not because any current code path exercises it.
  A future cleanup round could remove it if it's confirmed to still be unused.

#### Addendum — `Error 400: redirect_uri_mismatch` after the redirect URI was added
After the user added the `/exec` URL to Authorized redirect URIs as instructed above, sign-in still
failed, now with a *different* Google error: `Error 400: redirect_uri_mismatch` (previously it was
`Error 401: invalid_client — no registered origin`, the JS-origins problem this round already fixed).
Decoded the protobuf-encoded `authError` payload in the failure URL directly (`base64.urlsafe_b64decode`
on the `authError` query parameter) rather than guessing, and it embeds the EXACT `redirect_uri` Google
received:
```
https://script.google.com/a/avvaiyarpadasalai.org/macros/s/AKfycbxbUpa3SJKbxLt95NtTffiE-Bz62zJ0K4ncLzKFbIaK3n2w2ZuPNtaeooZtPYVrhhd_/exec
```
— which does **not** match the URL the user had registered (copied from their browser's address bar):
```
https://script.google.com/a/macros/avvaiyarpadasalai.org/s/AKfycbxbUpa3SJKbxLt95NtTffiE-Bz62zJ0K4ncLzKFbIaK3n2w2ZuPNtaeooZtPYVrhhd_/exec
```
Note the swapped path segments — `macros`/`avvaiyarpadasalai.org` appear in the opposite order. This is
a known Apps Script quirk for domain-bound (Google Workspace) Web Apps: `ScriptApp.getService().getUrl()`
(what `buildGoogleAuthUrl_()`/`exchangeCodeForTokens_()` actually use to build/match the `redirect_uri`)
can return a different URL path layout than what the browser's own address bar shows for the exact same
deployment. Since OAuth redirect URI matching is an exact string match, the address-bar-copied URL was
never going to work on its own.
**Fix given to the user:** add the `ScriptApp.getService().getUrl()`-style URL above as an *additional*
Authorized redirect URI entry (keeping the address-bar one too is harmless), save, wait a minute or two
for propagation, and retry. Re-tested live via the connected browser tool immediately after the first
report and reproduced the identical `redirect_uri_mismatch` with the identical mismatched `redirect_uri`
in the decoded error payload — confirming the diagnosis came from the live deployment's actual behavior,
not guesswork. **NOT yet verified**: whether adding the second URI resolves it — awaiting the user's
next attempt/report.

### Sept 2026, fifty-fourth round — hardcoded secrets/IDs/staff-email rosters moved to Script Properties

#### Trigger
User asked, in effect: "identify the hardcoded values in the code, and put them somewhere safer that
isn't visible to everyone" — prompted directly by the fact that `OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`/`OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`
(the real, live Google OAuth credentials, added in the fifty-third round above) were sitting as literal
text in `Code.gs`, which is copied into this project's local sync folder AND the Claude Project docs —
i.e. the real Client Secret existed in plaintext in at least three places. Asked the user to scope the
change (AskUserQuestion — just the OAuth credentials, credentials + resource IDs, or everything
including staff email rosters); the user chose the broadest option, everything.

#### What changed
Apps Script has no dedicated "environment variables" feature. Script Properties (Apps Script editor >
Project Settings > Script Properties) is the closest equivalent already in use elsewhere in this project
(e.g. the pre-existing `TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID` Script Property) — values live only inside the script
project itself, never in this source file's text, so they're absent from any copy of `Code.gs` that gets
exported, pasted, or shared.

Added two small loader helpers near the top of `Code.gs` — `getConfigString_(key, fallback)` and
`getConfigList_(key, fallback)` (the latter `JSON.parse`s the stored text into an array, since Script
Properties can only store strings) — and replaced every one of the following literal values with a
call to one of them. **Deliberately never throws at module-load time**: a missing property silently
returns `fallback` (default `''`/`[]`) so one unset property degrades only the specific feature that
needs it, not the entire script for every visitor including the public sign-in page. The functions that
actually depend on a value being present check for an empty result themselves and throw a clear,
specific setup error at that point instead — see "Guarded usage sites" below.

Full list of values moved, and the exact Script Property name each now reads:

| Category | Script Property name(s) | Previously |
|---|---|---|
| OAuth credential | `OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` | literal in `Code.gs` |
| OAuth credential (real secret) | `OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` | literal in `Code.gs` |
| Resource ID | `TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID` | had a hardcoded fallback default (`TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID_DEFAULT_`), now removed entirely |
| Resource ID | `ATTENDANCE_SPREADSHEET_ID` | literal in `Code.gs` |
| Resource ID | `REFERENCE_LETTER_TEMPLATE_DOC_ID` | literal in `Code.gs` |
| Resource ID (optional) | `REFERENCE_LETTER_PDF_ARCHIVE_FOLDER_ID` | literal (blank) in `Code.gs` |
| Staff roster (JSON array) | `SUPERADMIN_EMAILS` | literal array |
| Staff roster (JSON array) | `ADMIN_EMAILS` | literal array |
| Staff roster (JSON array) | `HEADMASTER_EMAILS` | literal array |
| Staff roster (JSON array) | `ROSTER_HIDDEN_STAFF_ADDITIONAL_EMAILS` | literal array |
| Staff roster (JSON array) | `VCFO_AMCHATS_BOD_EMAILS` | literal array |
| Staff roster (JSON array) | `GRADE_CHANGE_APPROVER_EMAILS` | literal array |
| Staff roster (JSON array) | `REFERENCE_LETTER_APPROVER_EMAILS` | literal array |
| Staff roster (JSON array) | `HIDDEN_TEACHER_EMAIL_PREFIXES` | literal array (mix of a generic prefix and specific staff emails) |
| Staff roster (JSON array) | `ON_CALL_ADDITIONAL_NAMED_TEACHER_EMAILS` | literal array |
| Single email | `ON_CALL_NAMED_TEACHER_EMAIL` | literal string |
| Single email | `FINAL_APPROVER_EMAIL` | literal string |
| Single email | `REFERENCE_LETTER_FINAL_APPROVER_EMAIL` | literal string |
| Single email | `REFERENCE_LETTER_COMPLETION_CC_EMAIL` | literal string |
| Single email | `APS_DASHBOARD_EMAIL_CC` | literal string |

Deliberately left alone: generic, non-personal config like `APS_ALLOWED_DOMAINS`, `HIDDEN_TEACHER_NAME_PREFIXES`,
numeric thresholds/windows, sheet/tab names, and UI label strings — these were not part of the scoped
list shown to the user before they chose "everything," and moving them would have widened the change
without a security or privacy benefit.

#### Guarded usage sites (so a missing property fails loudly, but only where it's actually used)
- `buildGoogleAuthUrl_()` — throws immediately if `OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` is blank.
- `exchangeCodeForTokens_()` — throws immediately if `OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` or `OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` is blank.
- `doGet()` — the call to `buildGoogleAuthUrl_()` used to be unguarded; now wrapped in `try/catch` so a
  missing `OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` sets `APS_BOOT_ERROR` (code `oauth_not_configured`, shown via the existing
  `apsShowAuthError('authorization_failure', ...)` path in `Dashboard.html` — no client-side change
  needed) and still renders the page, instead of crashing `doGet()` entirely for every visitor.
- `getWorkbook_()` — now throws immediately, with a specific message, if `TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID` is
  blank, **instead of** silently falling through to the `CACHE_SHEET_ID_KEY` auto-create-a-different-
  spreadsheet branch. This is a deliberate, additional safety improvement: removing
  `TARGET_SPREADSHEET_ID_DEFAULT_`'s hardcoded fallback (per this round's actual ask) would otherwise
  have reopened the exact thirty-fourth-round regression (a missing Script Property silently resolving
  to the wrong spreadsheet) that an earlier round already fixed once. Loud-and-clear beats
  silent-and-wrong.
- `getAttendanceWorkbook_()` — left as-is; a blank `ATTENDANCE_SPREADSHEET_ID` already surfaces as a
  clear "could not open" error via its existing try/catch (no silent-auto-create fallback exists there
  to reopen), so no additional guard was needed.

#### One-time migration (NOT delivered as a project file — see chat)
Deliberately did **not** write the actual current values (the OAuth secret, staff emails, resource IDs)
into any persisted file — not `Code.gs`, not a new `.gs` file delivered to the local sync folder, and
not a Claude Project doc — since doing so would just recreate the exposure this round exists to remove.
Instead, a one-time migration function (`PropertiesService.getScriptProperties().setProperties({...})`,
setting all ~20 properties above from their current live values in a single call) was given to the user

under Project Settings > Script Properties, then delete. Chat history is the one place this content was
always going to exist regardless (the user supplied the real Client ID/Secret directly in chat in the
fifty-third round), so this doesn't newly widen exposure; every FILE this round touches is clean.

#### Test results

- Full-file duplicate top-level `function`/`var` scan — zero duplicates.
- Grepped `Code.gs` for the literal OAuth secret, both spreadsheet IDs, the reference-letter template
  doc ID, and `SUPERADMIN_EMAILS`'s one entry — zero matches anywhere in the file.
- Grepped for every `@avvaiyarpadasalai.org`/`@amchats.org`/`@apsamerica.org`/`@namaps.org` address still

#### Self-review flags
- **The migration function itself is a temporary, throwaway artifact by design** — it necessarily
  contains the real secret and staff emails (there's no way to seed Script Properties from their current

### Sept 2026, fifty-sixth round — Teacher's Reference Letter tab reported not clickable; full click/RPC audit

#### Trigger
User reported: "teacher role reference letter tab is not clickable. scan all the tabl and funtionality are
working and fix this accoundagly" — both a specific bug report and a request for a broader audit.

#### Root cause
Already fixed, but apparently not yet in the user's live deployment. `Dashboard.html` contains a comment,
already present before this round's work began (i.e. from some earlier round of this ongoing engagement,
predating this conversation's own history), documenting the exact bug: the `rl-tab` / `rl-approvals-tab`
buttons were shown/hidden correctly by `updateReferenceLetterTabVisibility()` but — unlike every other
tab — never had a `click` listener registered at all, so clicking either did nothing. The fix
(`document.getElementById('rl-tab').addEventListener('click', function () { switchView('referenceLetter'); });`,
and the same for `rl-approvals-tab`) is present in the current `Dashboard.html`, alongside the other eight
tab buttons' listeners it sits next to.

Attempted to confirm directly against the live deployment via the connected browser tool (as in the
fifty-third round's OAuth investigation), but Apps Script Web Apps render their actual content inside a
sandboxed, cross-origin `*.script.googleusercontent.com` iframe — the same fact discovered in that round —
which blocks this session's browser-automation tools from reading the iframe's DOM/JS/console content from
the top `script.google.com` frame (`get_page_text`/`read_page` returned empty; coordinate-based clicking
inside the frame also failed with a frame-attribution error). This is a tooling limitation, not a
statement about the live deployment's actual state — it could not be used to positively confirm or rule
out whether the fix is live. Given the user's report, the most likely explanation is a stale deployment:
the Apps Script project is still serving a `Dashboard.html` version pasted in before this fix existed.

#### Broader audit performed (the "scan all tabs and functionality" ask)
Since the exact bug class here — a static HTML button with a fixed `id` that nothing ever calls
`addEventListener` on — is easy to repeat elsewhere, wrote small Python scripts to check for it and
adjacent bug classes systematically across the whole file, not just re-check this one spot:
1. **Every top-level view tab** (`tabClasses`, `tabOnboarding`, `tabKb`, `tabClassChange`,
   `tabAssignClassroom`, `tabUserRoles`, `rl-tab`, `rl-approvals-tab`, `tabAttendance`) — confirmed each
   has a `switchView()` case, a view-container display toggle, and a `click` listener. All 9 clean.
2. **Every static `<button>`/`<input type="button|submit">` with a literal `id`** (63 found) cross-checked
   against every `getElementById('id').addEventListener`, `onclick=`, and `querySelector('#id')` in the
   file. Two false positives (`gtrSubmitBtn`, `studentNoticeAcceptBtn`) — both wired correctly via a
   variable-assignment pattern (`var btn = document.getElementById(...); btn.addEventListener(...)`) or
   event delegation (`data-gtr-submit`), just not caught by the direct-chain regex. Manually confirmed
   both work as designed; zero real gaps beyond the already-known Reference Letter one.
3. **Every event-delegation hook** (`e.target.closest('[data-X]')`, 14 distinct attribute names across
   Grade/Time Change, Attendance, Assign Classroom, and Reference Letter) cross-checked against every
   `data-X=` attribute actually rendered in a template string, and the reverse (every `data-X=` attribute
   rendered anywhere checked against a matching `closest()`/`getAttribute()` consumer). Two more false
   positives (`data-gtr-comments`, `data-rl-comments` — read via a value-specific `querySelector`, not a
   bare delegation hook, so the regex missed them). Zero real orphaned hooks or unconsumed attributes.
4. **Every client → server RPC call target** (`apsScriptRun...).functionName(...)`) cross-checked against
   every `function` defined in `Code.gs` — roughly 60 call sites, all resolve to a real server function.
   Zero broken RPC targets (consistent with the full cross-reference already done in the fifty-third
   round, still holding after this round's edits).
5. **Duplicate static `id="..."` attributes** anywhere in the file — zero found.
6. Spot-checked the server side of the Reference Letter feature itself
   (`getReferenceLetterAccessInfo`/`getMyReferenceLetterRequests`/`submitReferenceLetterRequest` in
   `Code.gs`) — all present, and the Teacher-role gate (`viewer.role !== 'teacher' && !isClassroomTeacher`)
   is intact and unrelated to the client-side bug above.

**Result: the Reference Letter tab click-listener gap was the only real defect found.** It was already
fixed in the delivered `Dashboard.html`; no further code change was made this round.

#### What the user needs to do
Confirm the *live* Apps Script project's `Dashboard.html` actually contains the fix — open the file in the
Apps Script editor and search (Ctrl+F) for `rl-tab').addEventListener`. If it's not found, paste in the
current `Dashboard.html` (already delivered, and saved to the local sync folder / Claude Project) and
redeploy (Manage deployments > Edit > New version), then retry as a Teacher account.

#### Self-review flags
- **Could not positively verify the live deployment's actual state** — the iframe-sandboxing limitation
  that blocked deeper OAuth diagnosis in the fifty-third round applies here too, for the same underlying
  reason. Gave the user a precise, low-effort way to check it themselves (a text search in the editor)
  rather than guessing or claiming false certainty either way.
- **The static-analysis scripts used here are heuristic, not exhaustive** — they catch the specific "id
  defined, listener missing" and "delegation hook orphaned" bug shapes, which is exactly the shape of the
  one confirmed bug in this codebase, but a differently-shaped bug (e.g. a listener attached to the wrong
  element, or correct wiring with incorrect logic inside the handler) would not be caught by this kind of
  scan. Flagging the audit's actual scope rather than implying "scanned everything, guaranteed bug-free."

### Sept 2026, fifty-eighth round — Reference Letter tab not visible for teachers: race condition between two independent per-login RPCs (root cause found and fixed)

#### Trigger
User reported, after the fifty-sixth round's click-listener fix: "In the teacher view - Reference letter
tab is not visible. All the teacher can view and raise the reference letter." — a step beyond the earlier
"not clickable" report (the tab wasn't even showing at all), plus an explicit requirement that every
teacher account be able to see and use it, not just some.

#### Root cause (confirmed this round, not just suspected)
`updateReferenceLetterTabVisibility()` (`Dashboard.html`) decides whether to show `rl-tab`/`rl-approvals-tab`
from `currentUser.role` / `currentUser.isClassroomTeacher`. `currentUser` is only ever populated by the
`getDashboardData()` RPC (in `load()`'s and `quietRefreshDashboard()`'s success handlers) — a relatively
heavy call that reads and decorates the full classroom roster, availability, on-call picks, etc.

But `updateReferenceLetterTabVisibility()` itself was, before this round, only ever *called* from
`loadReferenceLetterAccessInfo()`'s success handler — the handler for a second, completely independent RPC
(`getReferenceLetterAccessInfo()`) that `Code.gs` explicitly documents as "the same cheap, no-Sheet-access,
once-per-login call" (checks three email lists in memory, nothing else).

Both RPCs are fired together, with no sequencing, from `apsFinishPermissionConfirm_()` right after login:
```js
load();                          // -> getDashboardData()      (heavy)
...
loadReferenceLetterAccessInfo(); // -> getReferenceLetterAccessInfo() (trivially cheap)
```
Because `getReferenceLetterAccessInfo()` is so much cheaper, it essentially always resolves first. Its
success handler then calls `updateReferenceLetterTabVisibility()` while `currentUser` is *still null*
(`load()`'s response hasn't landed yet), so `isTeacher` evaluates to `false` and the tab is hidden. Once
`load()`'s response *does* land a moment later and correctly sets `currentUser.role`/`currentUser.isClassroomTeacher`,
nothing calls `updateReferenceLetterTabVisibility()` again to re-evaluate it — unlike every sibling
tab-visibility function (`updateChatVisibility()`, `updateClassChangeTabVisibility()`,
`updateAttendanceTabVisibility()`, `updateForceSyncVisibility()`, `updateHiddenStaffToggleVisibility()`),
which are all called from inside `load()`'s own success handler, after `currentUser` is set. The Reference
Letter one was the only tab-visibility function missing from that list — a straightforward oversight, not a
role/permissions bug. It also explains why the report was universal ("All the teacher") rather than
affecting one account: the race is won the same way on every login, for every teacher, every time.

Confirmed server-side that this really is timing, not incorrect data: `getDashboardData()`
(`Code.gs`, ~line 3607-3624) computes `ctx.role` via `getViewerContext_()` and
`ctx.isClassroomTeacher = courses.some(c => courseHasTeacherEmail_(c, ctx.email))` and returns `ctx`
directly as the RPC result — so by the time `load()`'s handler runs, `currentUser.role` and
`currentUser.isClassroomTeacher` are both correct for every real classroom teacher, dual-hat or not (the
fifty-fourth round's widened `isClassroomTeacher` check already covers a Headmaster/Admin who also
co-teaches a course). The data was always right; it just never triggered a re-check of the tab's visibility.

#### What was fixed
Added a call to `updateReferenceLetterTabVisibility()` in both places `currentUser` gets (re)populated,
matching the existing pattern used by every other tab-visibility function:
- `load()`'s success handler (`getDashboardData()`, the initial per-login load) — right after
  `updateAttendanceTabVisibility()`.
- `quietRefreshDashboard()`'s success handler (the same RPC, called again on the recurring background
  refresh) — same placement, so the tab also recovers correctly if a teacher's Classroom co-teaching status
  changes mid-session.

This closes the race regardless of which of the two RPCs happens to answer first: whichever one lands
second now re-evaluates visibility with complete, correct data. `loadReferenceLetterAccessInfo()`'s own
call to `updateReferenceLetterTabVisibility()` was left in place — it's still needed so `referenceLetterAccessInfo`-driven state (`isApprover`/`isFinalApprover`/`isReadOnlyViewer`, which gates the separate Approvals tab) gets applied as soon as that data arrives too.

No change was needed to any role-resolution logic, the `Dashboard_User_Roles` sheet, or the server-side
Reference Letter eligibility checks — all of those were already correct; only the client-side visibility
re-check was missing.

#### Validation performed
`node --check` on `Code.gs` (unchanged this round, re-verified clean regardless), HTML tag-balance check
and extracted-`<script>` `node --check` on `Dashboard.html` after the edit — both clean. Live verification
inside the actual Apps Script sandboxed iframe was not possible from this session (the same tooling
limitation documented in the fifty-third/fifty-sixth rounds), so this is a static-analysis-confirmed fix,
not one confirmed against the live deployed page.

#### What the user needs to do
Redeploy the delivered `Dashboard.html` (Manage deployments > Edit > New version) and confirm as a Teacher
account that the Reference Letter tab now appears immediately after signing in, without needing to click
around first.

#### Self-review flags
- **Root cause is now a specific, named race condition with a code-level explanation, not a heuristic
  guess** — the "stale `Dashboard_User_Roles` sheet entry" theory considered while first investigating this
  report was checked and ruled out: `getDashboardData()`'s returned `ctx.role`/`ctx.isClassroomTeacher` are
  correct at the point they're computed, so a stale sheet entry was not the explanation.
- **Could not verify against the live deployment** for the same iframe-sandboxing reason noted in every
  prior round that needed live confirmation — flagged rather than glossed over.

### Sept 2026, fifty-ninth round — Login broken for everyone with "We couldn't verify your Google sign-in" / UrlFetchApp permission error; misdiagnosed-by-design error copy corrected

#### Trigger
User posted two screenshots of the branded login-error screen: title "We couldn't verify your Google
sign-in," body "Your Google sign-in could not be verified. Please try signing in again. Details: You do
not have permission to call UrlFetchApp.fetch. Required permissions:
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/script.external_request," with the "Required Web App setting: OAuth
Client ID" hint shown underneath.

#### Root cause
Not an OAuth Client ID / redirect URI problem (the hint the screen was showing) — a completely different
issue: the Apps Script *platform itself* blocked `UrlFetchApp.fetch()` inside `exchangeCodeForTokens_()`/
`verifyGoogleIdToken_()` (the fifty-third round's redirect-flow token exchange and ID-token verification)
because the account that deployed this Web App (`"executeAs": "USER_DEPLOYING"` in `appsscript.json`) has
not (re-)granted the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/script.external_request` scope. That scope *is*
already correctly declared in `appsscript.json` (confirmed by reading the file directly) — but declaring a
scope in the manifest does not retroactively grant it. Google requires the authorizing user to go through
the consent prompt again (by running any function once in the Apps Script editor) before a newly-declared
scope actually takes effect for that project's execution identity. This blocks sign-in for **every**
visitor, not just one account, because every fresh sign-in goes through this same server-side token
exchange.

Traced exactly why the screen showed the wrong ("OAuth Client ID") explanation for this: `doGet()`'s catch
block around the token-exchange/verification call unconditionally set `bootError.code = 'invalid_token'`
for *any* exception raised inside that try block — a genuinely expired/reused auth code, a forged token,
*and* this raw platform authorization exception were all being lumped into the same bucket, which the
client's `apsShowAuthError('invalid_token', ...)` renders with copy and a hint written for a real
ID-token/OAuth-Client-ID problem. The `Details:` line correctly showed the raw platform message (so the
actual cause was recoverable by reading it closely), but the screen's own diagnosis and fix instructions
pointed at the wrong setting entirely.

#### What was fixed
- `Code.gs`, `doGet()`'s catch block: now inspects the caught exception's message and classifies it
  separately — `bootError.code = 'scope_authorization'` when the message matches Apps Script's own
  standard wording for this failure ("do not have permission to call" / "Required permissions:"), versus
  the existing `'invalid_token'` for everything else.
- `Dashboard.html`: `apsClassifyServerError_()` gets the same check (defensive — in case this same raw
  exception ever surfaces through a different RPC path later, not just the fresh-login redirect). The
  hardcoded ternary that used to collapse every boot-error code down to just `'invalid_token'` or
  `'authorization_failure'` now also passes `'scope_authorization'` through unchanged.
- `apsShowAuthError()` gets a new `'scope_authorization'` branch with accurate title/copy: explains that
  only the account that owns/deployed the project can fix it, and gives the exact steps (open the Apps
  Script editor, pick any function in the Run toolbar, click Run once, Allow every listed permission,
  no redeploy needed). The "Required Web App setting" hint line (previously a static `OAuth Client ID`
  in the HTML, now a JS-settable `<b id="apsDeploymentHintValue">`) is repointed to "Re-authorize the
  script (Apps Script editor → Run → Allow)" for this case instead of showing the misleading OAuth Client
  ID hint; the `invalid_token`/`authorization_failure` branches now explicitly reset that same element back
  to "OAuth Client ID" so they're unaffected by the shared DOM node.

#### What the user needs to do right now (this is the actual, immediate fix — no redeploy strictly required)
As the account that owns/deployed this Apps Script project: open the project (Extensions → Apps Script
from the linked Google Sheet, or script.google.com), pick **any** function from the Run toolbar dropdown,
click ▶ **Run** once. Google will show its standard authorization prompt listing every scope in
`appsscript.json` (including external requests) — sign in as that owner account, click through "Advanced →
Go to [project] (unsafe)" if it's an unverified app, and **Allow**. That alone should unblock sign-in for
every teacher/student/admin immediately, since it's an authorization-grant fix, not a code/deployment one.
Redeploying the updated `Dashboard.html`/`Code.gs` from this round is still worth doing so the error screen
itself gives the correct instructions if this ever happens again (e.g. after a future scope is added).

#### Validation performed
`node --check` on the full `Code.gs`, HTML tag-balance check and extracted-`<script>` `node --check` on
`Dashboard.html` — all clean. Could not trigger this exact runtime condition live (it depends on the real
owner account's Google-side authorization grant, which this session has no access to) — the fix was
verified by tracing the exact code path from the screenshot's error text back to `doGet()`'s catch block
and confirming the new classification/copy matches.

#### Self-review flags
- **This round's code change does not, by itself, fix the login failure** — it only makes the error
  screen's *diagnosis* accurate for this cause (and any future one that trips the same platform-level
  exception). The actual fix is the one-time re-authorization step above, which only the owner account can
  perform; no code or configuration change can substitute for it.
- Confirmed `appsscript.json`'s `oauthScopes` already lists `script.external_request` correctly — this is
  purely an authorization-grant staleness issue, not a manifest bug, so no manifest change was made.

#### Addendum — still failing for "a few users" after this round's error-copy fix; added a concrete function to run, and why it's "a few" and not everyone
User confirmed the corrected error screen is now live (title now correctly reads "APS Dashboard needs to
be re-authorized by its owner," proving the redeploy of this round's code landed) but reported it's still
happening for a few users, and asked for a specific function to run locally rather than "any function."

**Added `apsOwnerReauthorizeAllScopes()`** (`Code.gs`, placed directly above `doGet()`) — a single,
read-only, side-effect-free function the owner selects from the Apps Script editor's Run dropdown and
clicks Run once. It probes every scope this dashboard's code actually calls (UrlFetchApp/external
requests, userinfo, Sheets, Docs, Drive, Classroom, Admin Directory, Admin Reports, and a mail-quota check
that does NOT send anything), independently try/caught so one failure doesn't stop the rest, and logs a
clear PASS/FAIL/SKIP line per scope (`Logger.log`, also returned so it's visible in View > Executions). A
config-dependent probe (e.g. Docs, if `REFERENCE_LETTER_TEMPLATE_DOC_ID` isn't set) is marked SKIP rather
than FAIL, so it's not mistaken for an authorization problem. AdSense (declared as an enabled advanced
service in `appsscript.json` but never actually called anywhere in `Code.gs` — confirmed via a full-file
grep) was deliberately left out of the probe list; it has no matching entry in `oauthScopes` either, since
nothing uses it.

**Why "a few users" and not everyone, even though this Web App runs "Execute as: Me":** re-examined
`apsBootstrapSession()` (`Dashboard.html`) — a returning visitor with a still-valid remembered session
(localStorage, up to 30 days) skips the OAuth-redirect flow entirely and goes straight to
`getAuthenticatedAPSUser()`, which never touches `UrlFetchApp`. Only a *fresh* Google sign-in exercises
`exchangeCodeForTokens_()`/`verifyGoogleIdToken_()` — the only two functions that call `UrlFetchApp` during
sign-in — so only people without a valid remembered session (new device/browser, cleared storage, a
first-ever login, or a session whose 30-day/6-hour timeout has actually lapsed) currently hit the broken
path. Since the scope gap is owner-side, not per-account, this isn't a handful of specific accounts with a
real permissions problem — it's every fresh sign-in, and the affected group will keep growing as more
people's remembered sessions expire, until `apsOwnerReauthorizeAllScopes()` is actually run and every
permission is Allowed.

**What the user needs to do:** open the project as the owner, select `apsOwnerReauthorizeAllScopes` in the
Run dropdown, click Run, Allow every permission Google lists, then check View > Logs for an all-PASS
readout (SKIP lines are fine; any FAIL line names exactly what's still missing). No redeploy needed for the
fix itself — this round's `Code.gs` only needs to be deployed once so the function exists to run.

#### Validation performed
`node --check` on the full `Code.gs` (function added, no other logic touched) — clean. The probe function's
individual API calls were not executed against live data in this session (no access to the production
Google account) — each call was checked against its documented Apps Script signature and cross-referenced
against the exact same call pattern already used elsewhere in this file for the same service, not invented
fresh.

#### Self-review flags
- **Could not verify this function actually resolves the error** for the same reason as every prior round
  needing live confirmation — this session has no access to the owning Google account to run it. The
  PASS/FAIL readout it produces is designed so the user can self-diagnose precisely rather than reporting
  back "it still doesn't work" with no further detail.
- The Admin Directory / Admin Reports probes can legitimately FAIL for a reason unrelated to script scope
  authorization (the owner account not being a Workspace domain admin) — flagged in the function's own
  comment so a FAIL there specifically isn't mistaken for the same external_request problem the user
  originally reported.

## Sept 26, 2026 — Attendance module redesign: weekly Student & Teacher attendance from Google Meet login/logout, overrides, audit log

**Scope.** Only the Attendance module was changed: the `STUDENT & TEACHER ATTENDANCE CAPTURE` block at the
end of `Code.gs`, and the Attendance tab's CSS/markup/script in `Dashboard.html`. Every line outside those
blocks is byte-identical to `CURRENT_PROD_CODE` (verified with `diff`: all `Code.gs` hunks start after the
module header; all `Dashboard.html` hunks are inside the Attendance CSS, `#attendanceView`, the `att*`
functions, and the `att*` event listeners). `appsscript.json` is unchanged — no new scope or service.

### Why the Attendance tab was not capturing weekly attendance (root causes, reproduced against production code)
Running the production `Code.gs` in a mocked Apps Script harness reproduced all four problems:

1. **Wrong data source → everyone ABSENT.** Capture used the Google Meet REST API, which only returns
   conference data for Meet spaces the *calling* account organized or can access. Teachers' own Meets are not
   visible to the owner account, and unmapped courses were written as 0 minutes/ABSENT. A student who attended
   the full class was recorded ABSENT.
2. **Date-cell corruption.** Rows were written without text formatting, so Sheets auto-converted
   `2026-09-25`, `7:30 PM` and `MM/dd/yyyy h:mm a` into Date cells. Read back as `Date` objects, this
   (a) broke the idempotency key, so every sync **duplicated** the roster rows; (b) made
   `getAttendanceRecordsForViewer` throw `(b.date || "").localeCompare is not a function`, so the tab showed
   nothing; (c) made every edit fail with "Could not find that attendance record"; and (d) Dates are illegal
   `google.script.run` return values anyway.
3. **No weekly catch-up.** A class was only captured if a sync ran on class day within 6 h of the start. One
   missed or failed trigger run lost that week permanently.
4. **Overrides were overwritten.** An edit wrote the Status cell, and the next 15-minute sync rewrote the
   whole row with the captured status.

### What changed (Code.gs)
- **Capture source: Google Meet audit log (Admin Reports API, `meet` / `call_ended`).** This uses the same
  `AdminReports` service and owner identity the dashboard already uses every sync for Live/Started detection.
  Each event is one participant session: logout = event time, login = `start_timestamp_seconds` (fallback:
  logout − `duration_seconds`), plus `meeting_code` and `organizer_email`. **One query per class date** (not
  per course), with a `fields` projection, filtered to roster emails.
- **Class attribution** (`attAttributeSessionsToClass_`), so another Meet the same evening is never counted:
  1) Admin-mapped Meet code, if it had activity → 2) codes the course teacher(s) used or organized in the
  window (HM/support staff excluded) → 3) the code most of the class used (teacher absent). The result is
  stored per row in **Capture Source**. Mapping a Meet link is now optional.
- **Last 2 weeks captured on every run.** `attendancePendingOccurrences_` returns each course's class
  occurrences in the last **14 days** (Script Property `ATTENDANCE_BACKFILL_DAYS`, 1–35, overrides this) that
  have started and are not yet finalized. An occurrence is re-captured until 6 h after its scheduled end
  (`ATTENDANCE_FINALIZE_AFTER_END_HOURS`), then marked final in `attendanceFinalizedThrough_v1`
  (`{courseId: 'yyyy-MM-dd'}`, about 30 bytes per course; finalization never jumps past an older pending
  occurrence).
- **No false ABSENTs on API failure.** If the audit query fails, that date's occurrences are *not written*
  and stay pending. Courses with a mapped Meet code fall back to the original Meet REST API path. The run is
  flagged `degraded` in the sync summary and logged once per run.
- **Overrides preserved.** Seven columns were **appended** (columns 1–21 unchanged): `Auto Status`,
  `Override Status`, `Override By`, `Override At`, `Override Reason`, `Capture Source`, `Week Of`.
  `Attendance Status` stays the *effective* status. The upsert refreshes captured fields but keeps any
  override. `editAttendanceRecordStatus(courseId, date, email, role, newStatus, reason)` keeps its signature,
  and now accepts `PRESENT|PARTIAL|ABSENT|EXCUSED`, plus `AUTO` to clear an override and restore the captured
  status.
- **Audit log.** Two columns were appended to `Attendance_Audit_Log`: `Action` (`OVERRIDE` / `CLEAR_OVERRIDE`)
  and `Auto Status`. Rows are written text-formatted, so the date column stays a string.
- **Permissions (unchanged model, server-enforced).** Admin/HM/Super Admin can override any row. A Teacher can
  override only STUDENT rows in courses they teach (never their own row). Students and BOD are view-only.
  Students see only their own rows; the override author and reason are stripped for them. Edit buttons are
  also hidden when the role's dashboard permission is read-only.
- **Legacy data self-heals.** Reads convert Date cells and Sheets serial numbers back to strings. The first
  sync of a course collapses the old duplicate rows, rewrites the sheet text-formatted, and adds the new
  columns (`ensureSheetHeader_` adds physical columns first — a new sheet has only 26).
- **Concurrency.** Sync upsert and override share `LockService.getScriptLock()`, so an override saved during a
  sync cannot be lost.
- **New endpoint.** `getAttendanceWeekOptions()` returns the current Friday-anchored week plus the 15
  previous weeks, and a default of the most recent week that has started. It does no Sheet reads.

### Performance
| Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Attendance tab read (N courses) | ~2N Sheets calls + one `openById` per course | `openById` once (memoized) + `getSheets` + **one** `Sheets.Values.batchGet` (automatic SpreadsheetApp fallback) |
| Sync capture | Meet REST calls per course × per participant | **one** Admin Reports query per class date |
| Sync writes | clear + full rewrite of every in-scope sheet, every 15 min | write skipped when the captured data did not change; no up-front clear |
| AWK map | re-read for every course | read once per run |
| Unused `readAllCoursesFromCache_()` in 7 attendance endpoints | full cache-sheet read + JSON parse per call | removed (the value was never used) |
| Sync runtime | unbounded | 4.5-min budget; leftovers roll to the next run |
| Client | — | week picker fetched once per session; stale responses discarded (request sequence) |

### Dashboard.html (Attendance tab only)
Week picker (default = latest started week), status summary chips, an **Override** button (replaces Edit)
opening a modal that shows the captured status and minutes, an EXCUSED option, and "Use captured status —
clear override". An **ADJUSTED** tag (tooltip shows the captured status, who, when and why; students get the
tag only). A capture-source line per row, a richer sync status (sessions captured/finalized/open, degraded
warning), and an Action column in the audit log. Every existing element id and function name is kept.

### Setup / deploy
1. Deploy `Code.gs` + `Dashboard.html` (new version of the existing deployment). No manifest change.
2. Confirm the **Admin SDK API** and **Google Sheets API** are enabled in the linked Cloud project. Both are
   already declared advanced services.
3. If not already done, run `createAttendanceSyncTrigger()` once as the owner. The owner must be a Workspace
   admin with Reports access — the same requirement as the existing Live/Meet detection.
4. Click **Sync Attendance Now** once: the last 2 weeks are backfilled. For a deeper one-time backfill, set
   Script Property `ATTENDANCE_BACKFILL_DAYS` (≤35), run a sync, then remove it.

### Validation performed
- `node --check` on `Code.gs` and on the extracted `Dashboard.html` script; HTML tag balance; every
  `getElementById('att…')` resolves.
- **Server E2E (25 tests, mocked Apps Script services including Sheets auto-conversion):** statuses from audit
  sessions (present/partial/absent, other-meeting session excluded), all three attribution paths, 2-week
  backfill, week filter, finalization and next-day behaviour, role scoping for all roles, permission denials,
  override surviving re-sync, clear override, no-op, audit log, idempotent re-sync (0 writes), degraded mode
  (nothing written), legacy Date/duplicate sheet upgrade, batchGet fallback parity.
- **UI E2E (headless Chromium, real Dashboard.html, `google.script.run` wired to the server harness):**
  Admin/Teacher/Student/BOD/HM layouts, a teacher override through the modal, week switching, the "My
  Attendance" scope, an HM clearing the override, Sync Now, and audit-log rendering. No page errors.
- Same harness against **production** code reproduced root causes 1, 2 and 4 above.
- **Not verified live:** real Admin Reports payloads (parameter names follow the documented Meet audit schema)
  and real Sheets/batchGet behaviour — confirm on the first real sync.

### Sept 26, 2026 (follow-up) — Week-wise AWK sheets: one sheet per school week, all classrooms

**Request.** Capture every student's and teacher's attendance week-wise across all Google Classrooms:
**AWK01ATT = Week 1, AWK02ATT = Week 2, …**, each holding every classroom's rows for that week. This
**supersedes** the "one sheet per course" storage described in the section above. Capture, the Meet audit
source, overrides and the audit log are unchanged.

**Week numbering.** Weeks are the school's Friday–Sunday blocks, using the same anchor as
`getCurrentWeekId_()`. A Mon–Thu class belongs to the upcoming weekend's week, as in "This Week".
**Week 1 = Fri Sep 11, 2026** (AY26-27), taken from Script Property `ATTENDANCE_WEEK1_START` (`yyyy-MM-dd`,
snapped to that week's Friday; default `2026-09-11`). Set it at the start of each academic year.

**Storage.**
- `AWKnnATT` = week *nn* (`formatAwkSheetName_(n)`), created on first write.
- Header is 29 columns: the previous 28 plus an appended `Week No`.
- Rows are sorted by class → date → teachers first → students A–Z.
- Key is Course ID + Date + Email + Role, so several classrooms safely share a sheet.

**Capture.** Every run captures all unfinalized class occurrences **from Week 1 onward**, oldest first. It
fetches at most `ATTENDANCE_MAX_DATES_PER_RUN` (8) class dates per run; later dates are queued for the next
run, shown in the sync status as "queued". Records are grouped by week and written with **one upsert per
week sheet** (previously one per classroom). A classroom is finalized only when every week sheet it touched
was written. `ATTENDANCE_BACKFILL_DAYS` is removed; Week 1 replaces it.

**One-time migration** (`migrateAttendanceToWeekSheets_`, guarded by Script Property
`attendanceSheetLayout_v1 = 'weekly'`, runs under the script lock):
1. Each legacy per-classroom sheet listed in `Course_AWK_Map` is renamed to **`OLD_AWKnnATT`**. It is kept
   untouched as a backup and never deleted.
2. Its rows (dates normalized, duplicates collapsed, overrides kept) are copied into the matching week sheet.
   Rows dated before Week 1 remain only in the backup.
3. The regular capture then refreshes everything from Meet.

`Course_AWK_Map` is left in place as history and is only read by the migration.

**Reads and edits.**
- The Attendance tab reads one week sheet for a week or date filter, otherwise all week sheets, in one
  `batchGet`. Role scoping is unchanged.
- `editAttendanceRecordStatus` finds the week sheet from the record's date.
- `getAttendanceWeekOptions` lists Week 1…current, labelled "Week N — Sep 11 - Sep 13, 2026 (AWK01ATT)".
- `getAttendanceCourseAwkMap` (name kept for the client) now returns the Week ↔ AWK sheet list with row counts.

**Removed** (made obsolete by the redesign): `assignAwkSheetNameForCourse_`, `getOrCreateCourseAwkMapSheet_`,
`getOrCreateAttendanceCourseSheet_` (now `getOrCreateAttendanceWeekSheet_`), `upsertAttendanceRecordsForCourse_`
(now `upsertAttendanceRecordsForWeekSheet_`), `getAttendanceBackfillDays_`, and `ATTENDANCE_AWK_COUNTER_PROP_KEY`.

**UI.** The admin "Course ↔ AWK Sheet" panel is now **"Week ↔ AWK Sheet"** (Week, Sheet, Rows). Each record
shows its week number under the date. The week picker covers Week 1 to the current week. The sync status
lists the week sheets updated and any queued dates.

**Validation.**
- **Server tests (31, mocked Apps Script):** Week 1–3 sheets each containing both classrooms; `Week No`
  column; sort order; week, date and pre-Week-1 filters (the latter does no read); week options; admin panel;
  every role's scope and denial; overrides across week sheets surviving re-sync; clear; audit log; idempotent
  re-sync; next-day finalization; Meet audit outage; 16 dates split 8 + 8 across two runs; migration
  (OLD_ backups, legacy row landing in Week 2, runs once); batchGet fallback parity; mapped Meet code;
  configurable Week 1.
- **Browser test:** Admin/Teacher/Student/BOD/HM layouts, Week ↔ AWK panel, override/clear, Sync Now.

**Deploy note.** On LIVE, the first sync after deploying renames the existing per-classroom AWK sheets to
`OLD_…` and builds Week 1…current. Make a copy of the Attendance spreadsheet first, or test on a copy.

### Sept 26, 2026 (follow-up 2) — Exclusions, call-window scoring, overall %, full-refresh Sync Now, Monday schedule, weekly report email

**Exclusions.** `attIsExcludedEmail_` excludes:
- every address in `ADMIN_EMAILS` and `HEADMASTER_EMAILS`;
- any email starting with a `HIDDEN_TEACHER_EMAIL_PREFIXES` entry (same prefix rule as `isHiddenTeacherName_`).

Excluded accounts are:
- never captured;
- never used to detect a class's Meet or its call window;
- filtered from every read;
- purged from existing week sheets on the next write;
- left out of `Attendance_Summary` and the report emails.

**Scoring (APS policy; replaces the old 80%-of-scheduled PRESENT threshold).**
- **Class call window:** per classroom per class date, from the earliest *First Join* to the latest *Last
  Leave* among its (non-excluded) students and teachers (`attClassCallWindow_`). It is bounded to 30 min
  before the scheduled start through 60 min after the scheduled end, so a Meet left open can't stretch it.
- **Attended %** = the person's merged minutes inside the window ÷ window minutes.
- **Captured score tiers:** above 75% = 100, 60–75 = 90, 50–59 = 80, 40–49 = 70, 30–39 = 60, 20–29 = 50,
  0–19 = 0.
- **Captured status:** 100 = PRESENT, 0 = ABSENT, anything else = PARTIAL.
- **Override scores:** PRESENT 100, PARTIAL 70, EXCUSED 70, ABSENT 0.
- **No call recorded:** call minutes are 0, so the score is 0.
- **New week-sheet columns (appended, now 35):** `Call Start`, `Call End`, `Call Minutes`, `Attended %`,
  `Auto Score`, `Score` (effective).
- **Removed** (the threshold no longer applies): `setAttendancePresentThresholdPct`,
  `getAttendancePresentThresholdPct_`, `attComputeStatus_`. `getAttendanceConfig()` now returns the tiers
  and override scores.
- **Re-capture:** the finalized-weeks property moved to `attendanceFinalizedThrough_v2`, so every week is
  re-captured once with the new scoring.

**Overall % (per student per classroom, all weeks).**
- Formula: Σ(week score × week call minutes) ÷ Σ(week call minutes). A week with no call counts only if it
  was overridden, weighted by its scheduled minutes.
- Stored in a new **`Attendance_Summary`** sheet, which the sync rebuilds whenever rows changed.
- Each override adjusts it in O(1) (`attApplyOverrideToSummary_`), so the tab and emails never re-read
  every week.

**Sync Attendance Now = full refresh.**
- `forceSyncAttendanceNow` runs `syncAttendanceForAllCourses({ full: true })`: every week from Week 1 is
  re-captured, ignoring "finalized".
- Existing rows are updated in place (key Course+Date+Email+Role). There are never duplicate entries, and
  overrides are kept.
- Up to 24 class dates per click. If more remain, a cursor (`attendanceFullRefreshCursor_v1`, valid 2 h)
  lets the next click continue, and the status says so.

**Schedule.** Run `createAttendanceSyncTrigger()` once as the owner. It removes the old every-15-minutes
trigger and installs:
- `syncAttendanceForAllCourses` — **weekly, Monday ~5:00 AM ET**;
- `sendWeeklyAttendanceReports` — **daily ~7:00 AM ET**. It sends on **Monday** only; on Tue/Wed it only
  resumes a Monday batch paused by the email quota; otherwise it exits immediately.

Apps Script fires an `atHour()` trigger at some minute within that hour.

**Weekly report email** (`sendWeeklyAttendanceReports` → `attSendAttendanceReportsForWeek_`).
- **Coverage:** the week that just ended (the week containing today − 3 days).
- **Freshness:** if no sync ran yet that day, it syncs first.
- **One email per Google Classroom:**
  - To: its teachers and students.
  - CC: `ATTENDANCE_REPORT_CC` (JSON Script Property; default `admin@avvaiyarpadasalai.org`,
    `info3@avvaiyarpadasalai.org`).
  - Template: the standard APS template (`apsEmailShell_` / `sendApsHtmlEmail_`).
- **Content:**
  - class name, week, and **Class Teacher name(s) with email**;
  - the class's Google Meet call window per date;
  - a per-student table: joined–left, minutes/call minutes, attended %, week score, status (with an
    "adjusted by teacher" note), and overall %;
  - the scoring legend;
  - **"Need a change or correction? Please contact your Class Teacher: Name (email)."**
- **Idempotent and quota-aware:** progress is kept per week in `attendanceReportState_v1` and saved after
  every classroom, so a classroom is never emailed twice. If `MailApp.getRemainingDailyQuota()` is too low,
  the batch pauses and resumes the next day.
- **Audience option:** Script Property `ATTENDANCE_REPORT_AUDIENCE` = `CLASS` (default, as requested: the
  whole class sees the table) or `PRIVATE` (teachers + CC get the table; each student gets only their own row).
- **Testing helper:** `sendAttendanceReportPreviewToMe(courseId?)` — run from the editor; it emails one
  classroom's report only to you (no students, no CC, nothing marked sent).

**UI.**
- The records table now shows Joined–Left, Minutes (attended / call), Attended %, Week Score and Overall.
- The summary chips add the average week score.
- The Override window shows the captured minutes/% and the override score mapping.
- The sync status shows full-refresh progress.
- The admin text states the Monday 5 AM sync / 7 AM report schedule and the exclusions.

**Validation.**
- **Server tests (35):**
  - excluded accounts are never captured, shown, or used for the call window;
  - call window and tier boundaries;
  - overall % weighting;
  - each override score (including a no-call week);
  - clearing an override;
  - full refresh updating finalized weeks with no duplicates and stale excluded rows purged;
  - the 24-date cursor across two clicks;
  - trigger installation;
  - report recipients/CC/content, no same-day resend, Tuesday no-op, quota pause and resume, PRIVATE
    mode, preview-to-me;
  - degraded mode, migration, batchGet fallback, teacher scope.
- **Browser test:** all five roles.
- **Sample email:** rendered and visually checked.

**Watch-outs.**
- **MailApp quota:** the default Workspace limit is 1,500 recipients/day. One email per classroom counts
  (students + teachers + 2 CC) recipients. The resume logic covers overflow, but check the diagnostics after
  the first Monday.
- **Privacy:** `CLASS` mode shows every student's attendance to the whole class (and their families' inboxes).
  Confirm this is intended, or set `ATTENDANCE_REPORT_AUDIENCE = PRIVATE`.

**Manifest fix (Sept 26, 2026).** Running `createAttendanceSyncTrigger()` failed with *"Specified permissions
are not sufficient to call ScriptApp.getProjectTriggers. Required permissions:
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/script.scriptapp"*.

- **Cause:** `appsscript.json` declares `oauthScopes` explicitly, and it lacked the trigger-management scope.
- **Fix:** added `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/script.scriptapp`. That is the only change to the manifest.
- **After updating the manifest in the Apps Script project:** run `createAttendanceSyncTrigger()` once as
  the owner and click **Allow** on the new consent screen.
- **Who re-consents:** with owner execution, only the owner re-consents. If the deployment really is
  `USER_ACCESSING` (as the checked-in manifest says), every user sees the consent prompt once.

### Sept 26, 2026 (follow-up 4) — Always exclude vsugadev@avvaiyarpadasalai.org

`vsugadev@avvaiyarpadasalai.org` is now **always** excluded from attendance, alongside ADMIN_EMAILS,
HEADMASTER_EMAILS and HIDDEN_TEACHER_EMAIL_PREFIXES. It is set in `ATTENDANCE_ALWAYS_EXCLUDED_EMAILS_` in
`Code.gs` and matched case-insensitively.

Exclusion means:
- never captured;
- never used to find a class's Meet or its call window;
- hidden from every read and from the report emails;
- existing rows purged on the next sync.

More addresses can be excluded without a code change through the Script Property
**`ATTENDANCE_EXCLUDED_EMAILS`** (JSON array, e.g. `["someone@avvaiyarpadasalai.org"]`). It only adds to the
list; it can never remove the built-in addresses.

Tested in the server suite (now 36): excluded in any letter case, with real Meet activity, and without
stretching the class call window; the property adds an extra address.

### Sept 27, 2026 — Search, auto-refresh, APSID, and the 90/95 class-duration rule

**Baseline.** `CURRENT_PROD_CODE` (read-only) does not yet contain the redesigned Attendance module, so these
enhancements are built on the project-root working files. They were diffed against `CURRENT_PROD_CODE`:
- Code.gs changes are confined to the Attendance module, plus the user's own Knowledge Base video entries.
- Dashboard.html changes are confined to the Attendance tab.

**1. APSID — one centralized function: `getAPSIdFromEmail(email)`.**
- `raja_aps1234@…` → `APS1234`; `kumar_APS5678@…` → `APS5678`; unrecognized → `APSXXX`.
- It reuses `extractAPSID_()`'s single regex (no second parser). `extractAPSID_` itself is unchanged and
  still returns `NA`, because the class cards, login screen and reference letters hide their badge on `NA`.
- It is the only APSID source in the Attendance module: stored APS ID column, every row read (legacy
  values are re-derived), audit log (`personApsId`, `editedByApsId`), the Teacher filter, search, and report
  emails.

**2. Class-duration rule (`getEffectiveClassMinutes`).**
- **Actual Class Minutes** = the class window from the teacher's first valid join to their last valid
  leave, taken from the class's attributed Meet sessions.
  - Rejoins inside that span are part of it, and it is not clipped, so the real Meet duration is kept.
  - With several (non-excluded) teachers, it runs from the earliest join of any of them to the latest leave.
  - If no teacher joined, it falls back to the whole class's call window (previous behaviour), recorded as
    `Class Window Basis = CLASS` instead of `TEACHER`.
- **Effective Class Minutes** = `actual < 90 ? actual : 95`. 95 is a calculation maximum, never the Meet duration.
- **Columns (week sheets now 38):** new `Actual Class Minutes`, `Effective Class Minutes` and
  `Class Window Basis`. `Call Minutes` = Effective (the denominator).
- Student minutes are counted only inside the teacher's window, with overlapping and rejoined sessions
  merged (existing `attMergeAndBoundSessions_`).
- **Attended %** = attended ÷ effective, 2 decimals, capped at 100 (`attAttendedPct_`).
- **Unchanged downstream:** week-score tiers, override scores, status rules, and the overall weighting.
  Overall now weights by effective minutes, since that is what `Call Minutes` holds.
- **Each class stands alone:** each class record gets its own effective minutes (e.g. 75 + 130 + 85 in one
  week → 75 + 95 + 85 = 255).
- **Teacher rows** keep their real attended minutes (e.g. 130).
- **Display:** the UI and emails show "Actual: 130 min · Calculation: 95 min (Max)" or "Actual: 75 min ·
  Calculation: 75 min" (`attClassMinutesLabel_` / `attClassMinutesHtml_`).
- **Re-capture:** the finalized-weeks property moved to `attendanceFinalizedThrough_v3`, so the next sync
  re-captures every week once under the new rule. Sync Attendance Now does the same immediately.

**3. Search.** Case-insensitive "contains" match on name, email and APSID, in:
- **Weekly Attendance** ("Search Student / Teacher / APSID");
- **Override Audit Log**, which matches both the person and the editor.

Search is client-side over the loaded rows (shared `attMatchesSearch_`), debounced 300 ms, with no server
call per keystroke. It combines with every filter.

**4. Auto-refresh (no Apply button).**
- **Week, Class, Date and Role** reload from the server automatically. The table stays visible, dimmed,
  with a "Refreshing…" indicator, and stale responses are discarded.
- **Two new filters — Teacher** (class teacher; Admin/HM/BOD only, like Role) **and Status** — plus
  **Search** filter the loaded rows instantly in the browser.
- **Audit log:** the course filter reloads automatically; its search filters in the browser.
- All selections and the search text are kept across refreshes.
- The summary chips (records, **Avg attended %**, avg week score, status counts) follow the filtered rows.
- The Refresh buttons remain for a manual reload.

**5. Other.**
- Rows carry `classTeachers` (from the course cache; no extra reads) for the Teacher filter.
- The APSID appears under each person's name in both tables and in report emails.
- `ATTENDANCE_MAX_DATES_PER_RUN` was raised 8 → 24. With the Monday-only schedule, the old cap could leave
  a backlog behind for weeks; the 50%-time-budget guard still bounds each run.

**Exclusions:** `SUPERADMIN_EMAILS` and `VCFO_AMCHATS_BOD_EMAILS` are now excluded too, as the
requirements expected. Before this round, only Admin/HM, the hidden prefixes and the always-excluded address were.

**Unchanged:** roles and permissions, exclusions (Admin/HM lists, hidden prefixes, the
always-excluded address), the Meet audit collection and class attribution, the idempotent upsert key
(Course + Date + Email + Role), override preservation, and the audit log (append-only; all fields kept).

**Validation.**
- **Acceptance suite (16, including the SuperAdmin/BOD exclusion):**
  - APSID examples;
  - 30/45/60/75/89/90/91/95/100/120/130/150 duration table;
  - 130→95 with 95/80/60 min → 100 / 84.21 / 63.16 %;
  - 75 + 60 → 80 %; 89 (teacher rejoin) + 80 → 89.89 %; 90 + 90 → 94.74 %;
  - three classes in a week → 255 effective;
  - overlapping student joins not double-counted; minutes before the teacher joined not counted;
  - overall weights by effective minutes;
  - scheduled + Sync Now ×2 is idempotent (same rows, same values);
  - override kept across Sync Now; audit log has APSIDs;
  - roles unchanged; email shows Actual/Calculation and APSID.
- **Browser test (17):** search by name / case / APSID / email / email local-part / APSXXX, with no
  server call per keystroke; chips follow the search; search combined with the Teacher and Status filters;
  Class, Week and Role auto-refresh with selections kept; audit-log search by APSID, email, name and editor;
  audit course filter auto-refresh.
- **Regression:** earlier server suite (36) and all-roles browser test pass.

### Sept 27, 2026 (follow-up) — 95-minute cap applied on every read, "(Max)" display, rejoins after the scheduled end, Teacher dropdown auto-refresh

**Reported.** NILAI 7 - CB | FRI 7:30 - 9:00 PM EST: teacher 7:25 PM – 10:00 PM (155 min) showed "147 / 155"
instead of being calculated against 95.

**Causes and fixes.**
1. **Rows captured before the 90/95 rule** had no Actual/Effective columns, and the tab trusted their stored
   `Call Minutes` (155). `attApplyClassDurationRule_()` now runs on **every** row read:
   - actual = stored actual, or the old `Call Minutes` for pre-rule rows;
   - effective = `getEffectiveClassMinutes(actual)`;
   - when the stored denominator differs, Attended %, captured score and status are recomputed against the
     effective minutes (an override is left untouched).

   So old rows show and score against 95 immediately. They are flagged `legacyDuration` and rewritten in the
   sheet by the next sync.
2. **Display:** attended minutes are credited up to the calculation maximum.
   - The teacher's 147 of a 155-min class shows **"95 / 95 (Max)"**, with "Actual: 155 min / Calculation:
     95 min (Max)" below; the real Meet minutes are in the tooltip and the `Active Minutes` column.
   - Every capped student row works the same way; emails too (`attCountedMinutes_`).
   - The attended % is unchanged: it was already capped at 100.
3. **Sessions after the scheduled end were being dropped.** A session was matched to a class only if it
   overlapped the scheduled 7:30–9:00 window, so a teacher or student who rejoined after 9:00 lost that time.
   Matching now uses the scheduled time widened by 30 min before and 60 min after (the same bounds as the
   call-window guard), so a class that runs to 10:00 PM, rejoins included, is counted in full.
4. **Weekly Attendance filters:** one delegated `change` handler per filter bar replaces per-element
   listeners, so **any** dropdown, including future ones, refreshes immediately.
   - Week / Class / Date / Role reload from the server; Teacher / Status (and any other) filter the loaded
     rows instantly.
   - The Teacher filter now falls back to the class's captured TEACHER rows when the server response has no
     `classTeachers` (e.g. a Dashboard.html deployed ahead of Code.gs), so it always has options and always
     filters.

**Validation.**
- Acceptance suite 20/20 (adds the NILAI 7 - CB case: Actual 155 / Calculation 95 (Max), teacher 95/95 =
  100 %, students 150 → 100 %, 80 → 84.21 %, 60 → 63.16 %; an old "147 / 155" row shown as 95/95 before
  re-sync; re-sync rewrites the old rows with no duplicates).
- Browser suite 21/21 (adds "95 / 95 (Max)" display; Teacher dropdown refreshing on every choice, including
  without `classTeachers`; every dropdown triggers refresh).
- Regression 36/36 and the all-roles browser test pass.

### Sept 27, 2026 — On-Call Teacher Attendance (TCS_ / TTS_) + Minutes display per the updated examples

**On-Call Teacher Attendance button** (Attendance tab → sync bar; Admin, SuperAdmin, HM and BOD only — the bar
is hidden for Teacher/Student and `getOnCallTeacherAttendance()` rejects them server-side).
- The button opens a **separate pop-up window**, opened synchronously in the click so pop-up blockers allow it.
  The dashboard writes a self-contained page into it and feeds it data through `attOnCallFetch_` (the pop-up
  calls back via `window.opener`). If the browser still blocks it, the same page opens in an in-page overlay.
- **In the pop-up:**
  - week selector (All weeks / Week N);
  - "Include rostered classes not joined";
  - search by teacher name, APSID or email (debounced);
  - Refresh, Print and Download CSV;
  - **Summary by teacher:** classes joined, weeks active, Meet minutes, credited minutes, average attended %,
    last class;
  - **Classes:** date/week, class, teacher + APSID, joined–left, Minutes (Actual / Calculation), attended %,
    week score, status (+ADJUSTED), Roster ("On roster" / "Joined (not on roster)").
- **On-call accounts:** emails starting `tcs_` / `tts_`, case-insensitive (`attIsOnCallEmail_`). More prefixes
  can be added via Script Property `ATTENDANCE_ON_CALL_PREFIXES` (JSON array).

**Capture changes (Code.gs).**
- **Guests:** an on-call teacher who joins a class's identified Meet **without being on its roster** is now
  captured as a TEACHER row with capture source `MEET_AUDIT_ON_CALL_GUEST` (`attOnCallGuestSessions_`). The
  Meet audit fetch keeps on-call accounts even when they are on no roster. Names come from the on-call
  directory or rosters, else from the email.
- **Correctness:** on-call accounts sit on many rosters, so they **no longer define a class's Meet code**. An
  on-call teacher on class X's roster who joins class Y's Meet no longer shapes class X's window or code.
- **Class window order:**
  1. the regular teacher(s)' first join → last leave;
  2. otherwise the on-call teacher's (`Class Window Basis = ON_CALL_TEACHER`);
  3. otherwise the whole class.
- **Exclusions:** a `tcs_`/`tts_` account that is also in `VCFO_AMCHATS_BOD_EMAILS` / `SUPERADMIN_EMAILS` is
  captured, because on-call wins over those two lists. ADMIN/HM/always-excluded/hidden-prefix still exclude.

**Minutes column (per the user's examples).**
- The first number is the **real attended Meet minutes**; the second is the calculation minutes. "(Max)" appears
  only on the Calculation line:
  - `75 / 75` · Actual: 75 min · Calculation: 75 min
  - `135 / 95` · Actual: 135 min · Calculation: 95 min (Max)
  - `0 / 0` · Actual: 0 min · Calculation: 0 min (no Meet)
- **Actual** = the teacher's Google Meet first join → last leave. **Calculation**: < 90 → actual; 90–95 → 95;
  > 95 → 95.
- The same display is used in the pop-up and the report email. `attCountedMinutes_` (attended capped at the
  calculation minutes) now only feeds the pop-up's "Credited minutes" total.

**Validation.**
- Acceptance 28/28 (adds the 90–95 band and 155 in the rule table, plus on-call cases):
  - rostered on-call in class X joining class Y gives 0 min in X;
  - with the regular teacher absent, on-call defines the window (Actual 105 / Calculation 95 (Max));
  - non-rostered TTS_ guest captured;
  - a BOD `tcs_` account captured while plain BOD is excluded;
  - report joined-only / include-not-joined / all weeks / per-teacher summary;
  - access for Admin/SuperAdmin/HM/BOD, denied for Teacher/Student;
  - re-sync ×2 creates no duplicates.
- Browser: Weekly Attendance 24/24 (adds the three Minutes examples and the 90–95 band) and On-Call UI 8/8
  (button visibility per role; pop-up content, search, checkbox, week auto-refresh, CSV download; blocked
  pop-up falls back to the overlay).
- Regression 36/36 and the all-roles browser test pass.

### Sept 27, 2026 — Mandatory override reason (5–25 words) + Admin Bulk Override

**Mandatory reason.** Every override needs a reason of **5 to 25 words**. This covers the single Override
window (including "Use captured status — clear override") and Bulk Override.
- **Server:** `attValidateOverrideReason_()` rejects a missing, too-short or too-long reason. It collapses
  whitespace and keeps the 500-character hard cap.
- **Client:** a live "N / 25 words" counter; Save / Apply stay disabled until the reason is valid.

**Bulk Override (Admin).** A new collapsible card in the Attendance tab, shown only to Admin and Super Admin.
`bulkOverrideAttendance()` enforces `isAdminRole_` plus the read-only role permission.
- **Fields:**
  - Week;
  - Class (All classes or one);
  - Apply to (Students and Teachers / Students only / Teachers only);
  - Only records currently (Any / Present / Partial / Absent / Excused);
  - New status (Present 100 / Partial 70 / Excused 70 / Absent 0 / Clear overrides → captured status);
  - Reason (5–25 words, required).
- **Two steps:** **Preview** (dry run, no writes) shows exactly "N record(s) will change — S students, T teachers
  in C classes"; then **Apply to N record(s)**. Changing any field clears the preview, so Apply always matches
  what was previewed.
- **Per record, the same semantics as a single override:**
  - override columns set, with Status = override and Score = the fixed override score;
  - records already at the target are skipped;
  - excluded accounts are never touched;
  - the captured Meet data (minutes, attended %) is untouched;
  - later syncs preserve it.
- **Performance and audit:**
  - one sheet read, one sheet write (same row order, so no duplicates);
  - one batched audit write (`appendAttendanceAuditLogEntries_`), with one audit row per changed record,
    action `BULK_OVERRIDE` / `BULK_CLEAR_OVERRIDE`, shown as "Bulk override" / "Bulk clear" in the log;
  - runs under the script lock;
  - the overall % summary is then rebuilt.

**Validation.**
- **Acceptance 35/35** (adds):
  - reasons: missing / 4 words / 26 words rejected; 5 and 25 accepted; clear also needs a reason;
  - bulk: Admin/Super Admin only; preview writes nothing;
  - bulk apply: one class, teachers only → PRESENT; all classes, students currently PRESENT → EXCUSED (70)
    with others untouched and an audit row per record;
  - no rows added; re-apply is a no-op; overall % updated; Sync Now keeps bulk overrides; bulk clear
    restores captured statuses.
- **Browser:** Bulk UI 7/7 (card visible only for Admin/Super Admin; preview → reason → apply; field change
  resets the preview; table and audit log refresh). All-roles test updated for the reason counter (Save
  disabled at 2 words). Weekly 24/24, On-Call 8/8, regression 36/36.
